claims.statement: A succubus (plural succubi) is a female demon described in various European folklore as appearing in men's dreams to seduce them.
claims.statement_id: Succubus (jamak: succubi) adalah iblis perempuan yang dalam berbagai cerita rakyat Eropa digambarkan muncul dalam mimpi lelaki untuk merayu mereka.
claims.quote: A succubus ... succubi) is a female demon who was described in various European folklore as appearing in the dreams of male humans in order to seduce them.

claims.statement: Repeated encounters lead to sex and can produce a hybrid child called a cambion, but at the cost of the man's mental and physical health, which declines fast until he dies if the succubus keeps courting him.
claims.statement_id: Hubungan berulang dengan succubus berujung pada persetubuhan dan dapat melahirkan anak hibrida yang disebut cambion, tetapi kesehatan jiwa dan raga lelaki itu cepat memburuk hingga ia mati bila succubus terus mendekatinya lama.
claims.quote: Repeated interactions between a succubus and a man will lead to sexual activity. The establishment and perpetuation of such a relationship enables the production of a hybrid child known as a cambion, but at the expense of the man, whose mental and physical health will deteriorate rapidly, eventually resulting in his death if the succubus continues courting him for a protracted period.

claims.statement: In modern depictions the succubus is often a beautiful seductress rather than a frightening demon; her male counterpart is the incubus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam gambaran modern, succubus sering tampil sebagai perempuan cantik penggoda, bukan iblis menakutkan; padanan lelakinya adalah incubus.
claims.quote: In modern representations, a succubus is often depicted as a beautiful woman seductress or charming, rather than as demonic or frightening, to attract people instead of repulsing them. The male counterpart of the succubus is the incubus.

claims.statement: Historically, belief in succubi was driven by distressing night phenomena, chiefly wet dreams and sleep paralysis.
claims.statement_id: Secara historis, kepercayaan pada succubi didorong gejala malam yang meresahkan, terutama mimpi basah dan kelumpuhan tidur.
claims.quote: Historically, folkloric belief in succubi was motivated by distressing nighttime phenomena, chiefly wet dreams and sleep paralysis.

claims.statement: In medieval Europe a union of an incubus or succubus with a human was thought by some to produce half-demon, half-human children; the legendary magician Merlin was said to be fathered by an incubus.
claims.statement_id: Di Eropa abad pertengahan, persatuan incubus atau succubus dengan manusia dianggap melahirkan anak setengah iblis setengah manusia; penyihir legendaris Merlin konon anak incubus.
claims.quote: In medieval Europe, union of an incubus or succubus and a human was supposed by some to result in the birth of beings half-demon and half-human children. Legendary magician Merlin was said to have been fathered by an incubus.

claims.statement: The term comes from Late Latin succuba, 'paramour', from succubare, 'to lie beneath' (sub-, 'under', and cubare, 'to lie'); the English word dates from the late 14th century.
claims.statement_id: Istilah ini dari bahasa Latin Akhir succuba, "kekasih gelap", dari succubare, "berbaring di bawah" (sub-, "di bawah", dan cubare, "berbaring"); kata Inggris succubus muncul pada akhir abad ke-14.
claims.quote: The term derives from Late Latin succuba "paramour" from succubare "to lie beneath" (sub- "under" and cubare "to lie"), used to describe this being's implied sexual position relative to the sleeper's position. The English word "succubus" dates from the late 14th century.

claims.statement: A succubus may look like a beautiful woman, but a closer look may reveal deformities such as bird-like claws or a serpent's tail.
claims.statement_id: Succubus dapat berwujud perempuan cantik, tetapi bila diamati lebih dekat tampak cacat tubuhnya seperti cakar burung atau ekor ular.
claims.quote: A succubus may take the form of a beautiful woman, but closer inspection may reveal deformities of her body, such as bird-like claws or serpentine tails.

claims.statement: In later folklore the succubus took the form of a siren.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat yang lebih kemudian, succubus berwujud siren.
claims.quote: In later folklore, a succubus took the form of a siren.

claims.statement: Through history priests and rabbis, including Hanina ben Dosa and Abaye, tried to curb the succubi's power over people.
claims.statement_id: Sepanjang sejarah, imam dan rabi, termasuk Hanina ben Dosa dan Abaye, berusaha membatasi kuasa succubi atas manusia.
claims.quote: Throughout history, priests and rabbis, including Hanina ben Dosa and Abaye, tried to curb the power of succubi over humans.

claims.statement: According to the Malleus Maleficarum by Heinrich Kramer (1486), succubi collect semen from the men they seduce, and incubi then use it to impregnate women, explaining how demons could seemingly father children.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Malleus Maleficarum karya Heinrich Kramer (1486), succubi mengumpulkan air mani dari lelaki yang dirayunya, lalu incubi memakainya untuk menghamili perempuan, yang menjelaskan bagaimana iblis seolah dapat beranak.
claims.quote: According to the Malleus Maleficarum, or Witches' Hammer, written by Heinrich Kramer (Institor) in 1486, succubi collect semen from men they seduce. Incubi, or male demons, then use the semen to impregnate human females, thus explaining how demons could apparently sire children

claims.statement: Children so begotten, cambions, were thought to be born deformed or more open to supernatural influence.
claims.statement_id: Anak-anak hasilnya, cambion, dianggap lahir cacat atau lebih rentan terhadap pengaruh gaib.
claims.quote: Children so begotten—cambions—were supposed to be those that were born deformed, or more susceptible to supernatural influences.

claims.statement: King James in his treatise Dæmonologie rejects the idea that angelic beings can reproduce.
claims.statement_id: Raja James dalam risalahnya Dæmonologie membantah kemungkinan makhluk malaikat dapat berkembang biak.
claims.quote: King James in his dissertation titled Dæmonologie refutes the possibility for angelic entities to reproduce

claims.statement: According to the Indonesian article, the targets of incubi and succubi are people weak in faith, unable to restrain lust, unfaithful to their partners, or lonely.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Indonesia, sasaran incubus dan succubus adalah orang yang lemah iman, tak dapat menahan syahwat, tidak setia kepada pasangannya, atau kesepian.
claims.quote: Sasaran dari target incubus dan succubus adalah orang yang tidak kuat iman, tidak bisa menahan syahwat, orang yang tidak setia kepada pasangannya, atau orang yang kesepian.

claims.statement: A cambion is said to grow like an ordinary child before the age of 7.
claims.statement_id: Cambion dikatakan tumbuh seperti anak biasa sebelum berusia 7 tahun.
claims.quote: Cambion dikatakan akan tumbuh seperti anak-anak normal di usia sebelum 7 tahun

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, the 17th-century Italian theologian Ludovico Maria Sinistrari (1622–1701) wrote that incubi and succubi are not demons but a different kind of rational creature from humans.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, teolog Italia abad ke-17 Ludovico Maria Sinistrari (1622–1701) menulis bahwa incubus dan succubus bukan iblis, melainkan makhluk berakal jenis lain di luar manusia.
claims.quote: 17世紀イタリアの神学者ルドヴィコ・マリア・シニストラリ（1622年 – 1701年）は著書にて、「インキュバス・サキュバスは悪魔ではなく、人間とは別の種類の理性的な動物」としている。

claims.statement: Thomas Aquinas in the Summa Theologiae describes it as a being that takes semen from men as a succubus and then, turned incubus, impregnates women, so the two are sometimes said to be one hermaphrodite being.
claims.statement_id: Thomas Aquinas dalam Summa Theologiae menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk yang mengambil air mani dari lelaki dalam wujud succubus lalu berubah menjadi incubus untuk menghamili perempuan, sehingga keduanya kadang dianggap satu makhluk berkelamin ganda.
claims.quote: 男性形のインキュバスとは表裏一体で、サキュバスの姿で男性から精液を採取し、それをインキュバスに変身後に女性へと注いで望まぬ妊娠をさせる存在とトマス・アクィナスは『神学大全』で記述しており、両性具有の同一者であるとも言われている。

claims.statement: William of Paris, confessor of Philip le Bel, lays down that there exist beings commonly called incubi or succubi who indulge their burning lusts.
claims.statement_id: William dari Paris, bapa pengakuan Philip le Bel, menyatakan bahwa ada makhluk yang lazim disebut incubi atau succubi dan bahwa mereka memuaskan nafsu yang menyala-nyala.
claims.quote: The learned William of Paris, confessor of Philip le Bel, lays down: “That there exist such beings as are commonly called incubi or succubi and that they indulge their burning lusts

claims.statement: A passage quoted in Summers's book states that the same evil spirit may serve as a succubus to a man and as an incubus to a woman.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kutipan dalam buku Summers menyatakan roh jahat yang sama dapat menjadi succubus bagi lelaki dan incubus bagi perempuan.
claims.quote: The same evil spirit may serve as a succubus to a man, and as an incubus to a woman.

claims.statement: In a passage quoted by Summers, evil spirits appear as incubi and succubi apparently to inflict a double hurt on man, in both soul and body, which is a supreme joy to devils.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan dalam buku Summers, roh jahat tampil sebagai incubi dan succubi tampaknya agar melukai manusia ganda, jiwa dan raganya, dan itu sukacita tertinggi bagi iblis.
claims.quote: The reason why evil spirits appear as incubi and succubi would seem to be that ... they inflict a double hurt on man, both in his soul and body, and it is a supreme joy to devils thus to injure humankind.

claims.statement: In a passage quoted by Summers, a demon assumes the form of the succubus.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan dalam buku Summers, seorang iblis mengambil rupa succubus.
claims.quote: A demon assumes the form of the succubus

claims.statement: In an accusation against witches quoted by Summers, the Devil appears in human form, is used by the men as a succubus and carnally serves the woman as an incubus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tuduhan terhadap para penyihir yang dikutip Summers, Iblis tampil berwujud manusia, dipakai oleh para lelaki sebagai succubus dan melayani perempuan sebagai incubus.
claims.quote: fornicating with the Devil himself who appears to them in a human form, being used by the men as a succubus, & carnally serving the woman as an incubus.

claims.statement: Summers allows that many such accounts may be ascribed to hysteria, hallucinations, nightmare and the imaginings of disease.
claims.statement_id: Summers mengakui bahwa banyak kisah semacam ini dapat dikembalikan pada histeria, halusinasi, mimpi buruk, dan khayalan akibat penyakit.
claims.quote: In the first place, we may freely allow that many of these lubricities are to be ascribed to hysteria and hallucinations, to nightmare and the imaginings of disease

claims.statement: Brignoli relates that at Bergamo in 1650 a young man of twenty-two came to him and made a long confession.
claims.statement_id: Brignoli menuturkan bahwa saat di Bergamo pada 1650, seorang pemuda berusia dua puluh dua tahun datang dan membuat pengakuan panjang.
claims.quote: Brignoli, in his ... relates that when he was at Bergamo in 1650, a young man, twenty-two years of age, sought him out and made a long and ample confession.

claims.statement: In the tale, before dawn the visitant revealed the true nature of the deceit and the young man realized he had lain with a succubus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, sebelum fajar sang tamu membuka sifat sebenarnya dari tipuan itu dan pemuda itu sadar telah tidur dengan seorang succubus.
claims.quote: Before dawn, however, the visitant revealed the true nature of the deceit, and the young man realized he had lain with a succubus.

claims.statement: Summers records Abrahel and Jezebel as names of familiars, each described as a succubus.
claims.statement_id: Summers mencatat Abrahel dan Jezebel sebagai nama roh pendamping (familiar) yang disebut succubus.
claims.quote: Martinet; Abrahel (a succubus); and to animal familiars in England, Tissy; Grissell; Greedigut; Blackman; Jezebel (a succubus)

claims.statement: In the Summa Theologiae, the demon assumes first the form of a woman and afterwards that of a man, in answer to the claim that demons beget human children.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Summa Theologiae, iblis mengambil dahulu rupa perempuan lalu rupa lelaki dalam menanggapi anggapan bahwa iblis dapat memperanakkan manusia.
claims.quote: as when the demon assumes first the form of a woman, and afterwards of a man

claims.statement: Aquinas holds that if children are born from demons, it is not from the demons' own seed but from the seed of men taken for the purpose.
claims.statement_id: Aquinas menyatakan bahwa bila ada anak yang lahir dari iblis, itu bukan dari benih iblis, melainkan dari benih manusia yang diambil untuk tujuan itu.
claims.quote: but from the seed of men taken for the purpose

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica states that the female counterparts of incubus demons were called succubae.
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 menyatakan padanan perempuan dari setan-setan incubus disebut succubae.
claims.quote: The female counterparts of these demons were called succubae.

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica describes the incubus as a male demon supposed to haunt women in their sleep.
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 menyebut incubus sebagai setan lelaki yang diyakini menghantui perempuan dalam tidurnya.
claims.quote: a male demon which was supposed to haunt women in their sleep

claims.statement: The Beast of Gévaudan (La Bête du Gévaudan) is the historic name for one or more man-eating cryptids that terrorised the former province of Gévaudan in the Margeride Mountains of south-central France between 30 June 1764 and 19 June 1767.
claims.statement_id: Binatang Gévaudan (La Bête du Gévaudan) adalah nama historis untuk satu atau lebih kriptid pemangsa manusia yang meneror bekas provinsi Gévaudan di Pegunungan Margeride, Prancis selatan-tengah, antara 30 Juni 1764 dan 19 Juni 1767.
claims.quote: The Beast of Gévaudan ... is the historic name associated with a man-eating cryptid or cryptids that terrorized the former province of Gévaudan ... in the Margeride Mountains of south-central France between 30 June 1764 and 19 June 1767.

claims.statement: Contemporary witnesses said the attacks were by one or more tawny-russet beasts with dark stripes and a dark stripe down the back, with a tail 'longer than a wolf's' ending in a tuft.
claims.statement_id: Menurut saksi mata masa itu, serangan dilakukan satu atau lebih binatang berwarna cokelat kemerahan dengan belang gelap dan garis gelap di punggung, berekor lebih panjang daripada serigala dengan jumbai di ujungnya.
claims.quote: were said to have been committed by one or more beasts of a tawny/russet colour with dark streaks/stripes and a dark stripe down its back, a tail "longer than a wolf's" ending in a tuft according to contemporary eyewitnesses.

claims.statement: It attacked with fearsome teeth and claws, looked the size of a calf or cow, and seemed to fly or bound across fields at its victims.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyerang dengan gigi dan cakar yang mengerikan, tampak sebesar anak sapi atau sapi, dan seolah terbang atau melompat melintasi ladang ke arah korbannya.
claims.quote: It was said to attack with formidable teeth and claws, and appeared to be the size of a calf or cow and seemed to fly or bound across fields towards its victims.

claims.statement: These descriptions could fit a striped hyena, a large wolf, a large dog or a wolfdog, but its identity is still debated and unsolved.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran itu dapat cocok dengan dubuk belang, serigala besar, anjing besar, atau anjing-serigala, tetapi identitasnya masih diperdebatkan sampai kini.
claims.quote: These descriptions from the period could identify the beast as a striped hyena, a large wolf, a large dog, or a wolfdog, though its identity is still the subject of debate and remains unsolved to this day.

claims.statement: The Kingdom of France spent great wealth and manpower hunting the animals, including nobles, soldiers, royal huntsmen and civilians.
claims.statement_id: Kerajaan Prancis mengerahkan banyak dana dan tenaga untuk memburunya, termasuk bangsawan, tentara, pemburu kerajaan, dan warga.
claims.quote: The Kingdom of France used a considerable amount of wealth and manpower to hunt the animals responsible, including the resources of several nobles, soldiers, royal huntsmen, and civilians.

claims.statement: A 1987 study estimated 210 attacks causing 113 deaths and 49 injuries; 98 of those killed were partly eaten.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kajian tahun 1987 memperkirakan 210 serangan dengan 113 korban tewas dan 49 terluka; 98 korban tewas sebagian dimakan.
claims.quote: A 1987 study estimated there had been 210 attacks, resulting in 113 deaths and 49 injuries; 98 of the victims killed were partly eaten.

claims.statement: Its first official victim was recorded on 30 June 1764: 14-year-old Jeanne Boulet, killed near the village of Les Hubacs near Langogne.
claims.statement_id: Korban resmi pertamanya tercatat pada 30 Juni 1764: Jeanne Boulet, 14 tahun, yang tewas dekat desa Les Hubacs di dekat Langogne.
claims.quote: Shortly afterwards, on 30 June, the beast's first official victim was recorded: 14-year-old Jeanne Boulet was killed near the village of Les Hubacs near Langogne.

claims.statement: Several animals identified as the beast were reportedly killed before the attacks finally stopped.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa binatang yang dianggap sebagai Binatang Gévaudan dilaporkan dibunuh sebelum serangan akhirnya berhenti.
claims.quote: Several animals identified as the beast were reportedly killed before the attacks finally stopped.

claims.statement: The Indonesian article dates the man-eating wolf-like beast's attacks between 1764 and 1770.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Indonesia menyebut serangan hewan mirip serigala pemangsa manusia ini berlangsung antara 1764 dan 1770.
claims.quote: adalah nama historis yang merujuk kepada hewan mirip serigala pemangsa manusia yang meneror bekas provinsi Gévaudan (kini département Lozère bagian dari wilayah Haute-Loire), di Pegunungan Margeride di Prancis Selatan antara tahun 1764 dan 1770.

claims.statement: Witnesses also said the creature had been wounded many times, even shot at close range, yet did not die.
claims.statement_id: Saksi juga menyatakan makhluk itu sudah dilukai berkali-kali, termasuk ditembak dari jarak dekat, tetapi tidak juga mati.
claims.quote: Saksi juga menyatakan bahwa makhluk tersebut telah dilukai berkali-kali tetapi tidak kunjung mati.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article its killing method was unusual for a predator: it often went for the victim's head, ignoring the legs and throat predators usually target.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, cara membunuhnya tidak lazim bagi pemangsa: ia sering menyasar kepala korban dan mengabaikan kaki dan leher yang biasa disasar pemangsa.
claims.quote: この生き物の伝えられた殺害の仕方は捕食動物としては異常で、しばしば獲物の頭部を標的にし、普通なら捕食動物が狙う脚や喉を全く無視していた。

claims.statement: An incubus (plural incubi) is a male demon said in various folklore to appear in women's dreams to seduce them.
claims.statement_id: Incubus (jamak: incubi) adalah iblis lelaki yang dalam berbagai cerita rakyat muncul dalam mimpi perempuan untuk merayu mereka.
claims.quote: An incubus ... incubi) is a male demon who is described in various folklore as appearing in the dreams of female humans in order to seduce them.

claims.statement: According to the Indonesian article, a lasting relationship with an incubus can produce a hybrid child called a cambion.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Indonesia, hubungan yang berulang dengan incubus dapat melahirkan anak hibrida yang disebut kambion.
claims.quote: Pembentukan dan kelestarian hubungan semacam itu memungkinkan lahirnya anak hibrida yang dikenal sebagai kambion

claims.statement: In modern depictions the incubus is often a handsome seducer rather than a frightening demon; his female counterpart is the succubus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam gambaran modern, incubus sering tampil sebagai lelaki tampan penggoda, bukan iblis menakutkan; padanan perempuannya adalah succubus.
claims.quote: In modern representations, an incubus is often depicted as a handsome man seducer or charming, rather than as demonic or frightening, to attract people instead of repulsing them. The female counterpart of the incubus is the succubus.

claims.statement: Belief in incubi was driven by distressing night phenomena, chiefly wet dreams and sleep paralysis.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan pada incubi didorong gejala malam yang meresahkan, terutama mimpi basah dan kelumpuhan tidur.
claims.quote: Historically, folkloric belief in incubi was motivated by distressing nighttime phenomena, chiefly wet dreams and sleep paralysis.

claims.statement: The legendary magician Merlin was said to be an incubus's son, and Walter Stephens writes in Demon Lovers that some traditions hold repeated relations with an incubus or succubus may ruin health and mind or even kill.
claims.statement_id: Penyihir legendaris Merlin konon anak incubus, dan Walter Stephens dalam Demon Lovers menulis bahwa menurut sebagian tradisi hubungan berulang dengan incubus atau succubus dapat merusak kesehatan, jiwa, bahkan menyebabkan kematian.
claims.quote: Legendary magician Merlin was said to have been fathered by an incubus. Walter Stephens writes in his book Demon Lovers that some traditions hold that repeated sexual activity with an incubus or succubus may result in the deterioration of health, an impaired mental state, or even death.

claims.statement: The Late Latin incubus, 'a demon-induced nightmare', comes from incubō, 'what lies on one while asleep', and incubāre, 'to lie upon'.
claims.statement_id: Kata Latin Akhir incubus, "mimpi buruk yang ditimbulkan iblis", berasal dari incubō, "yang menindih orang tidur", dan incubāre, "berbaring di atas".
claims.quote: The Late Latin word incubus ("a nightmare induced by a demon") is derived from Latin incubō ("nightmare, what lies down on one whilst one sleeps") and further from incubāre ("to lie upon, to hatch").

claims.statement: One of the earliest mentions of an incubus-like demon is on the Sumerian King List from Mesopotamia, c. 2400 BC, naming Lilu, who 'disturbs' and 'seduces' sleeping women, as the father of the hero Gilgamesh.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu sebutan tertua iblis mirip incubus ada dalam Daftar Raja Sumeria dari Mesopotamia sekitar 2400 SM, yang mencantumkan Lilu, iblis yang mengganggu dan merayu perempuan dalam tidur, sebagai ayah pahlawan Gilgamesh.
claims.quote: One of the earliest evident mentions of a demon sharing qualities with an incubus comes from Mesopotamia on the Sumerian King List, circa 2400 BC, where the hero Gilgamesh's father is listed as Lilu. Lilu is described as "disturbing" and "seducing" women in their sleep

claims.statement: Mesopotamian accounts also name Ardat lili, who visits men by night, and Idlu lili, her male counterpart, who visits women by night and begets on them.
claims.statement_id: Catatan Mesopotamia juga menyebut Ardat lili yang mendatangi lelaki pada malam hari dan Idlu lili, padanan lelakinya, yang mendatangi perempuan dan membuat mereka hamil.
claims.quote: Two other corresponding demons also appear in Mesopotamian accounts: Ardat lili, who visits men by night, and Idlu lili, a male counterpart to Ardat lili who visits women by night and begets from them.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, Augustine in The City of God (book 15, chapter 23) records the belief of his time that the forest spirits Silvanus and Faunus were called incubi and often assailed women.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, Agustinus dalam De Civitate Dei buku 15 bab 23 mencatat kepercayaan masa itu bahwa roh hutan Silvanus dan Faunus disebut incubi dan sering menyerang perempuan.
claims.quote: 古くはアウグスティヌス『神の国』第15巻23章に、森の精霊シルウァーヌスやファウヌスはインキュバスと呼ばれ、しばしば女性を襲って欲望を満たす、という当時の俗信についての記述がある。

claims.statement: Incubi and succubi appear as their victim's ideal partner, so their temptation is very hard to refuse, and besides human form they are said to slip into the victim's bedroom as bats.
claims.statement_id: Incubus dan succubus muncul sebagai sosok lawan jenis idaman korbannya sehingga godaannya sangat sulit ditolak, dan selain berwujud manusia mereka konon menyusup ke kamar korban dalam wujud kelelawar.
claims.quote: どちらも、自分と性交したくてたまらなくさせるために、襲われる人の理想の異性像で、服を着ず下半身は裸で現れる。そのため、その誘惑を拒否することは非常に困難だった。人の形態をとるだけでなく、標的となった人間の寝室には蝙蝠に化けて侵入するともされている。

claims.statement: An ogre (female ogress) is a legendary monster, a large, hideous humanoid that eats people, especially babies and children.
claims.statement_id: Ogre (perempuan: ogress) adalah monster legendaris berwujud makhluk mirip manusia yang besar dan buruk rupa yang memakan manusia, terutama bayi dan anak-anak.
claims.quote: An ogre (feminine: ogress) is a legendary monster depicted as a large, hideous, humanoid being that eats ordinary human beings, especially infants and children.

claims.statement: Ogres are often shown as hugely large and tall, with oversized heads, thick hair, oddly coloured skin, voracious appetites and strong bodies, closely tied to giants and human cannibals.
claims.statement_id: Ogre sering digambarkan sangat besar dan tinggi, berkepala terlalu besar, berambut lebat, berkulit warna tak biasa, rakus, dan bertubuh kuat, serta erat terkait dengan raksasa dan manusia kanibal.
claims.quote: In mythology, ogres are often depicted as inhumanly large, tall, and having a disproportionately large head, abundant hair, unusually colored skin, a voracious appetite, and a strong body. Ogres are closely linked with giants and with human cannibals in mythology.

claims.statement: Famous folklore ogres include those in Puss in Boots and Hop-o'-My-Thumb.
claims.statement_id: Contoh terkenal adalah ogre dalam Puss in Boots dan Hop-o'-My-Thumb.
claims.quote: Famous examples of ogres in folklore include the ogre in "Puss in Boots" and the ogre in "Hop-o'-My-Thumb".

claims.statement: Other figures sometimes called ogres include Bluebeard, the Beast of Beauty and the Beast, Humbaba of the Epic of Gilgamesh, Grendel of Beowulf and Polyphemus of the Odyssey.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh lain yang kadang disebut ogre antara lain Bluebeard, si Buruk Rupa dalam Beauty and the Beast, Humbaba dari Epos Gilgamesh, Grendel dari Beowulf, dan Polifemus dari Odisseia.
claims.quote: Other characters sometimes described as ogres include the title character from "Bluebeard", the Beast from Beauty and the Beast, Humbaba from the Epic of Gilgamesh, Grendel from Beowulf, Polyphemus the Cyclops from Homer's Odyssey

claims.statement: The word ogre is French, from the Etruscan god Orcus, first attested in Chrétien de Troyes's late 12th-century romance Perceval, li contes del graal.
claims.statement_id: Kata ogre berasal dari bahasa Prancis, dari nama dewa Etruska Orcus, dan pertama tercatat dalam roman Perceval, li contes del graal karya Chrétien de Troyes akhir abad ke-12.
claims.quote: The word ogre is of French origin, originally derived from the Etruscan god Orcus. Its earliest attestation is in Chrétien de Troyes's late 12th-century verse romance Perceval, li contes del graal

claims.statement: The word orco was widely used in Italy since at least the 13th century, as Jacomo Tolomei attests.
claims.statement_id: Kata orco sudah banyak dipakai di Italia setidaknya sejak abad ke-13, seperti dicatat Jacomo Tolomei.
claims.quote: The word orco was widely used in Italy at least since 13th century, as attested by Jacomo Tolomei

claims.statement: The Italian writer Giambattista Basile (1575–1632) used the Neapolitan uerco, or orco, in his tales and first spoke of female ogres, as in Petrosinella.
claims.statement_id: Pengarang Italia Giambattista Basile (1575–1632) memakai kata Neapolitan uerco atau orco dalam dongengnya dan pertama kali menyebut orco perempuan, misalnya dalam Petrosinella.
claims.quote: The Italian author Giambattista Basile (1575–1632) used the related Neapolitan word uerco, or in standard Italian, orco in some of his tales, and first talks of female orcs (e.g. in "Petrosinella").

claims.statement: According to the Indonesian article, the ogre legend began in the Middle Ages in southern Europe, when many club-armed barbarians attacked Roman lands.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Indonesia, legenda ogre berawal dari Abad Pertengahan di Eropa Selatan, saat banyak orang barbar bersenjata pemukul batu menyerang wilayah Romawi.
claims.quote: Legenda Ogre berawal dari zaman pertengahan di Eropa Selatan, di mana banyak orang barbar yang bersenjatakan pemukul batu yang menyerang wilayah Romawi.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, the word may go back to Orcus, the Greco-Roman underworld god, but derives directly from the Italian dialect orco or orgo, 'fiend, monster'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, kata ini mungkin berasal dari Orcus, dewa dunia bawah mitologi Yunani-Romawi, tetapi secara langsung dari kata dialek Italia orco atau orgo, "iblis, monster".
claims.quote: 語源としては、古くさかのぼるばあい、ギリシア・ローマ神話の冥府の神オルクスに由来するという説がある。しかし、直接にはイタリア語方言で「悪鬼、怪物」を意味するオルコやオルゴ（イタリア語: Orco, Orgo）に基づくともされる。

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, in northern Europe the ogre is thought fierce and cruel and to eat raw human flesh, yet also shy and timid.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, di Eropa utara ogre dianggap buas dan kejam serta memakan daging manusia mentah, tetapi juga pemalu dan penakut.
claims.quote: 北ヨーロッパでは凶暴で残忍な性格であり、人の生肉を食べるとされる。一方で、引っ込み思案で臆病という面もある。

claims.statement: The hippogriff (Italian ippogrifo) or hippogryph is a legendary creature with the front half of an eagle and the hind half of a horse.
claims.statement_id: Hippogriff (bahasa Italia: ippogrifo) atau hippogryph adalah makhluk legendaris bertubuh depan elang dan bertubuh belakang kuda.
claims.quote: The hippogriff (Italian: ippogrifo) or hippogryph is a legendary creature with the front half of an eagle and the hind half of a horse.

claims.statement: It was invented early in the 16th century by Ludovico Ariosto in Orlando Furioso as a steed born of a mare and a griffin, thought impossible; it is extremely fast and can fly round the world and to the Moon.
claims.statement_id: Ia diciptakan pada awal abad ke-16 oleh Ludovico Ariosto dalam Orlando Furioso sebagai tunggangan yang lahir dari kuda betina dan griffin, hal yang dianggap mustahil; ia sangat cepat dan dapat terbang mengelilingi dunia sampai ke Bulan.
claims.quote: It was invented at the beginning of the 16th century by Ludovico Ariosto in his Orlando Furioso. Within the poem, the hippogriff is a steed born of a mare and a griffin—something considered impossible. It is extremely fast and is presented as being able to fly around the world and to the Moon.

claims.statement: Its first owner was the Saracen sorcerer Atlantes of Mount Carena in Morocco, then the knight-errant Ruggiero, his adopted son, who from its back frees the beautiful Angelica.
claims.statement_id: Pemilik pertamanya penyihir Saracen Atlantes dari Gunung Carena di Maroko, lalu ksatria pengembara Ruggiero, anak angkatnya, yang dari punggung hippogriff membebaskan Angelica yang cantik.
claims.quote: Its original owner was the sorcerer Atlantes, a Saracen who lived in Mount Carena in Morocco and the knight errant (his adopted son) Ruggiero, who, from the creature's back, frees the beautiful Angelica.

claims.statement: The hippogriff became a subject of art in the 19th century, often drawn by Gustave Doré.
claims.statement_id: Hippogriff menjadi subjek seni rupa pada abad ke-19 dan sering digambar Gustave Doré.
claims.quote: The hippogriff became a subject of visual art in the 19th century, when it was often drawn by Gustave Doré.

claims.statement: The word hippogriff comes from Ancient Greek híppos, 'horse', and Italian grifo, 'griffin'.
claims.statement_id: Kata hippogriff berasal dari bahasa Yunani Kuno híppos, "kuda", dan bahasa Italia grifo, "griffin".
claims.quote: The word hippogriff, also spelled hippogryph, is derived from the Ancient Greek: ἵππος híppos, meaning "horse", and the Italian grifo meaning "griffin"

claims.statement: The word entered English shortly before 1615; before that John Harington's 1591 translation called it a 'Griffith horse'.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini masuk ke bahasa Inggris tak lama sebelum 1615; sebelumnya terjemahan John Harington tahun 1591 menyebutnya "Griffith horse".
claims.quote: The word hippogriff was adopted into English shortly before 1615; prior to this, John Harington's 1591 translation of Orlando furioso called the creature a "Griffith horse."

claims.statement: According to Thomas Bulfinch's Legends of Charlemagne, like a griffin it has an eagle's head, taloned claws and feathered wings, the rest of its body being a horse's.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Legends of Charlemagne karya Thomas Bulfinch, seperti griffin ia berkepala elang, bercakar tajam, bersayap berbulu, dan selebihnya bertubuh kuda.
claims.quote: Like a griffin, it has the head of an eagle, claws armed with talons, and wings covered with feathers, the rest of its body being that of a horse.

claims.statement: According to the Indonesian article, hippogriffs appear in the Harry Potter series, such as Hagrid's Buckbeak in Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Indonesia, hippogriff muncul dalam serial Harry Potter, misalnya Buckbeak peliharaan Hagrid dalam Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban.
claims.quote: beberapa buku dalam serial Harry Potter, seperti dalam kisah Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban memunculkan Hippogriff seperti misalnya Buckbeak yang dipelihara oleh Hagrid dan menjadi kawan Harry.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, since griffins like to eat horses, a cross of the two once stood for the impossible, and by one theory became the name of an imaginary creature.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, karena griffin suka memakan kuda, gabungan keduanya dulu menjadi ungkapan untuk hal mustahil, dan menurut satu teori lalu menjadi nama makhluk khayalan.
claims.quote: グリフォンが馬を好んで食べるということから、ありえないもの（天敵と被食者のハーフ）の代名詞だったものが、そのまま想像上の生物の名前になってしまったという説もある。

claims.statement: The wyvern or wivern is a kind of mythical dragon with two legs, two wings and often a pointed tail.
claims.statement_id: Wyvern atau wivern adalah sejenis naga mitis berkaki dua, bersayap dua, dan sering berekor runcing.
claims.quote: The wyvern ... sometimes spelled wivern ... is a type of mythical  dragon with two legs, two wings, and often a pointed tail.

claims.statement: The wyvern is important in heraldry and often a mascot of schools and sports teams, mainly in the United States, United Kingdom and Canada.
claims.statement_id: Wyvern penting dalam heraldik dan sering menjadi maskot sekolah dan tim olahraga, terutama di Amerika Serikat, Britania Raya, dan Kanada.
claims.quote: The wyvern in its various forms is important in heraldry, frequently appearing as a mascot of schools and athletic teams (chiefly in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada).

claims.statement: Unlike other dragons, the wyvern of heraldry and folklore rarely breathes fire.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari naga lain, wyvern dalam heraldik dan cerita rakyat jarang menyemburkan api.
claims.quote: The wyvern in heraldry and folklore is rarely fire-breathing, unlike other dragons.

claims.statement: According to the Oxford English Dictionary, the word developed from Middle English wyver (14th century), from Anglo-French wivre (compare vouivre and guivre), from Latin vīpera, 'viper'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Oxford English Dictionary, kata ini berkembang dari bahasa Inggris Pertengahan wyver (abad ke-14), dari bahasa Anglo-Prancis wivre (bandingkan vouivre dan guivre), yang berasal dari bahasa Latin vīpera, "ular berbisa".
claims.quote: According to the Oxford English Dictionary, the word is a development of Middle English wyver (attested fourteenth century), from Anglo-French wivre (compare French: vouivre and guivre), which originate from Latin: vīpera, meaning "viper", "adder", or "asp".

claims.statement: The final -n was added by the early 17th century, when John Guillim in 1610 described the 'wiverne' as having a fowl's wings and legs and a serpent's tail.
claims.statement_id: Akhiran -n sudah ditambahkan pada awal abad ke-17, ketika John Guillim pada 1610 menggambarkan "wiverne" sebagai makhluk bersayap dan berkaki burung dengan ekor seperti ular.
claims.quote: The concluding "–n" had been added by the beginning of the 17th century, when John Guillim in 1610 describes the "wiverne" as a creature that "partake[s] of a Fowle in the Wings and Legs ... and doth resemble a Serpent in the Taile".

claims.statement: The medievalist William Sayers proposed that the images of 'venomous snake' and 'light javelin' (guivre) merged into the new idea of a flying snake.
claims.statement_id: Medievalis William Sayers mengusulkan bahwa gambaran "ular berbisa" dan "lembing ringan" (guivre) berpadu menjadi konsep baru ular terbang.
claims.quote: By noting physical resemblances between the javelins and snakes, he proposed that the images of "venomous snake" and "light javelin" were melded to produce the novel concept of a flying snake.

claims.statement: Winged snakes appear across ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern cultures, for example the Egyptian goddess Wadjet, a winged cobra protecting Lower Egypt from Predynastic times.
claims.statement_id: Konsep ular bersayap ada di banyak budaya kuno Mediterania dan Timur Dekat, misalnya dewi Mesir Wadjet, kobra bersayap pelindung Mesir Hilir sejak masa Pradinasti.
claims.quote: The Egyptian goddess Wadjet, depicted as a winged cobra or uraeus, exemplifies this tradition and served as a protective deity of Lower Egypt from the Predynastic period onwards.

claims.statement: According to the Indonesian article, depending on the culture the wivern may breathe fire, have deadly venom, both, or neither.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Indonesia, bergantung budayanya wivern dapat menyemburkan api, memiliki bisa mematikan, keduanya, atau tidak sama sekali.
claims.quote: Tergantung budaya bersangkutan, wivern dapat dideskripsikan menyemburkan api atau memiliki bisa mematikan, atau memiliki dua kemampuan tersebut atau tidak sama sekali.

claims.statement: There is a sea variant, the sea-wyvern, with a fish's fin in place of its coiled dragon tail.
claims.statement_id: Ada varian penghuni laut, wivern laut, yang bersirip ikan sebagai ganti ekor naga yang melingkar.
claims.quote: Ada varian wivern yang menghuni laut, disebut Wivern laut yang memiliki sirip ikan sebagai pengganti ekor naganya yang melingkar.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, outside Britain two-legged dragons are treated as ordinary dragons in Europe; distinguishing them as wyverns is peculiar to Britain and its former colonies.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, di Eropa selain Inggris naga berkaki dua dianggap bentuk naga biasa; membedakannya sebagai wyvern adalah kekhasan Inggris dan bekas jajahannya.
claims.quote: 「二足の竜」の図像は、イギリスを除くヨーロッパではドラゴンの一般的な形態の一つとして扱われており、これをワイバーンとしてドラゴンから区別するのはイギリスおよびイギリスの旧植民地に特有のことである。

claims.statement: Some once equated wyvern with Latin viverra, 'ferret', a folk etymology.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula yang dahulu menyamakan wyvern dengan kata Latin viverra, "musang", sebuah etimologi rakyat.
claims.quote: 異説として、ワイバーンをラテン語の viverra（フェレット）と同一視する者があった。

claims.statement: The tooth fairy is a childhood folklore figure in Western and Western-influenced cultures: a child who loses a milk tooth puts it under the pillow or on the bedside table, and the tooth fairy comes during sleep and replaces it with a small payment.
claims.statement_id: Peri gigi adalah tokoh cerita rakyat masa kanak-kanak dalam budaya Barat dan yang terpengaruh Barat: anak yang tanggal gigi susunya menaruhnya di bawah bantal atau di meja samping ranjang, lalu peri gigi datang saat ia tidur dan menggantinya dengan sedikit uang.
claims.quote: The tooth fairy is a folkloric figure of early childhood in Western and Western-influenced cultures. The folklore states that when children lose one of their baby teeth, they should place it underneath their pillow or on their bedside table; the tooth fairy will visit while they sleep, replacing the lost tooth with a small payment.

claims.statement: In the Middle Ages English children were told to burn their milk teeth or spend eternity searching for them in the afterlife, and fear of witches was another reason to bury or burn teeth.
claims.statement_id: Pada Abad Pertengahan anak-anak di Inggris disuruh membakar gigi susunya agar tidak selamanya mencarinya di alam baka, dan ketakutan pada penyihir juga menjadi alasan gigi dikubur atau dibakar.
claims.quote: Children in England were instructed to burn their baby teeth, on pain of spending eternity searching for the baby teeth in the afterlife. Fear of witches was another reason to bury or burn teeth.

claims.statement: In medieval Europe a witch was thought to gain total power over someone by obtaining one of their teeth.
claims.statement_id: Di Eropa abad pertengahan, penyihir dipercaya dapat menguasai seseorang sepenuhnya bila memperoleh salah satu giginya.
claims.quote: In medieval Europe, it was thought that a witch could assume total power over someone if they were to obtain one of their teeth.

claims.statement: The earliest known record of the tooth fairy tradition itself is a 1908 'Household Hints' item in the Chicago Daily Tribune.
claims.statement_id: Catatan tertua tradisi peri gigi sendiri adalah rubrik "Household Hints" tahun 1908 di Chicago Daily Tribune.
claims.quote: While these beliefs may have had an influence, the earliest known record of the tooth fairy tradition itself is a 1908 "Household Hints" item in the Chicago Daily Tribune

claims.statement: Unlike Santa Claus and the Easter Bunny, few details of the tooth fairy's looks are consistent across versions.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari Sinterklas dan Kelinci Paskah, hanya sedikit rincian rupa peri gigi yang sama di berbagai versi.
claims.quote: Unlike Santa Claus and, to a lesser extent, the Easter Bunny, there are few details of the tooth fairy's appearance that are consistent in various versions of the myth.

claims.statement: A 1984 study by Rosemary Wells found 74% of respondents thought the tooth fairy female, 12% neither male nor female, and 8% either.
claims.statement_id: Kajian Rosemary Wells tahun 1984 menemukan 74% responden menganggap peri gigi perempuan, 12% bukan lelaki maupun perempuan, dan 8% bisa keduanya.
claims.quote: A 1984 study conducted by Rosemary Wells revealed that most – 74% of those surveyed – believed the tooth fairy to be female, while 12% believed the tooth fairy to be neither male nor female, and 8% believed the tooth fairy could be either male or female.

claims.statement: According to the Indonesian article, leaving a tooth under the pillow for the tooth fairy is practised across the Anglosphere.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Indonesia, tradisi menaruh gigi di bawah bantal untuk peri gigi dipraktikkan di berbagai negara Anglosfer.
claims.quote: Tradisi meninggalkan gigi di bawah bantal untuk peri gigi dipraktikkan di berbagai negara di Anglosfer.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, the tooth fairy (German Zahnfee, French la Petite Souris, Spanish Ratoncito Pérez) exchanges lost milk teeth for coins or gifts.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, peri gigi (Jerman: Zahnfee; Prancis: la Petite Souris; Spanyol: Ratoncito Pérez) menukar gigi susu yang tanggal dengan koin atau hadiah.
claims.quote: 歯の妖精（ドイツ語: Zahnfee, 英語: Tooth fairy, フランス語: la Petite Souris, スペイン語: Ratoncito Pérez）とは、抜けた乳歯をコイン（場合によってはプレゼント）に交換してくれる妖精である。

claims.statement: In Japan a lost upper milk tooth is thrown under the floor and a lower one towards the roof from a veranda or window.
claims.statement_id: Di Jepang, gigi susu atas yang tanggal dilempar ke kolong lantai dan gigi bawah ke atap dari beranda atau jendela.
claims.quote: 日本では、抜けた乳歯を、上の歯の場合には床下に、下の歯の場合には屋根に向かって縁側や窓などから放り投げることが行われる。

claims.statement: The azure jay (Cyanocorax coeruleus; Brazilian Portuguese gralha-azul) is a Near Threatened passerine species of the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.
claims.statement_id: Gralha-azul (Cyanocorax coeruleus; bahasa Portugis Brasil: gralha-azul) adalah spesies burung pengicau berstatus hampir terancam dari famili Corvidae (gagak dan jay).
claims.quote: The azure jay (Cyanocorax coeruleus) (Brazilian Portuguese: gralha-azul) is a Near Threatened species of passeriform bird in the family Corvidae, the crows and jays.

claims.statement: It appears to feed heavily on Araucaria angustifolia seeds and plays an important role in their dispersal.
claims.statement_id: Burung ini tampaknya banyak memakan biji Araucaria angustifolia dan berperan penting dalam penyebaran bijinya.
claims.quote: However, it appears to feed heavily on Araucaria angustifolia seeds, and plays an important role in its seed dispersal.

claims.statement: In Brazil the azure jay is found from southern São Paulo south through Paraná, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul almost to Uruguay.
claims.statement_id: Di Brasil, gralha-azul ditemukan dari selatan São Paulo ke selatan melalui Paraná, Santa Catarina, dan Rio Grande do Sul hingga hampir ke Uruguay.
claims.quote: The azure jay is found in Brazil from southern São Paulo south through Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul almost to Uruguay.

claims.statement: In the folklore of the state of Paraná the creation and upkeep of the araucaria forests is credited to this bird as a divine mission, which is why guns pointed at it would explode or fail to fire.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat negara bagian Paraná (Brasil), pembentukan dan pemeliharaan hutan araukaria dianggap misi ilahi burung ini, sehingga senapan yang diarahkan kepadanya akan meledak atau gagal menembak.
claims.quote: No folclore do estado do Paraná atribui-se a formação e manutenção das florestas de araucária a este pássaro, como uma missão divina, razão porque as espingardas explodiriam ou negariam fogo quando para elas apontadas.

claims.statement: The bird is one of the symbols of the state of Paraná under State Law no. 7957 of 1984, which names it the "symbol bird".
claims.statement_id: Burung ini adalah salah satu lambang negara bagian Paraná berdasarkan Undang-Undang Negara Bagian No. 7957 tahun 1984 yang menetapkannya sebagai "burung lambang".
claims.quote: é um dos símbolos do Estado do Paraná, segundo a Lei Estadual n. 7957 de 1984 que a consagra como "ave símbolo" deste estado.

claims.statement: Because it is part of Paraná folklore, the bird was chosen as the mascot of Paraná Clube, a traditional football club of Curitiba.
claims.statement_id: Karena menjadi bagian dari folklor Paraná, burung ini dipilih sebagai maskot Paraná Clube, klub sepak bola tradisional kota Curitiba.
claims.quote: Por fazer parte do folclore do Estado do Paraná, a ave foi escolhida como mascote do Paraná Clube, time tradicional de futebol da cidade de Curitiba.

claims.statement: Azure jays push pine seeds (pinhões) firmly into the soil, into fallen trunks already rotting, or into exposed roots, places suited to the growth of a new tree.
claims.statement_id: Gralha-azul menancapkan biji pinus (pinhão) kuat-kuat ke tanah, ke batang kayu tumbang yang mulai lapuk, atau ke akar di atas tanah, tempat yang cocok bagi tumbuhnya pohon baru.
claims.quote: as gralhas-azuis encravam fortemente os pinhões no solo ou em troncos caídos no solo, já em processo de putrefação, ou mesmo nas partes aéreas de raízes nas mesmas condições, local propício para a formação de uma nova árvore.

claims.statement: An elemental is a mythic supernatural being described in occult and alchemical works from around the European Renaissance, especially developed in Paracelsus's 16th-century writings.
claims.statement_id: Elemental adalah makhluk gaib mitis yang digambarkan dalam karya okultisme dan alkimia sekitar masa Renaisans Eropa, terutama dikembangkan dalam karya Paracelsus abad ke-16.
claims.quote: An elemental is a mythic supernatural being that is described in occult and alchemical works from around the time of the European Renaissance, and particularly elaborated in the 16th century works of Paracelsus.

claims.statement: According to Paracelsus and his followers there are four kinds of elementals, gnomes, undines, sylphs and salamanders, matching the four Empedoclean elements: earth, water, air and fire.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Paracelsus dan pengikutnya, ada empat jenis elemental, yaitu gnome, undine, sylph, dan salamander, yang sesuai dengan empat unsur Empedokles: tanah, air, udara, dan api.
claims.quote: According to Paracelsus and his subsequent followers, there are four categories of elementals, which are gnomes, undines, sylphs, and salamanders. These correspond to the four Empedoclean elements of antiquity: earth, water, air, and fire, respectively.

claims.statement: In his Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, Paracelsus assigned mythological beings to the four elements; part of the Philosophia Magna, it was first printed in 1566 after his death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam A Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, Paracelsus menggolongkan makhluk mitologis ke dalam empat unsur; buku ini bagian Philosophia Magna dan pertama dicetak pada 1566 setelah ia wafat.
claims.quote: In his 16th-century work A Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, Paracelsus identified mythological beings as belonging to one of the four elements. Part of the Philosophia Magna, this book was first printed in 1566 after Paracelsus' death.

claims.statement: The concept of elementals seems to have been devised by Paracelsus in the 16th century, though he did not actually use the word 'elemental' or a German equivalent.
claims.statement_id: Konsep elemental tampaknya diciptakan Paracelsus pada abad ke-16, walau ia sendiri tidak memakai istilah elemental atau padanannya dalam bahasa Jerman.
claims.quote: The concept of elementals seems to have been conceived by Paracelsus in the 16th century, though he did not in fact use the term "elemental" or a German equivalent.

claims.statement: He saw them not so much as spirits but as beings between creatures and spirits, usually invisible to humans yet with physical, mostly humanlike bodies, eating, sleeping and wearing clothes like people.
claims.statement_id: Ia menganggap mereka bukan roh semata, melainkan makhluk di antara makhluk jasmani dan roh, biasanya tak terlihat manusia tetapi bertubuh jasmani mirip manusia, makan, tidur, dan berpakaian seperti manusia.
claims.quote: He regarded them not so much as spirits but as beings between creatures and spirits, generally being invisible to mankind but having physical and commonly humanoid bodies, as well as eating, sleeping, and wearing clothes like humans.

claims.statement: According to the German article, the idea of elemental spirits comes from late-antique Neoplatonism and was revived by early modern natural philosophers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, gagasan roh unsur berasal dari Neoplatonisme akhir zaman kuno dan dihidupkan kembali para filsuf alam awal zaman modern.
claims.quote: Die Vorstellung von Elementargeistern stammt ursprünglich aus dem spätantiken Neuplatonismus und wurde von frühneuzeitlichen Naturphilosophen wieder aufgegriffen.

claims.statement: Elemental spirits are figures of natural philosophy and literature and do not occur in folk belief or folk tales.
claims.statement_id: Roh unsur adalah tokoh filsafat alam dan sastra, bukan bagian kepercayaan atau cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: Elementargeister sind Gestalten der Naturphilosophie und der Literatur, in Volksglauben und Volkserzählungen kommen sie nicht vor.

claims.statement: They also play a role in various forms of neopaganism and modern esotericism, such as anthroposophy.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga berperan dalam berbagai bentuk neopaganisme dan esoterisme modern, misalnya antroposofi.
claims.quote: Elementargeister spielen auch in verschiedenen Formen von Neuheidentum und moderner Esoterik eine Rolle, etwa in der Anthroposophie.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, Montfaucon de Villars's occult novel Le Comte de Gabalis (Paris, 1670) has its title character discuss marriage with the 'peoples of the four elements'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, novel okultisme Montfaucon de Villars, Le Comte de Gabalis (Paris, 1670), memuat tokoh Comte de Gabalis yang membahas pernikahan dengan "bangsa empat unsur".
claims.quote: その1世紀後にパリで出版されたモンフォーコン・ド・ヴィラール ... の隠秘学小説『ガバリス伯爵』（1670年）は、作中人物のガバリス伯爵をして「四大の民」との婚姻について語らしめた。

claims.statement: A cockatrice is a mythical beast, essentially a two-legged dragon, wyvern or serpent-like creature with a rooster's head.
claims.statement_id: Cockatrice adalah binatang mitis, pada dasarnya naga berkaki dua, wyvern, atau makhluk mirip ular berkepala ayam jantan.
claims.quote: A cockatrice is a mythical beast, essentially a two-legged dragon, wyvern, or serpent-like creature with a rooster's head.

claims.statement: Laurence Breiner called it 'an ornament in the drama and poetry of the Elizabethans'; it was prominent in English thought and myth for centuries, and by legend hatches from a chicken egg incubated by a toad or snake.
claims.statement_id: Laurence Breiner menyebutnya "hiasan dalam drama dan puisi era Elizabeth"; ia menonjol dalam pemikiran dan mitos Inggris selama berabad-abad, dan menurut legenda lahir dari telur ayam yang dierami kodok atau ular.
claims.quote: Described by Laurence Breiner as "an ornament in the drama and poetry of the Elizabethans", it was featured prominently in English thought and myth for centuries. According to legend, they are created by a chicken egg hatched by a toad or snake.

claims.statement: The first English mention is in John Wycliffe's 14th-century Bible translation, used for various Hebrew words for asp and adder in Isaiah 11, 14 and 59.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan Inggris pertama ada dalam terjemahan Alkitab John Wycliffe abad ke-14, untuk menerjemahkan berbagai kata Ibrani bagi ular berbisa dalam Kitab Yesaya 11, 14, dan 59.
claims.quote: The first English mention of the cockatrice was in the 14th-century John Wycliffe translation of the Bible. The word was used for the translation of various Hebrew words for asp and adder in the Book of Isaiah 11, 14 and 59.

claims.statement: The Oxford English Dictionary derives it from Old French cocatris, from medieval Latin calcatrix, a translation of Greek ichneumon, 'tracker'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Oxford English Dictionary, kata ini berasal dari bahasa Prancis Kuno cocatris, dari bahasa Latin abad pertengahan calcatrix, terjemahan kata Yunani ichneumon, "pelacak".
claims.quote: The Oxford English Dictionary gives a derivation from Old French cocatris, from medieval Latin calcatrix, a translation of the Greek ichneumon, meaning tracker.

claims.statement: The cockatrice came to be equated with the basilisk when the basiliscus in Bartholomeus Anglicus's De proprietatibus rerum (c. 1260) was translated by John Trevisa as cockatrice (1397).
claims.statement_id: Cockatrice mulai disamakan dengan basilisk ketika basiliscus dalam De proprietatibus rerum karya Bartholomeus Anglicus (sekitar 1260) diterjemahkan John Trevisa sebagai cockatrice (1397).
claims.quote: Cockatrice became seen as synonymous with basilisk when the basiliscus in Bartholomeus Anglicus's De proprietatibus rerum (ca 1260) was translated by John Trevisa as cockatrice (1397).

claims.statement: The cockatrice can kill by touch, breath or a glance, called in literature 'the death-darting eye of Cockatrice'.
claims.statement_id: Cockatrice dapat membunuh dengan sentuhan, napas, atau tatapan, yang dalam sastra disebut "mata cockatrice yang melemparkan maut".
claims.quote: According to myth, the cockatrice can kill people by touch, breath, or a glance, a trait referred to in literature as "the death-darting eye of Cockatrice".

claims.statement: Late-medieval bestiaries repeat that the weasel alone is immune to its glance, and it was thought to die instantly on hearing a rooster crow.
claims.statement_id: Bestiari akhir abad pertengahan menyebut musang satu-satunya hewan yang kebal terhadap tatapannya, dan cockatrice dipercaya langsung mati mendengar kokok ayam jantan.
claims.quote: It was repeated in the late-medieval bestiaries that the weasel is the only animal that is immune to the glance of a cockatrice. It was also thought that a cockatrice would die instantly upon hearing a rooster crow

claims.statement: A cock's egg was thought to hatch a cockatrice, which could be prevented by throwing the egg over the house without letting it hit the house.
claims.statement_id: Telur ayam jantan dipercaya menetaskan cockatrice, dan hal itu dapat dicegah dengan melemparkan telur melewati atap rumah tanpa mengenai rumah.
claims.quote: It is thought that a cock egg would hatch a cockatrice, and this could be prevented by tossing the egg over the family house, landing on the other side of the house, without allowing the egg to hit the house.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the cocatrix (also coquatrix or caucatrix) has a rooster's head, bat's wings and a serpent's or cock's body.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, cocatrix (juga coquatrix atau caucatrix) berkepala ayam jantan, bersayap kelelawar, dan bertubuh ular atau ayam.
claims.quote: Le cocatrix, coquatrix, caucatrix ou cocatrice est un animal fabuleux qui possède selon la légende une tête de coq, des ailes de chauve-souris et un corps de serpent ou de coq.

claims.statement: Some sources say the cocatrix was 'born by accident at the end of the 12th century and died in the mid-17th, a victim of science'.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sumber menyebut cocatrix "lahir secara kebetulan pada akhir abad ke-12 dan mati pada pertengahan abad ke-17, korban ilmu pengetahuan".
claims.quote: Selon certaines sources, la cocatrix serait « née par accident à la fin du XIIe siècle et est morte au milieu du  XVIIe siècle, victime de la science ».

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, it hatches from a rooster's egg incubated by a toad; the rooster is 7 years old and the toad broods it for 9 years.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, ia lahir dari telur ayam jantan yang dierami kodok; ayam jantan itu berumur 7 tahun dan kodok mengeraminya 9 tahun.
claims.quote: 雄鶏の産んだ卵をヒキガエルが温めて生まれるという（雄鶏は7歳で、卵はヒキガエルが9年間温めるとされる）。

claims.statement: In William Shakespeare's Twelfth Night a character mentions the cockatrice.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Twelfth Night karya William Shakespeare, seorang tokoh menyebut cockatrice.
claims.quote: ウィリアム・シェイクスピアの『十二夜』の中でも、登場人物がコカトリスについて言及している。

claims.statement: The European dragon is a legendary creature of the folklore and mythology of Europe's overlapping cultures.
claims.statement_id: Naga Eropa adalah makhluk legendaris dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi berbagai budaya Eropa yang saling bertumpang tindih.
claims.quote: The European dragon is a legendary creature in folklore and mythology among the overlapping cultures of Europe.

claims.statement: From the Early Middle Ages the European dragon is usually shown as a large, fire-breathing, scaly, horned, lizard-like creature with leathery bat-like wings and a long, muscular, grasping tail.
claims.statement_id: Sejak Abad Pertengahan Awal, naga Eropa biasanya digambarkan sebagai makhluk besar mirip kadal yang menyemburkan api, bersisik, bertanduk, bersayap kulit seperti kelelawar, dan berekor panjang berotot yang dapat mencengkeram.
claims.quote: In and after the Early Middle Ages, the European dragon is typically depicted as a large, fire-breathing, scaly, horned, lizard-like creature; the creature also has leathery, bat-like wings, and a long, muscular prehensile tail.

claims.statement: The typical dragon of Christian culture guards a cave or castle full of gold and treasure; an evil dragon is tied to a hero who tries to slay it, while a good one gives help or wise counsel.
claims.statement_id: Naga dalam budaya Kristen biasanya menjaga gua atau kastel berisi emas dan harta; naga jahat sering dikaitkan dengan pahlawan yang berusaha membunuhnya, sedangkan naga baik memberi bantuan atau nasihat bijak.
claims.quote: The typical dragon in Christian culture protects a cavern or castle filled with gold and treasure. An evil dragon is often associated with a great hero who tries to slay it, and a good one is said to give support or wise advice.

claims.statement: In some accounts the hero Sigurð defeats Fáfnir by digging a pit, lying in wait and stabbing his heart with a sword as he passes over.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian kisah, pahlawan Sigurð mengalahkan Fáfnir dengan menggali lubang, menunggu, lalu menusuk jantungnya dengan pedang ketika naga itu lewat di atasnya.
claims.quote: In some accounts, the hero Sigurð defeats Fáfnir by digging a pit and then lying in wait, piercing his heart with a sword as he passes overhead and slaying him.

claims.statement: The Roman poet Virgil, in his poem Culex (lines 163–201), calls the great snake a shepherd fights both serpens and draco, showing the two words could probably mean the same thing in his day.
claims.statement_id: Penyair Romawi Vergilius dalam puisi Culex (baris 163–201) menyebut ular besar yang dilawan seorang gembala dengan kata serpens sekaligus draco, menunjukkan kedua kata itu mungkin bermakna sama pada masanya.
claims.quote: The Roman poet Virgil in his poem Culex lines 163–201, describing a shepherd battling a big constricting snake, calls it "serpens" and also "draco", showing that in his time the two words probably could mean the same thing.

claims.statement: Roman dragons grew out of serpent-like Greek ones combined with Near Eastern dragons in the hybrid Hellenistic culture.
claims.statement_id: Naga Romawi berkembang dari naga Yunani yang berwujud ular, berpadu dengan naga Timur Dekat dalam budaya Helenistik.
claims.quote: Roman dragons developed from serpentine Greek ones, combined with the dragons of the Near East, in the context of the hybrid Greek/Eastern Hellenistic culture.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the word dragon comes from Ancient Greek drákōn, from dérkomai, 'to see, to stare', and Latin draco; in European tradition it is a winged creature with a lizard's tail and clawed feet.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, kata dragon berasal dari bahasa Yunani Kuno drákōn, dari kata kerja dérkomai, "melihat, menatap tajam", dan bahasa Latin draco; dalam tradisi Eropa ia makhluk bersayap berekor kadal dan berkaki bercakar.
claims.quote: Le dragon (du grec ancien δράκων / drákōn, du verbe δέρκομαι / dérkomai, « voir, percer du regard », et du latin draco) est, dans la tradition européenne, une créature légendaire ailée possédant une queue de saurien et dont les pattes se terminent par des griffes.

claims.statement: Python, Ladon and the Lernaean Hydra are often counted as dragons, but ancient works show them only as serpents, sometimes giant or many-headed.
claims.statement_id: Python, Ladon, dan Hydra dari Lerna sering dianggap naga, tetapi dalam karya kuno mereka hanya digambarkan sebagai ular, kadang raksasa atau berkepala banyak.
claims.quote: On considère souvent comme des dragons plusieurs créatures de la mythologie grecque : Python, Ladon, l'Hydre de Lerne, etc. Mais ceux-ci ne sont en réalité représentés sur les œuvres antiques que comme des serpents, parfois gigantesques ou multicéphales.

claims.statement: The terms worm (Germanic myth), wyrm (Anglo-Saxon) and wurm (Old High German) for dragon-like creatures also mean serpent.
claims.statement_id: Istilah worm (mitologi Jermanik), wyrm (Anglo-Saxon), dan wurm (Jerman Tinggi Kuno) untuk makhluk mirip naga juga berarti ular.
claims.quote: Les termes de worm (dans la mythologie germanique), wyrm (en anglo-saxon), ou wurm (en vieux haut allemand) décrivant parfois des créatures apparentées aux dragons signifient par ailleurs serpent.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, dragons whose forelegs are wings like a bird's or bat's are often called wyverns, while wingless ones are sometimes called worms.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, naga yang kaki depannya menjadi sayap seperti burung atau kelelawar sering disebut wyvern, sedangkan naga tanpa sayap kadang disebut worm.
claims.quote: 四肢とは独立して翼を持つのではなく、鳥やコウモリのように前足が翼になっている場合もあり、そうしたものはワイバーン（英: Wyvern）と呼ばれることが多い。逆に、翼を持たない姿で描かれる場合もあり、こちらはワーム（英: Worm）と呼ばれることがある。

claims.statement: In Japanese it is also called ryū; it resembles the Eastern dragon but is not directly related.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Jepang ia juga disebut ryū; ia mirip naga Timur tetapi tidak berhubungan langsung.
claims.quote: 日本語では竜（りゅう）とも呼ばれ、東洋の竜とはその特徴に類似性が認められるものの、直接の関係はない。

claims.statement: The Vegetable Lamb of Tartary (Latin Agnus scythicus or Planta Tartarica Barometz) is a legendary zoophyte of Central Asia believed to bear sheep as fruit; the sheep, tied to the plant by an umbilical cord, grazed around it, and when the foliage was gone both died.
claims.statement_id: Domba Tumbuhan Tartaria (Latin: Agnus scythicus atau Planta Tartarica Barometz) adalah zoofit legendaris Asia Tengah yang dipercaya berbuah domba; domba itu terhubung ke tumbuhan oleh tali pusar dan merumput di sekitarnya, dan bila rumput habis, tumbuhan dan dombanya mati.
claims.quote: The Vegetable Lamb of Tartary (Latin: Agnus scythicus or Planta Tartarica Barometz) is a legendary zoophyte of Central Asia, once believed to grow sheep as its fruit. It was believed the sheep were connected to the plant by an umbilical cord and grazed the land around the plant. When all accessible foliage was gone, both the plant and sheep died.

claims.statement: Behind the legend is the cotton plant, unknown in northern Europe before the Norman conquest of Sicily.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini berakar pada tanaman kapas, yang tidak dikenal di Eropa utara sebelum penaklukan Sisilia oleh bangsa Norman.
claims.quote: Underlying the legend is the cotton plant, which was unknown in Northern Europe before the Norman conquest of Sicily.

claims.statement: Thomas Browne's Pseudodoxia Epidemica called it the Boramez.
claims.statement_id: Pseudodoxia Epidemica karya Thomas Browne menyebutnya Boramez.
claims.quote: Thomas Browne's Pseudodoxia Epidemica named it as the Boramez.

claims.statement: The vegetable lamb was believed to have blood, bones and flesh like an ordinary lamb.
claims.statement_id: Domba tumbuhan ini dipercaya berdarah, bertulang, dan berdaging seperti domba biasa.
claims.quote: The vegetable lamb was believed to have blood, bones, and flesh like that of a normal lamb.

claims.statement: Once dead it could be eaten, its blood supposedly sweet as honey; locals made headwear and clothing from its wool, and apart from humans only wolves were drawn to prey on it.
claims.statement_id: Setelah mati ia dapat dimakan dan darahnya konon manis seperti madu; wolnya dipakai penduduk setempat untuk penutup kepala dan pakaian, dan selain manusia hanya serigala yang tertarik memangsanya.
claims.quote: It could be eaten, once dead, and its blood supposedly tasted sweet like honey. Its wool was said to be used by the native people of its homeland to make head coverings and other articles of clothing. The only carnivorous animals attracted to the lamb plant (other than humans) were wolves.

claims.statement: The Greek historian Herodotus wrote of trees in India whose fruit is a wool finer than sheep's, from which the natives make clothes.
claims.statement_id: Sejarawan Yunani Herodotos menulis tentang pohon di India yang buahnya berupa wol yang lebih indah dan lebih baik daripada wol domba, yang dipakai penduduk untuk pakaian.
claims.quote: The Greek historian Herodotus wrote of trees in India "the fruit whereof is a wool exceeding in beauty and goodness that of sheep. The natives make their clothes of this tree-wool."

claims.statement: A similar plant-animal called the Yeduah appears in Jewish folklore as early as AD 436.
claims.statement_id: Tumbuhan-hewan serupa yang disebut Yeduah sudah disebut dalam cerita rakyat Yahudi sejak tahun 436 M.
claims.quote: There is mention of a similar plant-animal in Jewish folklore as early as AD 436. This creature, called the Yeduah

claims.statement: According to the German article, in the Renaissance the Scythian lamb was the subject of many philosophical and botanical texts that used it to understand nature better.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, pada masa Renaisans domba Skithia menjadi pokok banyak teks filsafat dan botani yang memakainya untuk lebih memahami alam.
claims.quote: In der Renaissance war das Skythische Lamm das Objekt zahlreicher philosophischer und botanischer Texte, die es als Heuristik nutzen, um die Natur besser zu verstehen.

claims.statement: The epithet barometz refers to the Tatar baranetz, 'little lamb'.
claims.statement_id: Nama barometz merujuk kata Tatar baranetz, "anak domba".
claims.quote: Der Beiname barometz bezieht sich auf das tatarische baranetz, was „Lämmchen“ bedeutet.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, the Italian missionary Odoric around 1314 wrote in his travel account that in the Caspian (now Caucasus) mountains there was a melon that bore a beast the size of a lamb.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, misionaris Italia Odorico sekitar 1314 menulis dalam catatan perjalanannya bahwa di Pegunungan Kaspia (kini Kaukasus) ada melon yang melahirkan binatang sebesar anak domba.
claims.quote: イタリアの宣教師オデリコは、1314年ごろに東方布教の旅行を記録した書物『東洋旅行記』において、カスピ山脈（現在のコーカサス山脈）には一頭の仔羊大の獣が生まれるメロンがあると紹介した。

claims.statement: The sea bishop or bishop-fish is a legendary creature first recorded in the 16th century; by legend it was brought to the King of Poland, who wished to keep it, shown to Catholic bishops, gestured to be freed, and once released made the sign of the cross and vanished into the sea.
claims.statement_id: Uskup laut atau ikan uskup adalah makhluk legendaris yang pertama tercatat pada abad ke-16; menurut legenda ia dibawa kepada Raja Polandia yang ingin memeliharanya, lalu diperlihatkan kepada para uskup Katolik, memberi isyarat minta dilepaskan, dan setelah dibebaskan membuat tanda salib lalu lenyap ke laut.
claims.quote: The sea bishop or bishop-fish is a legendary creature first recorded in the 16th century. According to legend, it was taken to the King of Poland, who wished to keep it. It was also shown to a group of Catholic bishops, to whom the bishop-fish gestured, appealing to be released. They granted its wish, at which point it made the sign of the cross and disappeared into the sea.

claims.statement: Another was supposedly caught in the sea off Germany in 1531, refused to eat and died after three days; it was described and pictured in volume four of Conrad Gesner's Historiae animalium (1551–1558 and 1587).
claims.statement_id: Seekor lagi konon ditangkap di laut dekat Jerman pada 1531, menolak makan, dan mati setelah tiga hari; ia dideskripsikan dan digambar dalam jilid keempat Historiae animalium karya Conrad Gesner (1551–1558 dan 1587).
claims.quote: Another was supposedly captured in the ocean near Germany in 1531. It refused to eat and died after three days. It was described and pictured in the fourth volume of Conrad Gesner's famous Historiae animalium, published in 1551–1558 and 1587.

claims.statement: The cryptozoologist Bernard Heuvelmans believed the report was based on a large mutilated Grimaldi scaled squid.
claims.statement_id: Kriptozoolog Bernard Heuvelmans menduga laporan itu berasal dari penemuan cumi-cumi bersisik Grimaldi yang besar dan rusak.
claims.quote: Cryptozoologist Bernard Heuvelmans believed the report was based on the discovery of a large mutilated Grimaldi scaled squid.

claims.statement: The Indonesian article also says the bishop-fish caught near Germany in 1531 refused food and died three days later.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Indonesia juga menyebut ikan uskup yang ditangkap dekat Jerman pada 1531 menolak makan dan mati tiga hari kemudian.
claims.quote: Ikan uskup lainnya ditangkap di samudera dekat Jerman pada 1531. Ia menolak untuk makan dan mati tiga hari kemudian.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, it looks like a huge fish whose tail fin forms legs and pectoral fins clawed arms, with a conical head, walking upright like a man.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, ia berwujud ikan besar dengan sirip ekor seperti kaki, sirip dada seperti lengan bercakar, kepala kerucut, dan berjalan tegak seperti manusia.
claims.quote: 巨大な魚の姿をしているが、尾鰭が脚、胸鰭が鉤爪のついた腕のように発達しており、頭は円錐形。人間のように直立歩行で移動する。

claims.statement: Various identities have been proposed, such as the angelshark, walrus or hooded seal.
claims.statement_id: Ada berbagai dugaan tentang identitasnya, seperti hiu malaikat, walrus, atau anjing laut bertudung.
claims.quote: ビショップ・フィッシュの正体については諸説あり、カスザメ、セイウチ、ズキンアザラシなどの候補が挙げられている。

claims.statement: The Christian view that the sea, like the land, has its own clergy shaped the idea of the bishop-fish.
claims.statement_id: Pandangan Kristen bahwa laut pun memiliki rohaniwan seperti di darat ikut membentuk gagasan ikan uskup.
claims.quote: 地上と同じように、海中にも聖職者が存在するキリスト教的な世界観が、ビショップ・フィッシュの創造に影響を与え

claims.statement: The Japanese article equates the bishop-fish with the Sea monk ('monk of the sea'), a legendary sea creature of medieval European folklore.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Jepang menyamakan ikan uskup dengan Sea monk ("biarawan laut"), makhluk laut legendaris dalam cerita rakyat Eropa abad pertengahan.
claims.quote: ビショップ・フィッシュ（「海の司教」の意）またはシー・モンク（「海の修道士」の意）とは、中世ヨーロッパの民話に登場する伝説の海洋生物。

claims.statement: The Coco or Coca (also Cucuy, Cuco, Cuca or El Cucuí) is a mythical ghost-like monster, the bogeyman's equivalent, found in Portugal and Spain, whose belief has spread to many Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries.
claims.statement_id: Coco atau Coca (juga Cucuy, Cuco, Cuca, atau El Cucuí) adalah monster mitis mirip hantu, padanan bogeyman, di Portugal dan Spanyol, yang kepercayaannya juga menyebar ke banyak negara berbahasa Spanyol dan Portugis.
claims.quote: The Coco or Coca (also known as the Cucuy, Cuco, Cuca, Cucu, Cucuí or El Cucuí) is a mythical ghost-like monster, equivalent to the bogeyman, found in Portugal and Spain. Those beliefs have also spread in many Hispanophone and Lusophone countries.

claims.statement: The Cucuy is male and the Cuca the female version; the monster comes at night to the homes of disobedient children and takes them away.
claims.statement_id: Cucuy adalah sosok laki-laki dan Cuca versi perempuannya; monster ini datang pada malam hari ke rumah anak yang tidak patuh dan membawa mereka pergi.
claims.quote: The Cucuy is a male being while Cuca is a female version of the mythical monster. The "monster" will come to the house of disobedient children at night and take them away.

claims.statement: The myth of the Coco or Cucuy began in northern Portugal and Galicia; colloquially in Spanish coco means the human head, and also 'skull'.
claims.statement_id: Mitos Coco atau Cucuy berasal dari Portugal utara dan Galisia; dalam bahasa Spanyol sehari-hari coco berarti kepala manusia, dan juga "tengkorak".
claims.quote: The myth of the Coco, or Cucuy, originated in northern Portugal and Galicia. The word coco is used in colloquial speech to refer to the human head in Spanish. Coco also means "skull".

claims.statement: In Brazilian folklore it is the Cuca, pictured as a blonde female humanoid alligator; this reptile form actually comes from the 1952 TV show Sítio do Pica-pau Amarelo.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Brasil ia disebut Cuca, digambarkan sebagai buaya perempuan mirip manusia berambut pirang; wujud reptil ini sebenarnya berasal dari acara televisi Sítio do Pica-pau Amarelo tahun 1952.
claims.quote: In Brazilian folklore, the monster is referred to as Cuca and pictured as a female humanoid alligator with blond hair. Though this reptilian form resembles the Portuguese coca, a dragon, it actually originates from the 1952's TV show Sítio do Pica-pau Amarelo (1952 TV series).

claims.statement: In the only book she appears in, O saci (1921), Monteiro Lobato says only that Cuca had an 'alligator face' and 'clawed fingers'.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu-satunya buku yang memuatnya, O saci (1921), Monteiro Lobato hanya menyebut Cuca berwajah buaya dan berjari bercakar.
claims.quote: In the only book she appears, O saci (1921), Cuca's description is vague, Monteiro Lobato only states that she had an "alligator face" and "clawed fingers".

claims.statement: Many Latin American countries call it El Cuco, and in northern New Mexico and southern Colorado it is 'the Coco Man'.
claims.statement_id: Banyak negara Amerika Latin menyebutnya El Cuco, dan di New Mexico utara serta Colorado selatan ia disebut "the Coco Man".
claims.quote: Many Latin American countries refer to the monster as El Cuco. In northern New Mexico and southern Colorado, where there is a large Hispanic population, it is referred to by its anglicized name, "the Coco Man".

claims.statement: According to the French article, the Coco, also Cuco, Cucuy or Cuculelé, is a kind of bogeyman of Hispanic and Portuguese folklore who comes to punish badly behaved children.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Coco, juga Cuco, Cucuy, atau Cuculelé, adalah semacam momok dalam cerita rakyat Spanyol dan Portugal yang datang menghukum anak nakal.
claims.quote: Le Coco, aussi nommé Cuco, Cucuy ou Cuculelé dans les pays d'Amérique latine, est une créature du folklore hispanique et portugais correspondant à une sorte de croque-mitaine qui vient punir les enfants qui se sont mal conduits.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, it is often described as a disciplinary agent that frightens children into obedience under threat of 'taking away' those who misbehave or will not sleep, and it has no defined physical form.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, ia sering digambarkan sebagai alat disiplin yang menakuti anak agar patuh, dengan ancaman akan "membawa pergi" anak yang nakal atau tidak mau tidur, dan tidak memiliki wujud fisik yang pasti.
claims.quote: Es a menudo descrita como un agente disciplinario, cuya función principal es emplear tácticas de intimidación con fines disuasorios para inducir la obediencia en los menores, generalmente bajo la amenaza de "llevarse" o aprehender a aquellos que exhiben conductas inapropiadas o presentan resistencia al sueño. Carece de una forma física definida
