claims.statement: The tale of the Knight of the Swan is a medieval story of a mysterious rescuer who arrives in a swan-drawn boat to defend a damsel, on the sole condition that he must never be asked his name.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Ksatria Angsa adalah dongeng abad pertengahan tentang penyelamat misterius yang datang dengan perahu yang ditarik angsa untuk membela seorang gadis, dengan satu-satunya syarat bahwa namanya tidak boleh ditanyakan.
claims.quote: The story of the Knight of the Swan, or Swan Knight, is a medieval tale about a mysterious rescuer who comes in a swan-drawn boat to defend a damsel, his only condition being that he must never be asked his name.

claims.statement: The earliest versions, in John of Alta Silva's Dolopathos, give the knight no identity, but the Old French Crusade cycle of chansons de geste made the Swan Knight (Le Chevalier au Cigne, first version c. 1192) the legendary ancestor of Godfrey of Bouillon.
claims.statement_id: Versi tertua dalam Dolopathos karya John of Alta Silva tidak menyebut identitasnya, tetapi siklus chanson de geste Perang Salib dalam bahasa Prancis Kuno menjadikan Ksatria Angsa (Le Chevalier au Cigne, versi pertama sekitar 1192) leluhur legendaris Godefroy dari Bouillon.
claims.quote: The earliest versions, preserved in John of Alta Silva's Dolopathos) do not provide specific identity to this knight, but the Old French Crusade cycle of chansons de geste adapted it to make the Swan Knight (Le Chevalier au Cigne, first version around 1192) the legendary ancestor of Godfrey of Bouillon.

claims.statement: Later the German poet Wolfram von Eschenbach brought the swan knight Loherangrin into his epic Parzival in the early 13th century.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian penyair Jerman Wolfram von Eschenbach memasukkan ksatria angsa Loherangrin ke dalam epos Parzival pada awal abad ke-13.
claims.quote: At a later time, the German poet Wolfram von Eschenbach incorporated the swan knight Loherangrin into his Matter of Britain epic Parzival (first quarter of the 13th century).

claims.statement: Wolfram's and Konrad von Würzburg's texts were used for the libretto of Richard Wagner's opera Lohengrin (Weimar, 1850).
claims.statement_id: Teks Wolfram dan Konrad von Würzburg menjadi dasar libretto opera Lohengrin karya Richard Wagner (Weimar, 1850).
claims.quote: Wolfram's and Konrad's texts were used to construct the libretto for Richard Wagner's opera Lohengrin (Weimar 1850).

claims.statement: The related Swan Children tale resembles The Six Swans, in which brothers turned into birds are saved by their sister.
claims.statement_id: Kisah anak-anak angsa yang terkait legenda ini mirip dongeng The Six Swans, tentang saudara-saudara yang diubah menjadi burung dan diselamatkan saudari mereka.
claims.quote: It also bears resemblance to the fairy tale The Six Swans, where brothers transformed into birds are rescued by the efforts of their sister.

claims.statement: According to the German article, the Swan Knight legend comes from the Burgundian Netherlands, was retold in works such as Konrad von Würzburg's verse tale Der Schwanritter, and served several Lower Rhine dynasties as an origin legend.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, legenda Ksatria Angsa berasal dari Belanda Burgundia, digubah antara lain dalam syair Der Schwanritter karya Konrad von Würzburg, dan menjadi legenda asal-usul beberapa wangsa di Rhein Hilir.
claims.quote: Die Schwanenrittersage ist eine in mehreren Varianten überlieferte mittelalterliche Sage aus den Burgundischen Niederlanden. Sie erhielt unterschiedliche Ausformungen in der Literatur (so die Verserzählung „Der Schwanritter“ von Konrad von Würzburg) und diente einigen Herrscherhäusern am Niederrhein als genealogische Ursprungssage.

claims.statement: According to the French article, in the shortest version an armed stranger lands in a swan-towed boat, proves his valour, wins a fief and a wife, and one day, when the swan returns, leaps into the boat and vanishes as he came.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, dalam versi paling ringkas seorang asing bersenjata mendarat dengan perahu yang ditarik angsa, menunjukkan keberanian, mendapat tanah dan istri, lalu suatu hari angsa itu kembali dan ia pergi seperti saat datang.
claims.quote: Dans la version la plus condensée de l’histoire, un inconnu en armes aborde sur un rivage dans une barque remorquée par un cygne. L'inconnu fait preuve de vaillance et obtient en récompense un fief et une épouse, avec qui il a des enfants. Un jour, le cygne réapparaît : l’inconnu saute dans la barque qui est aussitôt entraînée au large par l’oiseau et disparaît comme il était venu.

claims.statement: The Swan Knight is a legendary medieval figure of Western Europe attested from the 12th century.
claims.statement_id: Ksatria Angsa adalah tokoh legendaris abad pertengahan Eropa Barat yang tercatat sejak abad ke-12.
claims.quote: Le chevalier au cygne est un personnage légendaire médiéval de l'Europe occidentale, attesté dès le XIIe siècle.

claims.statement: The yale or centicore (Latin eale) is a mythical beast of European mythology and heraldry.
claims.statement_id: Yale atau centicore (Latin: eale) adalah binatang mitis dalam mitologi dan heraldik Eropa.
claims.quote: The yale or centicore (Latin: eale) is a mythical beast found in European mythology and heraldry.

claims.statement: The name yale is thought to come from the Hebrew yael, 'ibex'.
claims.statement_id: Nama yale diyakini berasal dari kata Ibrani yael, "ibex".
claims.quote: The name "yale" is believed to be derived from the Hebrew word יָעֵל (yael), meaning "ibex".

claims.statement: The yale is described as antelope- or goat-like, with a boar's tusks and large horns that swivel in any direction, useful for attack and defence.
claims.statement_id: Yale digambarkan mirip antelop atau kambing, bertaring babi hutan dan bertanduk besar yang dapat diputar ke segala arah sehingga berguna untuk menyerang maupun bertahan.
claims.quote: The yale is described as an antelope- or goat-like creature with the tusks of a boar and large horns. These horns possess the ability to swivel in any direction which makes them good for both offensive and defensive attacks.

claims.statement: Pliny the Elder in his Natural History describes the eale of Aethiopia as the size of a hippopotamus, with an elephant's tail, black or tawny, with a boar's jaws and movable horns over a cubit long.
claims.statement_id: Plinius Tua dalam Naturalis Historia menggambarkan eale dari Aethiopia sebesar kuda nil, berekor gajah, berwarna hitam atau cokelat kekuningan, berahang babi hutan, dan bertanduk yang dapat digerakkan, lebih panjang dari satu hasta.
claims.quote: it is the size of the river-horse, has the tail of the elephant, and is of a black or tawny colour. It has also the jaws of the wild boar, and horns that are moveable, and more than a cubit in length

claims.statement: Antelope and buffalo of the sub-Saharan plains loosely match Pliny's description and may have caused his misunderstanding.
claims.statement_id: Antelop dan kerbau di dataran Afrika sub-Sahara agak cocok dengan gambaran Plinius dan mungkin menjadi asal salah pahamnya.
claims.quote: Pliny reports sighting the yale while on the sub-Saharan African plains. The antelope and buffalo inhabit this region and loosely match his description, so may have given rise to his misunderstanding.

claims.statement: According to the German article, the yale is among the heraldic beasts of the British royal family, used as a supporter by John of Lancaster, Duke of Bedford, and by the House of Beaufort, its link with the British monarchy beginning around 1485 with Henry VII Tudor.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, yale termasuk binatang heraldik keluarga kerajaan Britania, dipakai sebagai penyangga lambang John of Lancaster, Duke of Bedford, dan oleh Wangsa Beaufort, dan hubungannya dengan monarki Britania bermula sekitar 1485 dengan Henry VII Tudor.
claims.quote: Das Yale ist unter den heraldischen Bestien der britischen Königsfamilie vertreten. Es fand als „Supporter“ der Streitkräfte von John of Lancaster, Herzog von Bedford, und im englischen House of Beaufort Verwendung. Seine Verbindung mit der britischen Monarchie begann etwa 1485 mit Heinrich VII. Tudor.

claims.statement: It appears in medieval bestiaries and heraldry, where it stands for strong defence.
claims.statement_id: Ia muncul dalam bestiari abad pertengahan dan heraldik sebagai lambang pertahanan yang kuat.
claims.quote: Die Kreatur kommt in mittelalterlichen Bestiarien und in der Heraldik vor, wo sie für eine starke Verteidigung steht.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, in a fight it points one horn forward and keeps the other back, swapping them when the first is damaged.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, saat bertarung ia menjulurkan satu tanduk ke depan dan menarik yang lain ke belakang, lalu menukarnya bila tanduk pertama rusak.
claims.quote: 戦いの時は、片方の角を前に伸ばして戦い、もう片方の角は後ろに向けておくという。それで、戦っている方の角が傷付くと、もう片方の角と入れ替えるという。

claims.statement: Per medieval European bestiaries, the basilisk is the yale's enemy and pierces the eyes of a sleeping yale.
claims.statement_id: Menurut bestiari Eropa abad pertengahan, basilisk adalah musuh yale yang menusuk mata yale yang sedang tidur.
claims.quote: 中世ヨーロッパの動物寓意譚によるとバジリスクはエアレーの敵で、眠っているエアレーを見つけると目を刺し、張り裂けるまで膨らませるという。

claims.statement: The churel is a mythical woman-like creature, perhaps a demonic revenant, found in South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Caribbean, especially India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Trinidad and Tobago, Guyana and Suriname.
claims.statement_id: Churel adalah makhluk mitis berwujud perempuan, mungkin mayat hidup yang jahat, yang dikenal di Asia Selatan, Asia Tenggara, dan Karibia, terutama di India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Trinidad dan Tobago, Guyana, dan Suriname.
claims.quote: is a mythical or legendary creature resembling a woman, which may be a demonical revenant said to occur in South Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Caribbean, particularly popular in India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Trinidad and Tobago, Guyana, and Suriname.

claims.statement: The churel is usually called 'the ghost of an unpurified living thing', also a tree-spirit since she clings to trees; by some legends a woman who dies cruelly returns as a churel for revenge, especially on the men of her family.
claims.statement_id: Churel biasa disebut "hantu makhluk hidup yang tidak disucikan", juga roh pohon karena sering menempel di pohon; menurut sebagian legenda perempuan yang mati secara kejam kembali sebagai churel untuk membalas dendam, terutama kepada lelaki dalam keluarganya.
claims.quote: The churel is typically described as  "the ghost of an unpurified living thing", but because she is often said to latch on to trees, she is also called a tree-spirit. According to some legends, a woman who dies very cruelly will come back as a revenant churel for revenge, particularly targeting the males in her family.

claims.statement: The churel is usually hideous but can disguise herself as a beautiful woman to lure men into the woods or hills, where she kills them or drains their life force until they turn old; her feet point backwards.
claims.statement_id: Churel biasanya sangat buruk rupa, tetapi dapat menyamar sebagai perempuan cantik untuk memikat lelaki ke hutan atau gunung, lalu membunuh mereka atau mengisap daya hidupnya hingga menjadi tua; kakinya menghadap ke belakang.
claims.quote: The churel is mostly described as extremely ugly and hideous but is able to shape-shift and disguise herself as a beautiful woman to lure men into the woods or mountains where she either kills them or sucks up their life-force or virility, turning them into old men. Their feet are believed to be turned the other way around, so the toes face the direction of their back.

claims.statement: The family of a woman who dies a tragic or unnatural death may hold special rites lest she return as a churel, and suspected corpses are buried in a particular way and posture.
claims.statement_id: Keluarga perempuan yang mati secara tragis atau tidak wajar dapat menggelar ritual khusus agar ia tidak kembali sebagai churel, dan jasad yang dicurigai dikubur dengan cara dan posisi tertentu.
claims.quote: The family of a woman who dies a traumatic, tragic, or unnatural death might perform special rituals fearing that the victimised woman might return as a churel. The corpses of suspected churels are also buried in a particular method and posture so as to prevent her from returning.

claims.statement: The churel is known as Pichal Peri in Punjab, Petni or Shakchunni in Bengal, and Pontianak in Malaysia and Indonesia.
claims.statement_id: Churel dikenal sebagai Pichal Peri di Punjab, Petni atau Shakchunni di Bengal, dan Pontianak di Malaysia dan Indonesia.
claims.quote: The churel is known as the Pichal Peri in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan, Petni/Shakchunni in the Bengal region, and Pontianak in Malaysia and Indonesia.

claims.statement: The churel legend supposedly began in Persia, where they were the spirits of women who died with 'grossly unsatisfied desires'.
claims.statement_id: Legenda churel konon berasal dari Persia, tempat mereka digambarkan sebagai roh perempuan yang mati dengan hasrat yang sangat tidak terpenuhi.
claims.quote: The legend of Churel supposedly originated from Persia where they were described as being the spirits of women who died with "grossly unsatisfied desires".

claims.statement: According to the Italian article, many folk remedies and sayings explain how to get rid of churels and stop them returning.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, ada banyak penangkal rakyat dan pepatah tentang cara mengusir churel dan mencegahnya kembali.
claims.quote: Esistono molti rimedi popolari e detti che spiegano come liberarsi dalle Churel e diverse misure per impedire il loro ritorno in vita.

claims.statement: According to the Assamese article, a woman who dies in childbirth, in pregnancy or through her in-laws' cruelty returns as a churel for revenge, especially on the family's men.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Assam, perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan, saat hamil, atau karena siksaan mertuanya kembali sebagai churel untuk membalas dendam, terutama kepada lelaki keluarganya.
claims.quote: কিছুমান কিংবদন্তি অনুসৰি প্ৰসৱ বা গৰ্ভাৱস্থাৰ সময়ত বা শহুৰেকৰ হাতত দুখ-কষ্টৰ ফলত মৃত্যু হোৱা মহিলাগৰাকীয়ে প্ৰতিশোধৰ বাবে, বিশেষকৈ পৰিয়ালৰ পুৰুষসকলক লক্ষ্য কৰি প্ৰেতনী হিচাপে ঘূৰি আহে।

claims.statement: In Germanic mythology Sigmund (Old Norse Sigmundr, Old English Sigemund) is a hero whose story is told in the Völsunga saga.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Jermanik, Sigmund (Norse Kuno: Sigmundr; Inggris Kuno: Sigemund) adalah pahlawan yang kisahnya diceritakan dalam saga Völsunga.
claims.quote: In Germanic mythology, Sigmund (Old Norse: Sigmundr [ˈsiɣˌmundz̠], Old English: Sigemund) is a hero whose story is told in the Völsunga saga.

claims.statement: He and his sister Signý are the children of Völsung and his wife Hljod, and Sigmund is best known as the father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer.
claims.statement_id: Ia dan saudarinya Signý adalah anak Völsung dan istrinya Hljod, dan Sigmund paling dikenal sebagai ayah Sigurð si pembunuh naga.
claims.quote: He and his sister, Signý, are the children of Völsung and his wife Hljod. Sigmund is best known as the father of Sigurð the dragon-slayer

claims.statement: Odin, disguised as a beggar, thrusts the sword Gram into the tree Barnstokk in Völsung's hall, saying whoever pulls it out may keep it; only Sigmund succeeds.
claims.statement_id: Odin yang menyamar sebagai pengemis menancapkan pedang Gram ke pohon Barnstokk di tengah balairung Völsung dan menyatakan siapa pun yang mencabutnya boleh memilikinya; hanya Sigmund yang berhasil.
claims.quote: when Odin, disguised as a beggar, plunges a sword (Gram) into the living tree Barnstokk ("offspring-trunk") around which Völsung's hall is built. The disguised Odin announces that the man who can remove the sword will have it as a gift. Only Sigmund is able to free the sword from the tree.

claims.statement: When the Völsungs arrive in Gautland they are attacked by the Gauts; King Völsung is killed and his sons captured.
claims.statement_id: Ketika klan Völsung datang ke Gautland, mereka diserang orang Gaut; Raja Völsung tewas dan putra-putranya ditawan.
claims.quote: When the Völsung clan arrive, they are attacked by the Gauts; King Völsung is killed and his sons captured.

claims.statement: After the she-wolf, Siggeir's shapeshifting mother, devours his brothers one by one, on the ninth night Signý has honey smeared on Sigmund's face; when the wolf licks it and puts her tongue in his mouth, he bites it off and kills her.
claims.statement_id: Setelah serigala betina jelmaan ibu Siggeir memangsa saudara-saudaranya satu per satu, pada malam kesembilan Signý menyuruh pelayan mengoleskan madu ke wajah Sigmund; ketika serigala itu menjilat dan memasukkan lidahnya ke mulut Sigmund, ia menggigit putus lidahnya.
claims.quote: On the ninth night, she has a servant smear honey on Sigmund's face and when the she-wolf arrives, she starts licking the honey off and sticks her tongue into Sigmund's mouth, whereupon Sigmund bites her tongue off, killing her.

claims.statement: According to the German article, with his twin sister Signy he fathered Sinfjötli, with whom he avenged Völsung's murder.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, bersama saudari kembarnya Signy ia memperoleh putra Sinfjötli, yang bersamanya membalas pembunuhan Völsung.
claims.quote: Mit seiner Zwillingsschwester Signy zeugte er einen Sohn Sinfiötli, mit dem zusammen er den Mord an seinem Vater Wölsung rächte.

claims.statement: The two lived as outlaws, for a time as werewolves, until they avenged Völsung by killing Siggeir.
claims.statement_id: Keduanya hidup sebagai buronan, sempat menjadi manusia serigala, sampai berhasil membalas dendam dengan membunuh Siggeir.
claims.quote: Die beiden lebten als Geächtete, erlebten einige Abenteuer, zwischenzeitlich auch als Werwölfe, bis es ihnen gelang ihren Vater/Großvater Wölsung zu rächen, indem sie Siggeir töteten.

claims.statement: According to the French article, he appears in the Völsunga saga and Þiðrekssaga, is named Sigemund in Beowulf, and his story is adapted in the opera Die Walküre of Richard Wagner's Ring cycle.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, ia muncul dalam saga Völsunga dan Þiðrekssaga, disebut sebagai Sigemund dalam Beowulf, dan kisahnya diadaptasi dalam opera Die Walküre dari siklus Der Ring des Nibelungen karya Richard Wagner.
claims.quote: Il apparaît notamment dans la Völsunga saga, la Þiðrekssaga, et est également mentionné dans le poème anglo-saxon Beowulf sous le nom de Sigemund. Une adaptation de son histoire apparaît dans l'opéra La Walkyrie (Die Walküre) du cycle de L'Anneau du Nibelung (Der Ring des Nibelungen), de Richard Wagner.

claims.statement: Aatxe (a contraction of aratxe) is a spirit of Basque folk mythology; his name means 'young bull', and he is sometimes called Etsai.
claims.statement_id: Aatxe (kependekan dari aratxe) adalah roh dalam mitologi rakyat Basque; namanya berarti "banteng muda", dan kadang ia disebut Etsai.
claims.quote: Aatxe (pronounced [a.atʃe]; a contraction of aratxe) is a spirit in the folk mythology of the Basque people. His name is literally translated as "Young Bull", and he is sometimes known as Etsai.

claims.statement: He is a cave-dwelling spirit in the form of a young red bull, but as a shapeshifter sometimes becomes a man, a cow or a calf.
claims.statement_id: Ia roh penghuni gua yang berwujud banteng muda merah, tetapi sebagai pengubah wujud kadang menjadi manusia, sapi, atau anak sapi.
claims.quote: He is a cave-dwelling spirit who adopts the form of a young red bull, but being a shapeshifter, sometimes takes the shape of a man. Aatxe is also described as a shapeshifter that may appear not only as a bull but also as a cow or calf.

claims.statement: At night, especially in storms, he comes out of his lair and attacks criminals and other wicked people.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam hari, terutama saat badai, ia keluar dari lubang sarangnya dan menyerang penjahat serta orang jahat lain.
claims.quote: At night, more so in stormy weather, he arises from the hollow which is his lair. He attacks criminals and other malevolent people.

claims.statement: He is thought to represent the goddess Mari or enforce her will, punishing those who cheat her; another name is Aatxegorri, 'young red bull'.
claims.statement_id: Ia diduga wakil dewi Mari atau pelaksana kehendaknya yang menghukum orang yang menipunya; nama lainnya Aatxegorri, "banteng muda merah".
claims.quote: He is theorized to be a representative of the goddess Mari, or may be an enforcer of her will, punishing people who cheat her. Another name for him is Aatxegorri which means "young red bull".

claims.statement: In many caves Aatxe was thought to inhabit, such as Isturits, Sare and Errenteria, engravings and paintings of aurochs, bulls and oxen have been found, implying the myth goes back to the Palaeolithic.
claims.statement_id: Di banyak gua yang dihuni Aatxe, seperti Isturits, Sare, dan Errenteria, ditemukan ukiran dan lukisan aurochs, banteng, dan lembu, yang menunjukkan mitos ini berakar pada zaman Paleolitik.
claims.quote: It is believed Aatxe inhabited caves and hollows; in many (Isturits, Sare, Errenteria, among others) engravings and paintings depicting aurochs, bulls, and oxen have been found; which implies that this Basque myth has its origins in the Paleolithic.

claims.statement: According to the German article, the Aatxe are cave spirits that on stormy nights leave the Leze cave near Sare and drive villagers into their houses.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, Aatxe adalah roh gua yang pada malam badai keluar dari gua Leze dekat Sara dan menggiring penduduk desa masuk ke rumah.
claims.quote: Die Aatxe oder Aataxe sind Höhlengeister aus der Mythologie des Baskenlandes, die in stürmischen Nächten ihre Höhle Leze (bei Sara) verlassen und die Bewohner der Dörfer und Städte in die Häuser treiben.

claims.statement: According to the French article on Behigorri, Aatxe ('calf') is Behigorri's young, also called Aatxegorri or Txahalgorri.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis tentang Behigorri, Aatxe ("anak sapi") adalah anak Behigorri dan juga disebut Aatxegorri atau Txahalgorri.
claims.quote: Son petit, Aatxe qui signifie veau en basque est aussi appelé Behigorri, Aatxegorri ou Aatexegorrila, Txaalgorri, Txalgorri ou Txahalgorri.

claims.statement: In Basque mythology Basajaun ('Lord of the forest', plural basajaunak) is a huge hairy hominid living in the woods, thought to protect flocks and teach humans farming and ironworking.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Basque, Basajaun ("Tuan hutan", jamak basajaunak) adalah makhluk mirip manusia yang besar dan berbulu, tinggal di hutan, yang dipercaya melindungi kawanan ternak dan mengajari manusia bertani dan menempa besi.
claims.quote: is a huge, hairy hominid dwelling in the woods. They were thought to protect flocks of livestock and teach skills such as agriculture and ironworking to humans.

claims.statement: Basajaun (also Baxajaun) means 'Lord of the forest' or 'wild lord', and his female counterpart, the Basandere, was probably created later by analogy.
claims.statement_id: Basajaun (juga Baxajaun) berarti "Tuan hutan" atau "tuan liar", dan pasangan perempuannya Basandere mungkin diciptakan belakangan berdasarkan analogi.
claims.quote: Basajaun (var. Baxajaun, Basque pronunciation: [baʃajaun]) is glossed "Lord of the forest" or the "wild lord". The female counterpart is the Basandere (var. Basa Andre, Basa-Andre,) probably created during a later period by analogy.

claims.statement: The Basajaun is tall and humanlike, his face and body covered in hair reaching the knees, walking upright like a man.
claims.statement_id: Basajaun berwujud manusia yang tinggi, wajah dan tubuhnya tertutup rambut sampai lutut, dan berjalan tegak seperti manusia.
claims.quote: The Basajaun is said to have a tall, human form with his face and body covered in hair, with the strands reaching the knees, walking upright like a man.

claims.statement: His two feet differ: one is normal, while the left is round like a tree stump and leaves circular tracks.
claims.statement_id: Kedua kakinya berbeda bentuk: satu normal, sedangkan kaki kirinya bulat seperti tunggul pohon dan meninggalkan jejak melingkar.
claims.quote: His two feet are differently shaped, thus leaving an odd set of foot tracks. While one foot is normal, the other one (left foot) is rounded like the tree stump (base of a tree trunk) and leaves circular footprints.

claims.statement: He may have a single eye in the middle of his forehead, also a trait of the Tartalo, with whom he is often confused.
claims.statement_id: Ia kadang bermata satu di tengah dahi, ciri yang juga dimiliki Tartalo, raksasa yang sering dicampuradukkan dengannya.
claims.quote: He may have a single eye in the middle of the forehead, though this is also the attribute of the Tartalo with which the Basajaun is often confounded.

claims.statement: The basajaunak live in forests and caves at higher altitudes, such as the slopes of Gorbea in Biscay, around Ataun in Gipuzkoa and the Irati Forest in the Pyrenees.
claims.statement_id: Basajaunak tinggal di hutan dan gua di dataran tinggi, misalnya lereng Gorbea di Biscaya, sekitar Ataun di Gipuzkoa, dan Hutan Irati di Pyrenees.
claims.quote: The basajaunak dwell in the forests and caverns at higher altitudes or "prominent places". More specifically, it is said to inhabit the mountainside of the Gorbea in Biscay Province (or the forests of Zeanuri town nearby), around Ataun town which is the backwoods of neighboring Gipuzkoa Province, and the Irati Forest of the Pyrenees

claims.statement: It is called Basajun in the Basque-Navarre valleys and Aragonese Pyrenees, and Basajarau or Bonjarau in the Tena, Ansó and Broto valleys of Aragon.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut Basajun di lembah Basque-Navarra dan Pyrenees Aragon, serta Basajarau atau Bonjarau di lembah Tena, Ansó, dan Broto di Aragon.
claims.quote: The creature is called Basajun in the Basque-Navarre valleys as well as the Aragonese Pyrenees to where the name may have been transmitted (from Basque country) while the creature is called Basajarau, Bonjarau in the Tena Valley and the vales of the cities of Anso and Broto in Aragon

claims.statement: According to the French article he sometimes enters houses or sheepfolds and helps himself to prepared food without anyone daring to stop him, inspiring fear and respect.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, ia kadang masuk ke rumah atau kandang domba dan mengambil makanan yang sudah disiapkan tanpa ada yang berani menghalangi, sehingga ia ditakuti sekaligus dihormati.
claims.quote: Il pénètre parfois dans les maisons ou les bergeries, se sert sans vergogne de la nourriture préparée, sans que les humains n'osent intervenir. Il inspire crainte et respect.

claims.statement: In body and behaviour he resembles the 'wild men' of many European traditions or Silvanus, ancient protector of nature and of farming and herding.
claims.statement_id: Ciri dan perilakunya mirip "lelaki liar" dalam banyak tradisi Eropa atau Silvanus, pelindung kuno alam serta pertanian dan penggembalaan.
claims.quote: Par ses caractères physiques et son comportement, il s'apparente aux « hommes sauvages » de nombreuses traditions européennes ou aux sylvains (Sylvanus), protecteurs antiques de la nature et des activités agro-pastorales

claims.statement: The Japanese article also says Basajaun guarded the flocks and taught humans farming and smithing.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Jepang juga menyebut Basajaun melindungi kawanan domba dan mengajari manusia bertani dan menempa besi.
claims.quote: バシャジャウンは、畜産羊の群れを守り、人間に農業や鉄鍛冶の技術を教えた、とされている。

claims.statement: The dahu is a legendary creature like a mountain goat, well known in France and the French-speaking parts of Switzerland and Italy, including the Aosta Valley.
claims.statement_id: Dahu adalah makhluk legendaris mirip kambing gunung yang terkenal di Prancis serta daerah berbahasa Prancis di Swiss dan Italia, termasuk Lembah Aosta.
claims.quote: The dahu (French pronunciation: [da.y]) is a legendary creature that resembles a mountain goat and is well known in France and francophone regions of Switzerland and Italy, including the Aosta Valley.

claims.statement: The dahu may have been inspired by the chamois, a small horned goat-antelope once common in European mountains, and also resembles the ibex.
claims.statement_id: Dahu mungkin terilhami chamois, kambing-antelop bertanduk kecil yang dulu banyak di pegunungan Eropa, dan juga mirip ibex.
claims.quote: The dahu, a quadrupedal mammal, may have been inspired by the chamois, a small, horned goat-antelope once plentiful in European mountainous regions, and also resembles the ibex.

claims.statement: Its main feature is that the legs on one side of its body are shorter than on the other, to help it stand and walk on steep slopes.
claims.statement_id: Ciri utamanya adalah kaki di satu sisi tubuh lebih pendek daripada sisi lain agar mudah berdiri dan berjalan di lereng gunung yang curam.
claims.quote: The dahu's principal distinguishing characteristic is that the legs on one side of its body are shorter than the legs on the opposite side, to facilitate standing on and walking on steep mountain slopes.

claims.statement: So there are two kinds: the laevogyrous dahu, with shorter left legs, circles the mountain anticlockwise, and the dextrogyre dahu, with shorter right legs, clockwise.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu ada dua jenis dahu: dahu levogir berkaki kiri pendek yang berjalan mengitari gunung berlawanan arah jarum jam, dan dahu dekstrogir berkaki kanan pendek yang berjalan searah jarum jam.
claims.quote: Therefore, there are two different types of dahu: the laevogyrous dahu, with shorter legs on its left side, walks around the mountain counterclockwise; the dextrogyre dahu, with the shorter legs on its right side, walks clockwise around the mountain.

claims.statement: The 'dahu hunt' (chasse au dahu), like the snipe hunt, is a prank in which the victim is taken out at night to catch a dahu and then abandoned on the mountain.
claims.statement_id: "Perburuan dahu" (chasse au dahu), mirip lelucon snipe hunt, adalah keisengan di mana korban diajak keluar malam-malam untuk menangkap dahu lalu ditinggalkan di gunung.
claims.quote: The "dahu hunt" (French: chasse au dahu), similar to another wildlife-related practical joke, the snipe hunt, is a prank in which pranksters may take a victim out at night with the stated intention of catching a dahu only to abandon the victim on the mountain.

claims.statement: Supposedly, when the dahu turns towards an imitated call, it loses its balance and rolls down the slope to the person with the sack.
claims.statement_id: Konon dahu yang menoleh ke arah suara tiruan akan kehilangan keseimbangan dan berguling ke bawah lereng ke arah orang yang memegang karung.
claims.quote: When the dahu turns around to see the source of the sound, it will lose its balance and roll down the slope to the person with the bag.

claims.statement: According to the German article, the dahu (also Dahut, Däjü or Dairi in the Jura, Darou in the Vosges, Tamarou in the Pyrenees) is a fabulous creature, the French-speaking counterpart of the Bavarian Wolpertinger.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, dahu (juga Dahut, Däjü, atau Dairi di Jura, Darou di Vosges, Tamarou di Pyrenees) adalah makhluk dongeng padanan berbahasa Prancis bagi Wolpertinger Bayern.
claims.quote: Der Dahu (schweiz. auch das Dahu, auch Dahut, Däjü oder Dairi im Jura), Darou in den Vogesen oder Tamarou in den Pyrenäen – ist ein Fabelwesen und eine frankophone Entsprechung zum bayerischen Wolpertinger beziehungsweise dem Hanghuhn.

claims.statement: The dahu is sometimes described as chamois-like, sometimes as a mix of weasel, rabbit, squirrel, bird and goat.
claims.statement_id: Dahu kadang digambarkan mirip chamois, kadang sebagai campuran musang, kelinci, tupai, burung, dan kambing.
claims.quote: Der Dahu wird manchmal als gämsenähnliches Tier beschrieben, manchmal als Mischform von Wieseln, Kaninchen, Eichhörnchen, Vögeln und Ziegen.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the dahu is usually brought up in the countryside as a joke on naive people or city folk unfamiliar with mountain wildlife.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, keberadaan dahu biasanya disebut di pedesaan sebagai lelucon kepada orang yang lugu atau orang kota yang tidak mengenal satwa pegunungan.
claims.quote: L'existence du dahu est généralement évoquée en milieu rural et par plaisanterie auprès de personnes particulièrement naïves et de citadins peu au fait, par exemple, de la faune montagnarde

claims.statement: The amphiptere (also amphithere, amphitere or phipthere, 'two-winged') is a kind of winged serpent found in European heraldry.
claims.statement_id: Amphiptere (juga Amphithere, Amphitere, atau Phipthere, "bersayap dua") adalah sejenis ular bersayap dalam heraldik Eropa.
claims.quote: Amphiptere (also called Amphithere, Amphitere, or Phipthere; meaning bi-winged, two-winged) is a type of winged serpent found in European heraldry.

claims.statement: Amphipteres were generally said to have light feathers like a sunrise, a serpentine lindworm-like body, bat-like wings mostly feathered and often greenish, and a long wyvern-like tail.
claims.statement_id: Amphiptere umumnya digambarkan berbulu terang seperti matahari terbit, bertubuh ular mirip lindworm, bersayap kelelawar yang sebagian besar berbulu dan sering kehijauan, serta berekor panjang seperti wyvern.
claims.quote: Amphipteres generally were said to have light-colored feathers like a sunrise, a serpentine body similar to a lindworm, bat-like wings with feathers covering most of the forearm and often greenish in coloration, and a long tail much like a wyvern's tail.

claims.statement: Amphipteres were seldom used in heraldry; they appear on the arms of the House of Potier and as supporters of the Duke of Tresmes and Duke of Gesvres.
claims.statement_id: Amphiptere jarang dipakai dalam lambang; ia ada pada lambang Wangsa Potier dan sebagai penyangga lambang Duke of Tresmes dan Duke of Gesvres.
claims.quote: Amphipteres saw infrequent use as heraldic devices. Amphipteres are present on the arms of the House of Potier, which depict a bendlet purpure between two amphipteres. The Potier heraldry also uses amphipteres as supporters, as do those of the Duke of Tresmes and Duke of Gesvres.

claims.statement: According to the German article, in heraldry the amphitere is a snake with bird wings, later also shown with bat wings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, dalam heraldik amphitere adalah ular bersayap burung yang kemudian juga digambarkan bersayap kelelawar.
claims.quote: In der Heraldik ist die Amphitere eine Schlange mit Vogelflügeln. Später wird sie auch mit Fledermausflügeln dargestellt.

claims.statement: Amphitere legends are also known from Wales and Ireland, where they are often bringers of luck, unlike the destructive lindworms.
claims.statement_id: Legenda amphitere juga dikenal di Wales dan Irlandia, tempat makhluk ini sering dianggap pembawa keberuntungan, berbeda dari lindworm yang merusak.
claims.quote: Legenden von Amphiteren sind auch aus Wales und Irland bekannt. In den Erzählungen gelten die Fabelwesen oft als Glücksbringer, anders als die ähnlichen Lindwürmer, die destruktiv sind.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, the amphiptere is shown as a winged snake like the French guivre (vouivre), and such monsters were often painted on arms to threaten enemies in battle.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, amphiptere digambarkan sebagai ular bersayap mirip guivre (vouivre) Prancis, dan monster semacam ini sering dilukis pada lambang untuk menakuti musuh di medan perang.
claims.quote: アンピプテラは翼の生えた蛇として表現され、フランスのギーヴル（ヴイーヴル）に似ている。アンピテプラやヴイーブルといった怪物は、戦場で敵に脅威を与え威嚇する意味もあって紋章にしばしば描かれていた。

claims.statement: The woods around a castle in Glamorgan had the reputation of being frequented by winged serpents, the terror of old and young alike.
claims.statement_id: Hutan di sekitar sebuah kastel di Glamorgan dikenal sering didatangi ular bersayap, yang menjadi teror bagi tua dan muda.
claims.quote: The woods around Penllyne Castle, Glamorgan, had the repu- tation of being frequented by winged serpents, and these were the terror of old and young alike.

claims.statement: An aged inhabitant of Penllyne said that in his boyhood the winged serpents were described as very beautiful.
claims.statement_id: Seorang penduduk lanjut usia Penllyne mengatakan bahwa pada masa kecilnya ular bersayap itu digambarkan sangat indah.
claims.quote: An aged inhabitant of Penllyne, who died a few years ago, said that in his boyhood the winged serpents were described as very beautiful.

claims.statement: When angry, the winged serpents flew over people's heads with bright outspread wings, sometimes with eyes like the feathers in a peacock's tail.
claims.statement_id: Bila marah, ular bersayap itu terbang di atas kepala orang dengan sayap terkembang yang cemerlang, kadang bermata seperti bulu ekor merak.
claims.quote: flew over people's heads, with outspread wings bright, and sometimes with eyes, too, like the feathers in a peacock's tail.

claims.statement: The speaker's father and uncles had killed some of them because they were "as bad as foxes for poultry".
claims.statement_id: Ayah dan paman penutur telah membunuh beberapa ular bersayap itu karena mereka "seburuk rubah" bagi unggas.
claims.quote: father and uncles had killed some of them, for they were " as bad as foxes for poultry.

claims.statement: An old woman often heard people talking about the ravages of the winged serpents around Penmark Place, Glamorgan.
claims.statement_id: Seorang perempuan tua sering mendengar orang membicarakan kerusakan yang ditimbulkan ular bersayap di sekitar Penmark Place, Glamorgan.
claims.quote: An old woman, whose parents in her early childhood took her to visit Penmark Place, Glamorgan, said she often heard the people talking about the ravages of the winged serpents in that neighbourhood.

claims.statement: In one account men shot a winged serpent, which fell wounded, then rose and attacked the speaker's uncle, beating him with its wings.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, orang-orang menembak seekor ular bersayap yang jatuh terluka, lalu bangkit menyerang paman sang penutur dan memukulinya dengan sayapnya.
claims.quote: Then they shot at it, and the creature fell wounded, only to rise and attack my uncle, beating him about her head with its wings.

claims.statement: A fierce fight ensued between the men and the winged serpent, which was at last killed.
claims.statement_id: Pertarungan sengit terjadi antara para lelaki itu dan ular bersayap tersebut, yang akhirnya terbunuh.
claims.quote: She said a fierce fight ensued between the men and the serpent, which was at last killed.

claims.statement: The old people said that wherever winged serpents were to be seen, buried money or something of value was sure to be near at hand.
claims.statement_id: Orang tua dahulu berkata bahwa di mana pun ular bersayap terlihat, pasti ada uang terpendam atau barang berharga di dekatnya.
claims.quote: wherever winged serpents were to be seen, there ** was sure to be buried money or something of value " near at hand.

claims.statement: The biscione ('big grass snake'), also called vipera, is a heraldic charge of a divine serpent with a child in its mouth, read either as swallowing the child or as the child emerging from its mouth.
claims.statement_id: Biscione ("ular rumput besar"), juga disebut vipera, dalam heraldik adalah gambar ular ilahi dengan seorang anak di mulutnya, yang ditafsirkan sedang menelan anak itu atau anak itu keluar dari mulutnya.
claims.quote: The biscione (English: "big grass snake"), less commonly known also as the vipera, is in heraldry a charge consisting of a divine serpent with a child in its mouth; the serpent may be variously described as being in the act of swallowing the child, or the child may be emerging from its mouth.

claims.statement: It is a historic symbol of Milan, originally on the arms of the Visconti and Sforza dynasties.
claims.statement_id: Ia lambang bersejarah kota Milan, semula pada lambang dinasti Visconti dan Sforza.
claims.quote: It is a historic symbol of the city of Milan, originally on the coat-of-arms of the Visconti and Sforza dynasties.

claims.statement: Biscione is the augmentative of Italian biscia, 'grass snake', from bistia and ultimately Latin bestia, 'beast'.
claims.statement_id: Kata biscione adalah bentuk pembesar dari biscia, "ular rumput", dari bistia dan akhirnya bahasa Latin bestia, "binatang buas".
claims.quote: Etymologically, word biscione is a masculine augmentative of Italian feminine biscia "grass snake" (corrupted from bistia, ultimately from Latin bestia "beast").

claims.statement: The symbol may derive from a bronze serpent brought to Milan from Constantinople by Arnolf II of Arsago (Archbishop of Milan 998–1018) in the 11th century.
claims.statement_id: Lambang ini mungkin berasal dari ular perunggu yang dibawa ke Milan dari Konstantinopel oleh Arnolf II dari Arsago (Uskup Agung Milan 998–1018) pada abad ke-11.
claims.quote: The symbol may have been derived from a bronzed serpent brought to Milan from Constantinople by Arnolf II of Arsago (Archbishop of Milan 998–1018) in the 11th century.

claims.statement: One of the oldest depictions of the biscione is in the Great Hall of the Visconti Castle at Angera, frescoed in the late 13th century to celebrate Archbishop Ottone Visconti's victory over the Della Torre.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu gambaran tertua biscione ada di Aula Besar Kastel Visconti di Angera, yang dilukis fresko pada akhir abad ke-13 untuk merayakan kemenangan Uskup Agung Ottone Visconti atas keluarga Della Torre.
claims.quote: One of the oldest depictions of the Biscione is in the Great Hall of the Visconti Castle of Angera. The hall was painted at the end of the 13th century with frescoes celebrating Archbishop Ottone Visconti's victory against the rival family of the Della Torre.

claims.statement: The logo of the car maker Alfa Romeo, founded in Milan in 1910 and nicknamed the Casa del Biscione, shows the flag of Milan and the biscione.
claims.statement_id: Logo produsen mobil Alfa Romeo, yang didirikan di Milan pada 1910 dan dijuluki Casa del Biscione, memuat bendera Milan dan biscione.
claims.quote: The logo of automobile manufacturer Alfa Romeo (also known as the Casa del Biscione, Italian for "House of the Biscione" or "Biscione['s] marque"), established in Milan in 1910, features the flag of Milan and the biscione as the city's symbol.

claims.statement: According to the German article, besides many Italian towns the biscione appears in the arms of Dachau, Pružany, Dłutów and Sanok.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, selain di banyak kota Italia biscione juga ada pada lambang kota Dachau, Pružany, Dłutów, dan Sanok.
claims.quote: Neben zahlreichen italienischen Gemeinden findet sich der Biscione auch in den Stadtwappen von Dachau, Pružany, Dłutów und Sanok.

claims.statement: By a tradition recorded by Galvano Fiamma, Ottone Visconti won the viper emblem by defeating in a duel a Saracen who bore it, devouring a man, on shield and helm.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi yang dicatat Galvano Fiamma, Ottone Visconti merebut lambang ular ini setelah mengalahkan seorang Saracen dalam duel, yang membawa gambar ular melahap manusia di perisai dan helmnya.
claims.quote: Según una tradición recogida por Galvano Fiamma, Ottone Visconti habría conquistado la insignia de la víbora tras vencer en duelo a un sarraceno que la llevaba como arma, representada devorando a un hombre tanto en el escudo como sobre el yelmo.

claims.statement: In the Boniface legend, while he was away on crusade against the Muslims, a "serpent of marvellous size" terrorised Lombardy and killed his son.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Boniface, saat ia pergi perang salib melawan kaum Muslim, seekor "ular berukuran luar biasa" meneror Lombardia dan membunuh putranya.
claims.quote: Dans ses Mémoires datant de la fin du XVe siècle, Olivier de La Marche décrit l'aventure de Boniface, comte de Pavie marié à l'héritière de Milan. Alors qu'il était parti en croisade contre les Musulmans, un « serpent de merveilleuse grandeur » terrorisa la Lombardie et tua son fils.

claims.statement: Boniface returned and found the beast carrying a child in its jaws; after a fierce fight in which the serpent's severed head rejoined itself, the knight finally killed it.
claims.statement_id: Boniface kembali dan menemukan makhluk itu membawa seorang anak di rahangnya; setelah pertarungan sengit, ketika kepala ular yang dipenggal menyambung kembali, sang ksatria akhirnya membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Une fois revenu, Boniface retrouva cette « beste » qui emportait alors un enfant dans sa gueule. Après un combat acharné au cours duquel la tête du serpent se renouait une fois coupée, le chevalier finit par tuer l'animal.

claims.statement: In this legend, the knight's children took the emblem of a serpent with a child in its mouth in memory of the fight.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda itu, anak-anak sang ksatria mengambil lambang ular dengan seorang anak di mulutnya untuk mengenang pertarungan tersebut.
claims.quote: C'est en la mémoire de ce combat que ses enfants prirent l'emblème d'un serpent avec un enfant dans sa gueule.

claims.statement: In another legend, Othon, viscount of Milan, fought at the siege of Jerusalem a formidable Saracen giant named Volux, who wore on his helmet a crest of a serpent devouring a child to frighten his enemies.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda lain, Othon, vicomte de Milan, saat pengepungan Jerusalem melawan seorang Saracen raksasa bernama Volux yang memakai di helmnya lambang ular pemakan anak untuk menakuti musuh.
claims.quote: Othon, vicomte de Milan, aurait, pendant le siège de Jérusalem, combattu un redoutable Sarrasin, un géant nommé Volux. Ce dernier portait sur son casque un cimier représentant un serpent dévorant un enfant, afin d'effrayer ses ennemis.

claims.statement: In a third tale, the knight Azo, tired of war, took off his helmet to lie down; while he slept a serpent slid inside, and when he put it back on unawares the serpent fell down along his cheek without trying to bite him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah ketiga, ksatria Azo yang lelah berperang melepas helmnya untuk berbaring; saat ia tidur seekor ular masuk ke helm itu, dan ketika ia memakainya tanpa sadar ular itu merosot di pipinya tanpa menggigit.
claims.quote: Un jour, le chevalier Azo, fatigué de la guerre, voulant se reposer, ôta son casque pour s'allonger sur le sol. Mais alors qu'il dort, un serpent se glisse à l'intérieur. Sans se rendre compte de la présence de l'animal, il remet son casque sur sa tête et le serpent retombe le long de sa joue sans chercher à le mordre.

claims.statement: The exhibition author concludes the serpent of Milan was shown as a real animal, an imaginary animal or an emblematic animal, and in all three cases its negative and dangerous aspect remains present.
claims.statement_id: Penulis pameran menyimpulkan bahwa ular Milan digambarkan sebagai hewan nyata, hewan imajiner, atau hewan lambang, dan dalam ketiganya sifatnya yang negatif dan berbahaya tetap hadir.
claims.quote: Le serpent de Milan a donc été représenté de manières différentes, soit en animal réel, en animal imaginaire ou en animal emblématique. Dans les trois cas, son aspect négatif et dangereux reste toujours présent.

claims.statement: Tarantasio, the dragon of Lake Gerundo, was believed to devour children, destroy boats and foul the air with its pestilential breath, causing a strange disease called yellow fever.
claims.statement_id: Tarantasio, naga danau Gerundo, dipercaya memakan anak-anak, menghancurkan perahu, dan meracuni udara dengan napasnya yang mewabah sehingga menimbulkan penyakit yang disebut demam kuning.
claims.quote: Tarantasio è il nome di un drago leggendario che terrorizzava gli abitanti dell'antico e ipotetico lago Gerundo (poi prosciugato, secondo la leggenda), nella zona di Lodi, in Lombardia. Si riteneva che questo animale mitologico divorasse i bambini, distruggesse le imbarcazioni e ammorbasse l'aria con il suo fiato pestilenziale, causando una strana malattia denominata febbre gialla.

claims.statement: Tarantasio is a legendary dragon that terrorised the inhabitants of the ancient, hypothetical Lake Gerundo in the Lodi area of Lombardy.
claims.statement_id: Tarantasio adalah naga legendaris yang meneror penduduk danau Gerundo kuno di daerah Lodi, Lombardia.
claims.quote: Tarantasio è il nome di un drago leggendario che terrorizzava gli abitanti dell'antico e ipotetico lago Gerundo (poi prosciugato, secondo la leggenda), nella zona di Lodi, in Lombardia.

claims.statement: One tradition has the founder of the Visconti slay the dragon and adopt the defeated creature, the biscione with a child in its mouth, as his emblem.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu tradisi menyebut leluhur Visconti membunuh sang naga lalu memakai makhluk yang dikalahkan itu, biscione dengan anak di mulutnya, sebagai lambang.
claims.quote: La più suggestiva riguarda l'uccisione del drago da parte del capostipite dei Visconti, il quale avrebbe poi adottato come simbolo la creatura sconfitta, ovvero il biscione con il bambino in bocca.

claims.statement: The sea monk was a sea creature found off the east coast of the Danish island of Zealand in 1546, described as a 'fish' outwardly like a monk in his habit.
claims.statement_id: Biarawan laut adalah makhluk laut yang ditemukan di lepas pantai timur pulau Zealand, Denmark, pada 1546, digambarkan sebagai "ikan" yang dari luar mirip biarawan berjubah.
claims.quote: The sea monk (also monk-fish or monkfish) was a sea creature found off the eastern coast of the Danish island of Zealand in 1546. It was described as a "fish" that outwardly resembled a human monk in his habit.

claims.statement: Belon (1553) called it piscis monachus, 'monk fish', and Rondelet (1554) piscis monachi habitu, 'fish in a monk's habit'.
claims.statement_id: Belon (1553) menyebutnya piscis monachus, "ikan biarawan", dan Rondelet (1554) piscis monachi habitu, "ikan berjubah biarawan".
claims.quote: The creature was called "monk fish" (Latin: piscis monachus) by Belon (1553), and piscis monachi habitu ("fish [wearing] the habit of a monk") by Rondelet (1554).

claims.statement: Christian III of Denmark sent a picture of it to Emperor Charles V, and Vedel's Den danske Krønicke (1575) records it as 4 ells (4.6 m) long.
claims.statement_id: Christian III dari Denmark mengirim gambarnya kepada Kaisar Charles V, dan Den danske Krønicke karya Vedel (1575) mencatat panjangnya 4 ell (4,6 m).
claims.quote: Christian III of Denmark sent an illustration of it to Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor. The creature is recorded in Vedel's Den danske Krønicke (1575) as measuring 4 ells long (15 ft; 4.6 m).

claims.statement: Rondelet classed it as a merman (homo maris) but doubted that the pictures he received could be taken at face value.
claims.statement_id: Rondelet menggolongkannya sebagai manusia laut (homo maris), tetapi meragukan bahwa gambar yang ia terima bisa dipercaya begitu saja.
claims.quote: Rondelet (1554) called it "the fish with the habit of a monk (piscis monachi habitu), and classed it as a merman (homo maris). But he did not think the pictorial representations he obtained could be taken at face value

claims.statement: According to the German article, the sea monk was first mentioned around 1200 by Alexander Neckam, and later sightings were recorded, including a specimen sent to the King of Denmark around 1550.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, biarawan laut pertama disebut sekitar 1200 oleh Alexander Neckam, dan berbagai penampakan kemudian dicatat, termasuk spesimen yang dikirim kepada Raja Denmark sekitar 1550.
claims.quote: Erstmals erwähnt wird er um 1200 bei Alexander Neckam. In der Folge wurden verschiedene Sichtungen des Meermönches dokumentiert, unter anderem soll um 1550 ein Exemplar dem König von Dänemark zugeschickt worden sein.

claims.statement: Japetus Steenstrup in 1855 read it as a squid, while newer readings suggest anglerfish, angelsharks or seals.
claims.statement_id: Japetus Steenstrup pada 1855 menafsirkannya sebagai cumi-cumi, sedangkan tafsiran baru mengusulkan ikan sungut ganda, hiu malaikat, atau anjing laut.
claims.quote: Japetus Steenstrup interpretierte ihn 1855 als Tintenfisch, neuere Deutungen gehen zum Beispiel von Seeteufeln, Meerengeln oder Robben aus.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, Gesner also cited a similar monster in the Firth of Forth from the Scottish historian Hector Boece, and a sighting off Poland in 1531.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, Gesner juga menyebut monster serupa di Firth of Forth menurut sejarawan Skotlandia Hector Boece, serta penampakan di pantai Polandia pada 1531.
claims.quote: Éste también hizo referencia a un monstruo similar encontrado en el Fiordo de Forth, citando al historiador escocés Hector Boece, y a un avistamiento en la costa de Polonia en 1531.

claims.statement: The xana is a figure of Asturian mythology, always female and extraordinarily beautiful, believed to live in springs, rivers, waterfalls or forests with pure water.
claims.statement_id: Xana adalah tokoh mitologi Asturias, selalu perempuan dan luar biasa cantik, yang dipercaya tinggal di mata air, sungai, air terjun, atau hutan berair jernih.
claims.quote: The xana (Asturian: /ˈʃana/or [ˈɕa.na]) is a character found in Asturian mythology. Always female, she is a creature of extraordinary beauty believed to live in fountains, rivers, waterfalls, or forested regions with pure water.

claims.statement: The origin of xana is unclear, though some scholars derive it from the Latin name of the goddess Diana, and the xanas' homes are still common in Asturian place names.
claims.statement_id: Asal kata xana tidak jelas, tetapi sebagian sarjana menganggapnya turunan nama Latin dewi Diana, dan tempat tinggal xana masih banyak terekam dalam nama tempat di Asturias.
claims.quote: The origin of the Asturian word xana is unclear, though some scholars see it as a derivation from the Latin name for the goddess Diana. References to where the mythological xanas lived are still common in Asturian toponyms.

claims.statement: Xanas promise treasure and can be disenchanted; some also attack people and steal food, and they live in springs and caves.
claims.statement_id: Xana menjanjikan harta dan dapat dibebaskan dari sihir, sebagian juga menyerang orang dan mencuri makanan, dan mereka tinggal di mata air dan gua.
claims.quote: The xanas promise treasures and can be disenchanted. Some xanas also attack people and steal their food. They live in fountains and caves.

claims.statement: A xana can be kindly, offering 'love water' to travellers and gold or silver to those judged worthy, and her hypnotic voice is heard on spring and summer nights.
claims.statement_id: Xana dapat menjadi roh baik yang memberi "air cinta" kepada pelancong dan emas atau perak kepada yang dianggap layak, dan suaranya yang memukau terdengar pada malam musim semi dan musim panas.
claims.quote: A xana can be a beneficial spirit, offering "love water" to travellers and rewards of gold or silver to those found worthy through some undefined judgment. Their hypnotic voices can be heard during spring and summer nights.

claims.statement: The pure of soul who hear her song are filled with peace and love, while the impure feel smothered and may go mad.
claims.statement_id: Orang berjiwa murni yang mendengar nyanyiannya dipenuhi damai dan cinta, sedangkan yang tidak murni merasa tercekik dan bisa menjadi gila.
claims.quote: Those who have a pure soul and hear the song will be filled with a sense of peace and love. Those whose souls are not pure will feel they are being suffocated and may be driven insane.

claims.statement: Xanas have children called xaninos, but since they cannot make milk they usually swap a human baby in its cradle for their own fairy child, like changelings elsewhere.
claims.statement_id: Xana memiliki anak bernama xaninos, tetapi karena tidak dapat menyusui, mereka biasanya menukar bayi manusia di buaian dengan anak peri mereka, mirip changeling di budaya lain.
claims.quote: Xanas have children called xaninos (singular: xanín), but because they cannot take care of them—xanas cannot produce milk to feed their babies—they usually take a human baby from his cradle and put their own fairy child in instead, similar to changelings in other cultures.

claims.statement: According to the German article, the xana appears as a beautiful young woman who leaves her mountain cave in the morning to bathe in her ice-cold spring, and by oral tradition of the Picos de Europa wishes she hears then come true.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, xana tampak sebagai perempuan muda cantik yang pagi-pagi keluar dari gua gunung untuk mandi di mata airnya yang dingin, dan menurut tradisi lisan Picos de Europa keinginan yang ia dengar saat itu akan terkabul.
claims.quote: Die Xana erscheint als schöne junge Frau, die morgens aus einer Gebirgshöhle kommend zu ihrer Quelle wandert, um sich im eiskalten Wasser zu baden. Nach mündlicher Überlieferung aus den Picos de Europa gehen Wünsche, die in diesen Moment an ihr Ohr dringen, in Erfüllung.

claims.statement: A changeling betrays itself only when eggshells are stacked by the hearth, for it cries in surprise, 'I was born a hundred years ago, but I have never seen so many eggshells by the fire!'
claims.statement_id: Anak tukaran hanya ketahuan bila kulit telur ditumpuk di dekat perapian, karena ia akan berseru heran, "Seratus tahun lalu aku lahir, tetapi belum pernah melihat kulit telur sebanyak ini di dekat api!"
claims.quote: Nur durch das Stapeln von Eierschalen neben dem Herdfeuer verraten sich die ausgetauschten Wechselbälger selbst, weil sie dann überrascht rufen: „Vor hundert Jahren wurde ich geboren, aber so viele Eierschalen beim Feuer habe ich noch nie gesehen!“.

claims.statement: According to the French article, they appear as very beautiful young girls, blonde and light-eyed, combing their hair with golden combs on riverbanks while waiting to seduce travellers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, mereka tampak sebagai gadis muda yang sangat cantik, pirang dan bermata terang, yang menyisir rambut dengan sisir emas di tepi sungai sambil menunggu pelancong untuk dirayu.
claims.quote: Elles se présentent comme des filles jeunes et très belles, de caractère plutôt nordique, c'est-à-dire blondes et aux yeux clairs. Elles se peignent sur les rives des rivières avec des peignes d'or, attendant des voyageurs pour les séduire.

claims.statement: Adamastor is a mythological character created by the Portuguese poet Luís de Camões in his epic Os Lusíadas (first printed 1572) as a personification of the Cape of Good Hope.
claims.statement_id: Adamastor adalah tokoh mitologis ciptaan penyair Portugal Luís de Camões dalam epos Os Lusíadas (pertama dicetak 1572) sebagai personifikasi Tanjung Harapan.
claims.quote: Adamastor is a mythological character created by the Portuguese poet Luís de Camões in his epic poem Os Lusíadas (first printed in 1572), as a personification of the Cape of Good Hope

claims.statement: He symbolises the dangers of the sea and the forces of nature challenged and finally overcome by the Portuguese in the Age of Discovery, and he appears out of a storm.
claims.statement_id: Ia melambangkan bahaya laut dan kekuatan alam yang ditantang dan akhirnya diatasi bangsa Portugal pada Zaman Penjelajahan, dan ia muncul dari badai.
claims.quote: symbolizing the dangers of the sea and the formidable forces of nature challenged and ultimately overcome by the Portuguese during the Age of Discovery. Adamastor manifests itself out of a storm.

claims.statement: Camões made him one of the Giants of Greek mythology, banished to the Cape of Good Hope by the sea goddess Doris for falling in love with her daughter Tethis.
claims.statement_id: Camões menjadikannya salah satu Raksasa mitologi Yunani yang dibuang ke Tanjung Harapan oleh dewi laut Doris karena jatuh cinta pada putrinya, Tethis.
claims.quote: Camões gave his creation a backstory as one of the Giants of Greek mythology, banished to the Cape of Good Hope by sea goddess Doris for falling in love with her daughter Tethis

claims.statement: Vasco da Gama, leading the Portuguese expedition, confronts the creature by asking 'Who are you?', and Adamastor tells his story.
claims.statement_id: Vasco da Gama, pemimpin ekspedisi Portugal, menghadapi makhluk itu dengan bertanya "Siapa kau?", sehingga Adamastor menceritakan kisahnya.
claims.quote: Vasco da Gama, ahead of the Portuguese expedition, confronts the creature by asking "Who are you?", prompting Adamastor to tell his story.

claims.statement: Deeply moved, the giant finally vanishes, scattering the clouds and calming the sea so that the way to India lies open.
claims.statement_id: Karena terharu, raksasa itu akhirnya lenyap, mengusir awan dan menenangkan laut sehingga jalan ke India terbuka.
claims.quote: Deeply moved, the giant eventually vanishes, dispersing the clouds and calming the sea, leaving the path towards India open.

claims.statement: A popular gathering place in Lisbon, officially the Miradouro de Santa Catarina, is known as 'Adamastor' for the large stone statue of the figure there.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah tempat berkumpul populer di Lisboa, yang resminya bernama Miradouro de Santa Catarina, dikenal sebagai "Adamastor" karena patung batu besar tokoh itu di sana.
claims.quote: A popular gathering place in Lisbon is known by the name 'Adamastor' because of the large stone statue of the mythical figure which presides over the space, which is officially called the Miradouro de Santa Catarina.

claims.statement: The Portuguese poet Fernando Pessoa included in Mensagem (1934) verses on Adamastor titled O Mostrengo ('The Hideous Monster').
claims.statement_id: Penyair Portugal Fernando Pessoa memuat dalam bukunya Mensagem (1934) beberapa bait untuk Adamastor berjudul O Mostrengo ("Monster yang Mengerikan").
claims.quote: The Portuguese poet Fernando Pessoa included in his 1934 book Mensagem a number of verses dedicated to Adamastor, entitled O Mostrengo ("The Hideous Monster")

claims.statement: According to the German article, he appeared to Vasco da Gama as a mighty storm cloud guarding the way to the Cape of Good Hope or Cabo das Tormentas (Cape of Storms), beyond which lies the Indian Ocean.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, ia menampakkan diri kepada Vasco da Gama sebagai awan badai raksasa yang menjaga jalan ke Tanjung Harapan atau Cabo das Tormentas (Tanjung Badai), yang di baliknya terbentang Samudra Hindia.
claims.quote: Er sollte sich Vasco da Gama als mächtige Gewitterwolke offenbaren, die den Zugang zum Kap der Guten Hoffnung bzw. Cabo das Tormentas (Kap der Stürme) verteidigt, hinter dem sich der Indische Ozean erstreckt

claims.statement: According to the French article, Adamastor, the giant of the Storms, is the spirit of the Cape of Storms, mentioned by Claudian in his Gigantomachy and then popularised by Camões in Os Lusíadas.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Adamastor atau raksasa Badai adalah roh Tanjung Badai yang sudah disebut Claudianus dalam Gigantomachia-nya, lalu dipopulerkan oleh Camões dalam Os Lusíadas.
claims.quote: Adamastor ou le géant des Tempêtes est l'esprit du Cap des Orages (Cap de Bonne-Espérance), cité par Claudien dans sa Gigantomachie, puis popularisé par Luís de Camões (1524-1580) dans Les Lusiades.

claims.statement: The spirit supposedly appeared to Vasco da Gama and foretold the disasters that beset the voyage to India.
claims.statement_id: Roh itu konon menampakkan diri kepada Vasco da Gama dan meramalkan bencana-bencana yang menimpa pelayaran ke India.
claims.quote: L'esprit est censément apparu à Vasco de Gama et avait prédit les désastres qui émaillèrent le voyage vers l'Inde.

claims.statement: Victor Hugo mentions him in Les Misérables when describing the street urchin of Paris.
claims.statement_id: Victor Hugo menyebutnya dalam Les Misérables ketika menggambarkan anak jalanan Paris.
claims.quote: Victor Hugo le cite dans Les Misérables, livre III, dans sa description du gamin de Paris

claims.statement: The Beast of Bray Road is the name given to a wolf-like creature reportedly seen in or near Elkhorn, Walworth County, Wisconsin.
claims.statement_id: Beast of Bray Road adalah nama untuk makhluk mirip serigala yang dilaporkan terlihat di sekitar Elkhorn, Walworth County, Wisconsin.
claims.quote: The Beast of Bray Road is the name given to a wolf-like creature reported to have been witnessed in or near Elkhorn, Walworth County, Wisconsin.

claims.statement: Named after the farm road where it was first supposedly seen, reports in the 1980s and 1990s led the local paper Walworth County Week to assign reporter Linda Godfrey to the story.
claims.statement_id: Dinamai menurut jalan pertanian tempat ia konon pertama terlihat, laporan tentangnya pada 1980-an dan 1990-an membuat koran lokal Walworth County Week menugaskan wartawan Linda Godfrey meliputnya.
claims.quote: Named for the rural farm road on which it was first purportedly sighted, reports of the creature in the 1980s and 1990s prompted a local newspaper, the Walworth County Week, to assign reporter Linda Godfrey to cover the story.

claims.statement: Skeptics hold that it is probably a misidentification of known animals, most likely gray wolves.
claims.statement_id: Kaum skeptis berpendapat makhluk ini kemungkinan hasil salah kenal terhadap hewan biasa, paling mungkin serigala abu-abu.
claims.quote: Skeptics maintain that the creature is likely the result of misidentification of known animals, most likely gray wolves.

claims.statement: Witnesses often describe it as 1.8–2.1 m tall, humanlike in body and furred, with a wolf's head and large glowing red or orange eyes.
claims.statement_id: Para saksi sering menggambarkannya setinggi 1,8–2,1 m, bertubuh mirip manusia dan berbulu, berkepala serigala, dengan mata besar merah atau jingga yang menyala.
claims.quote: The Beast of Bray Road is often described by alleged witnesses as being between 6 feet (1.8 m) and 7 feet (2.1 m) tall, with a humanoid style body, covered in fur or hair, and with a head resembling a wolf and large, glowing red or orange eyes.

claims.statement: It is said to move on four legs and on two, and some reports liken it more to a traditional werewolf or Bigfoot.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon terlihat berjalan dengan empat kaki maupun dua kaki, dan sebagian laporan menggambarkannya lebih mirip manusia serigala tradisional atau Bigfoot.
claims.quote: It is purported to have been seen moving as both a quadruped and a biped, and some reports describe it more closely to resembling a traditional werewolf or Bigfoot.

claims.statement: It was supposedly first seen on two nights running in 1936 on the grounds of St. Coletta School in Jefferson, where a night watchman saw it digging at an Indian burial mound.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini konon pertama terlihat dua malam berturut-turut pada 1936 di halaman St. Coletta School di Jefferson, ketika seorang penjaga malam melihatnya menggali gundukan kubur Indian di sana.
claims.quote: The creature was allegedly first sighted on two consecutive nights in 1936 on the grounds of St. Coletta School for Exceptional Children in rural Jefferson, where a night watchman witnessed it digging on an Indian burial mound located on the property.

claims.statement: One witness claimed that after hitting something on Bray Road and getting out to look, a large red-eyed wolf-like creature chased her back to the car, leaving claw marks on the rear door.
claims.statement_id: Seorang saksi mengaku setelah menabrak sesuatu di Bray Road dan keluar memeriksa, makhluk besar mirip serigala bermata merah mengejarnya kembali ke mobil dan meninggalkan bekas cakar di pintu belakang.
claims.quote: The witness claimed that, upon exiting her vehicle to determine what she had hit, a large wolf-like creature with red eyes chased her back into her car, leaving claw marks in the rear passenger door.

claims.statement: Others suggest it may be an American black bear with mange.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula yang menduga makhluk itu beruang hitam Amerika yang terserang kudis.
claims.quote: Others have theorized that the creature may be an American black bear suffering from mange.

claims.statement: It was the main antagonist of the 2005 horror film The Beast of Bray Road from The Asylum.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini menjadi tokoh antagonis utama dalam film horor The Beast of Bray Road (2005) produksi The Asylum.
claims.quote: The creature was featured as the primary antagonist in the 2005 film The Beast of Bray Road, a horror film produced and distributed by The Asylum.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the name has since been applied to any sighting of an unknown creature from southern Wisconsin to northern Illinois.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, nama itu kemudian dipakai untuk setiap penampakan makhluk tak dikenal dari selatan Wisconsin sampai utara Illinois.
claims.quote: La même dénomination a été, depuis lors, appliquée à toute vision de créature inconnue, du sud du Wisconsin au nord de l'Illinois et aux routes menant à l'île de Vancouver en Colombie-Britannique.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, it is a supposed pseudo-cryptid whose first reported sighting dates only to the 1980s.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, ia makhluk pseudo-kriptid yang laporan penampakan pertamanya baru muncul pada 1980-an.
claims.quote: La Bestia de Bray Road es una supuesta criatura pseudocriptida. El primer reporte de su supuesta primera aparición es reciente y fue en los años 1980

claims.statement: Cuélebre (Asturian) or Culebre (Cantabrian) is a legendary creature of northern Spain, a giant winged serpent-dragon that lives in caves, guards treasure and often holds anjanas or xanas captive.
claims.statement_id: Cuélebre (Asturias) atau Culebre (Cantabria) adalah makhluk legenda Spanyol utara berupa naga-ular raksasa bersayap yang tinggal di gua, menjaga harta, dan sering menawan anjana atau xana.
claims.quote: Cuélebre (Asturian) or Culebre (Cantabrian) is a legendary creature in the mythology of Asturias and Cantabria in northern Spain. It is depicted as a giant, winged serpent-dragon that inhabits caves and guards treasures, often keeping anjanas (fairy-like beings, also known as xanas) captive.

claims.statement: Over time they age, their scales grow impenetrable and bat-like wings grow; though immortal, they finally leave their homeland and fly to a mythical paradise, Mar Cuajada, beyond the sea.
claims.statement_id: Seiring waktu mereka menua, sisiknya menjadi tak tertembus, dan tumbuh sayap mirip kelelawar; meski abadi, akhirnya mereka meninggalkan tanah asalnya dan terbang ke surga mitis Mar Cuajada di seberang laut.
claims.quote: Over time, these creatures age, their scales become impenetrable, and bat-like wings grow on their bodies. Although immortal, they eventually leave their homeland and fly to a mythical paradise called Mar Cuajada, located beyond the sea.

claims.statement: They seldom move except to eat cattle and people, and can be killed by feeding them a red-hot stone or a loaf filled with pins.
claims.statement_id: Mereka jarang bergerak kecuali untuk memakan ternak dan manusia, dan dapat dibunuh dengan diberi makan batu membara atau roti berisi jarum.
claims.quote: They do not usually move, but when they do, it is in order to eat cattle and people. To defeat the creature, one may feed it a red-hot stone or a loaf of bread filled with pins, which would cause its death.

claims.statement: Its spit is believed to turn into a magic stone that heals many diseases.
claims.statement_id: Ludahnya dipercaya berubah menjadi batu ajaib yang dapat menyembuhkan berbagai penyakit.
claims.quote: Its spit is believed to turn into a magical stone with the power to heal various diseases.

claims.statement: In Asturian and Cantabrian folklore, on Midsummer night (San Juan) its spells fail so the brave can challenge it, and whoever defeats it may marry the xana and take its treasure.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Asturias dan Cantabria, pada malam San Juan sihir cuélebre kehilangan kekuatan sehingga orang pemberani dapat menantangnya, dan yang mengalahkannya boleh menikahi xana dan mengambil hartanya.
claims.quote: According to Asturian and Cantabrian folklore, Midsummer (the night of San Juan) is a magical time when brave individuals can challenge the cuélebre, as its spells lose their power. Defeating it on this night allows one to marry the xana and claim its treasure.

claims.statement: But in Cantabrian lore, on Saint Bartholomew's Night the cuélebre grows stronger and vents its wrath on humans.
claims.statement_id: Namun dalam cerita Cantabria, pada malam Santo Bartolomeus cuélebre justru makin kuat dan melampiaskan amarahnya kepada manusia.
claims.quote: However, in Cantabrian lore, Saint Bartholomew's Night is said to be when the cuélebre becomes even more powerful, unleashing its wrath in vengeance against humans.

claims.statement: The German article also calls the cuélebre a giant winged snake-like dragon of Asturian and Cantabrian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Jerman juga menyebut cuélebre naga raksasa bersayap mirip ular dari mitologi Asturias dan Cantabria.
claims.quote: Der Cuélebre (asturisch: Cuélebre, kantabrisch: Culebre) ist ein riesiger, geflügelter, schlangenähnlicher Drache aus der asturischen und kantabrischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: According to the German article, their lamed wings gradually grow into the body, and they mostly lie motionless except to eat cattle or people.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, sayap mereka yang lumpuh lama-lama menyatu ke dalam tubuh, dan mereka kebanyakan berbaring diam kecuali untuk memakan ternak atau manusia.
claims.quote: Ihre erlahmten Flügel wachsen mit der Zeit in den Körper. Meistens liegen sie regungslos herum und bewegen sich nur, um Rinder oder Menschen zu fressen.

claims.statement: According to the Japanese article, the dragon lives mainly in forests, underground caves and springs, its scales so hard that even bullets bounce off, with wings it can fly with.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jepang, naga ini terutama tinggal di hutan, gua bawah tanah, dan mata air, bersisik sekeras sehingga peluru pun terpental, dan bersayap yang dapat terbang.
claims.quote: この竜は主に森や地下洞窟や源泉に住んでいるという。その体は、弾丸すらはじき飛ばすほど堅い鱗に覆われ、飛ぶことのできる羽を持つ。

claims.statement: For the cuélebre of the Brañaseca cave in Cudillero, villagers reportedly fed it corn or rye bread so it would not eat their livestock.
claims.statement_id: Untuk cuélebre di gua Brañaseca, Cudillero, penduduk desa konon memberi roti jagung atau gandum hitam agar ternak mereka tidak dimakan.
claims.quote: アストゥリアス州クディリェーロ ... ブラーニャセカ洞窟 (Brañaseca) のクエレブレには、家畜を食べられないように村人がとうもろこしやライ麦のパンを与えていたという。

claims.statement: Not every cuélebre is fierce; some are said to look after the xana, the blonde water fairy.
claims.statement_id: Tidak semua cuélebre ganas; ada yang konon merawat xana, peri air berambut pirang.
claims.quote: 強暴なクエレブレばかりとは限らない。金髪をもつ水の妖精・シャナの面倒をみている竜もいるという。

claims.statement: The Peluda (Spanish) or La Velue ('The Hairy One', originally French) is a mythical beast that terrorised the River Huisne area of France in the Middle Ages.
claims.statement_id: Peluda dalam bahasa Spanyol, atau La Velue ("Yang Berbulu") dalam bahasa Prancis aslinya, adalah binatang mitis yang meneror sekitar Sungai Huisne, Prancis, pada Abad Pertengahan.
claims.quote: The Peluda in Spanish, or La Velue ('The Hairy One') originally in French, is a mythical beast that terrorized the environs of the River Huisne, France, during the Middle Ages.

claims.statement: This serpent-headed creature had a body of long green fur with poison-tipped spines; it caused floods (or spat fire) that ruined crops, ate livestock and people, and killed with its tail.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk berkepala ular ini bertubuh tertutup bulu hijau panjang dengan duri berujung racun; ia menimbulkan banjir (atau menyemburkan api) yang merusak panen, memakan ternak dan manusia, dan membunuh dengan ekornya.
claims.quote: The supposed serpent-headed creature had a body covered in long green fur with poison-tipped spines protruding. It caused floods (or shot out fire from its mouth) that destroyed crops, devoured livestock and humans, and struck humans and animals dead with its tail.

claims.statement: It was defeated after trying to prey on a maiden named l'Agnelle; her fiancé killed it with a sword-stroke to the tail, its only weak spot.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikalahkan setelah mencoba memangsa gadis bernama l'Agnelle; tunangannya membunuhnya dengan menebas ekornya, satu-satunya titik lemahnya.
claims.quote: It was defeated after it tried to prey upon a maiden named l'Agnelle; her fiancé slew it by delivering a sword-strike to the tail, its only weak spot.

claims.statement: The velue, French for 'shaggy one', was introduced as 'la Peluda' in Spanish in Jorge Luis Borges's Book of Imaginary Beings (1957).
claims.statement_id: Velue, "yang berbulu" dalam bahasa Prancis, diperkenalkan sebagai "la Peluda" dalam bahasa Spanyol dalam Buku Makhluk Khayalan karya Jorge Luis Borges (1957).
claims.quote: The velue  (French, meaning ‘shaggy/hairy one’) was introduced as "la Peluda", in Spanish, in Jorge Luis Borges's Book of Imaginary Beings (1957)

claims.statement: A pamphlet on 'La Velue' was printed in 1889 for the Sarthe area, its text also describing the beast.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah pamflet tentang "La Velue" dicetak pada 1889 untuk daerah Sarthe, dan teksnya juga memuat gambaran fisik binatang itu.
claims.quote: A pamphlet of "La Velue" was printed in 1889 for the Sarthe area, and its text also gave a physical description of the mythical beast in similar language.

claims.statement: French sources say the beast was serpent-headed and serpent-tailed, ox-sized, with an egg-shaped body covered in 'long green fur'.
claims.statement_id: Sumber Prancis menyebut binatang ini berkepala dan berekor ular, sebesar lembu, dengan tubuh bulat telur yang tertutup "bulu hijau panjang".
claims.quote: The French sources tell that the beast was serpent-headed and serpent-tailed, ox-sized with an egg-shaped body covered in "long green fur"

claims.statement: Cordonnier-Détrie held that the beast belonged to the same family as the Tarasque of Tarascon and Beaucaire.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cordonnier-Détrie, binatang ini sekeluarga dengan Tarasque dari Tarascon dan Beaucaire.
