claims.quote: It was the opinion of Cordonnier-Détrie that the beast belonged to the same family as the mythical Tarasque of Tarascon and Beaucaire.

claims.statement: According to the lore, the beast was refused a place on Noah's Ark yet survived the Flood.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita, binatang ini tidak diterima di Bahtera Nuh tetapi tetap selamat dari Air Bah.
claims.quote: According to the lore, the beast was excluded from Noah's Ark, yet survived the Deluge, i.e., the Biblical Flood.

claims.statement: By popular tradition it died at the bridge of Yvré-l'Évêque; the victory was long celebrated at La Ferté-Bernard and Connerré, and its body was reportedly stuffed.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi, ia mati di jembatan Yvré-l'Évêque; kemenangan itu lama dirayakan di La Ferté-Bernard dan Connerré, dan konon bangkainya diawetkan.
claims.quote: According to popular tradition, it died at the bridge of Yvré-l'Évêque. The victory was long celebrated afterwards at La Ferté-Bernard and Connerré, and the people stuffed (or embalmed) the body of the beast, so it has been told.

claims.statement: At Tuffé a velue fountain was installed in 2007 in the square facing the Church of Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul.
claims.statement_id: Di Tuffé, sebuah air mancur berbentuk velue dipasang pada 2007 di alun-alun depan Gereja Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul.
claims.quote: Also at Tuffé, a velue fountain has been installed in 2007, on the open square facing the Église Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul.

claims.statement: The Indonesian article says its name comes from Occitan for 'hairy', its body is like a porcupine's, and it is ox-sized.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Indonesia menyebut namanya berasal dari bahasa Occitan yang berarti "berambut", tubuhnya seperti landak, dan besarnya seperti lembu.
claims.quote: Meskipun makhluk ini merupakan makhluk dalam legenda Prancis, namanya berasal dari bahasa Occitan yang berarti "berambut". Tubuhnya berbentuk seperti landak dan besarnya seperti seekor lembu.

claims.statement: The Japanese article calls the peluda or velue, 'the shaggy one', a monster told of in the Sarthe department of northern France.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Jepang menyebut peluda atau velue, "yang berbulu lebat", sebagai monster yang diceritakan di departemen Sarthe, Prancis utara.
claims.quote: ペルーダ（スペイン語: la Peluda）、ヴリュ（フランス語: la velue、「毛むくじゃら」の意）は、フランス北部サルト県に伝わる怪物。

claims.statement: In Basque mythology Sugaar (also Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) is the male half of a pre-Christian Basque deity of storms and thunder, much like Herensuge but far older.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Basque, Sugaar (juga Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) adalah separuh laki-laki dari dewa Basque pra-Kristen yang berkaitan dengan badai dan guntur, dan ia banyak mirip Herensuge meski jauh lebih tua.
claims.quote: In Basque mythology, Sugaar (also Sugar, Sugoi, Suarra, Maju) is the male half of a pre-Christian Basque deity associated with storms and thunder. He shows may similarities to Herensuge, with Sugaar being much older.

claims.statement: Sugaar sometimes takes the form of pure fire or lightning, but his true form is usually a serpent or dragon; he is Mari's consort and visits her at Anboto every Friday.
claims.statement_id: Sugaar kadang berwujud api murni atau petir, tetapi wujud aslinya biasanya ular atau naga; ia pasangan Mari dan konon mengunjunginya di Anboto setiap Jumat.
claims.quote: Sugaar is sometimes said to take the form of pure fire or lightning, but his true form is usually represented as a serpent or dragon. He is Mari's consort, and is said to visit her at Anboto every Friday.

claims.statement: The visits are also seen as sexual, a figure of the rain (Sugaar) fertilising the earth (Mari).
claims.statement_id: Kunjungan itu juga dianggap bersifat seksual, melambangkan hujan (Sugaar) yang menyuburkan bumi dan tanah (Mari).
claims.quote: The visits are also considered sexual in nature, a reference to how the rain (Sugaar) fertilizes the earth and soil (Mari).

claims.statement: Like Mari he lives in various caves and mountains, one of them the Aralar range.
claims.statement_id: Seperti Mari, Sugaar tinggal di berbagai gua dan gunung, salah satunya Pegunungan Aralar.
claims.quote: Like Mari, Sugar is said to live in various caves and mountains. One of his homes is said to be the Aralar Mountain Range.

claims.statement: In Betelu Sugaar is an evil spirit, and in Ataun a bogeyman.
claims.statement_id: Di Betelu Sugaar dianggap roh jahat, dan di Ataun ia dipakai sebagai momok untuk menakuti anak.
claims.quote: In Betelu, Sugaar is said to be an evil spirit, and in Ataun, he is used as a bogyman figure.

claims.statement: In one legend two brothers from Dima found Sugaar in the Baltzola cave, and the younger cut his tail with a stone.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah legenda, dua bersaudara dari Dima menemukan Sugaar di gua Baltzola, dan si adik memotong ekornya dengan batu.
claims.quote: The pair found Sugaar in a cave in Baltzola, and the younger of the two cut his tail with a stone.

claims.statement: Years later the younger brother refused a red belt from a mysterious man and tied it to a chestnut tree, which burst into flames, and they realised the man was Sugaar.
claims.statement_id: Bertahun-tahun kemudian si adik menolak memakai sabuk merah pemberian seorang lelaki misterius dan mengikatkannya ke pohon kastanye, yang langsung terbakar, sehingga mereka sadar lelaki itu Sugaar.
claims.quote: When the brothers met again, the younger brother refused to put the belt on and tied it to a chestnut tree. The tree burst into flames, and they realized that the man must have been Sugaar.

claims.statement: Sugaar comes from suge (serpent) and -ar (male), 'male serpent'; the reading su (fire) + gar (flame), 'flame of fire', is considered folk etymology.
claims.statement_id: Nama Sugaar berasal dari suge (ular) dan -ar (jantan), jadi "ular jantan"; tafsiran su (api) + gar (nyala), "nyala api", dianggap etimologi rakyat.
claims.quote: The name Suga(a)r is derived from suge (serpent) and -ar (male), thus "male serpent". The suggestions of a formation based on su (fire) and gar (flame), thus yielding "flame of fire" are considered folk etymology.

claims.statement: According to the French article, his main role is to join Mari periodically in the mountains (on Friday at two in the afternoon) to engender storms.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, tugas utamanya adalah bersatu secara berkala dengan Mari di gunung (hari Jumat pukul dua siang) untuk melahirkan badai.
claims.quote: L'essentiel de son existence est de se joindre périodiquement (le vendredi, à deux heures de l'après-midi) à Mari dans les montagnes pour y engendrer des orages.

claims.statement: There is also a myth that he seduced a Scottish princess at Mundaka and fathered Jaun Zuria, the mythical first lord of Biscay.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula mitos bahwa ia menggoda seorang putri Skotlandia di desa Mundaka dan menjadi ayah Jaun Zuria, penguasa pertama Biscaya yang mitis.
claims.quote: Additionnellement, il existe un mythe dans lequel il séduit une princesse écossaise dans le village de Mundaka, pour concevoir le mythique premier seigneur de Biscaye, Jaun Zuria.

claims.statement: Maju is considered an underground spirit who, leaving his lair to unite with Mari, brings a storm with hail.
claims.statement_id: Maju dianggap roh bawah tanah yang, ketika keluar dari sarangnya dan bersatu dengan Mari, menimbulkan badai disertai hujan es.
claims.quote: Maju est considéré comme un génie souterrain qui, en sortant de son antre, s’unit à Mari, provoquant alors une tempête accompagnée de grêle et de grêlons.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, he is a male deity, consort of the goddess Mari though with a much dimmer role, and father of Mikelatz (the wicked son) and Atarrabi (the good son).
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, ia dewa laki-laki, pasangan dewi Mari dengan peran yang lebih samar, dan ayah Mikelatz (anak jahat) serta Atarrabi (anak baik).
claims.quote: Es una divinidad de carácter masculino, consorte de la diosa Mari (tiene, sin embargo, un papel mucho más oscuro que esta), y padre de Mikelatz (hijo perverso) y Atarrabi (hijo bondadoso).

claims.statement: The Badalisc is a mythical creature of the Val Camonica, Italy, in the southern central Alps, shown today with a big goatskin-covered head, two small horns, a huge mouth and glowing eyes.
claims.statement_id: Badalisc adalah makhluk mitis dari Val Camonica, Italia, di Alpen tengah selatan, yang kini digambarkan berkepala besar berbalut kulit kambing, bertanduk dua kecil, bermulut sangat besar, dan bermata menyala.
claims.quote: is a mythical creature of the Val Camonica, Italy, in the southern central Alps. The Badalisc is represented today as a creature with a big head covered with a goat skin, two small horns, a huge mouth and glowing eyes.

claims.statement: By legend the Badalisc lives in the woods around Andrista (Cevo) and pesters the community, so each year it is captured on Epiphany eve (5 January).
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Badalisc tinggal di hutan sekitar desa Andrista (Cevo) dan mengganggu warga, sehingga setiap tahun ia ditangkap pada malam Epifani (5 Januari).
claims.quote: According to legend the Badalisc lives in the woods around the village of Andrista (commune of Cevo) and is supposed to annoy the community: each year it is captured during Epiphany's eve (5th January, the Twelfth Night)

claims.statement: It is led on a rope into the village by masked figures, including the tamer, the sweepers, the old man, the old woman, the hunters and the young maiden who is 'bait' for the animal's lust.
claims.statement_id: Ia dituntun dengan tali ke desa oleh tokoh-tokoh bertopeng, antara lain penjinak, para penyapu, lelaki tua, perempuan tua, pemburu, dan gadis muda yang menjadi "umpan" bagi nafsu binatang itu.
claims.quote: led on a rope into the village by masked characters, including il domatore, gli spazzavia (the sweepers), il vecchio (the old man), la vecchia (the old woman) and the young signorina (the maiden), who is "bait" for the animal's lust, and the hunters.

claims.statement: The Badalisc is mute, so its speech, now written in rhyme, is read by an 'interpreter'; it exposes the community's supposed sins and schemes.
claims.statement_id: Badalisc sendiri bisu, sehingga pidatonya, kini ditulis berima, dibacakan oleh seorang "penerjemah"; pidato itu membeberkan dosa dan tipu muslihat warga.
claims.quote: The Badalisc itself is a dumb creature, so the speech, nowadays written in rhyme, is read by an "interpreter". Once improvised, now written in advance, the speech reveals all the supposed sins and scheming of the community.

claims.statement: In the evening the community eats 'Badalisc polenta', a commercial version of which was launched in 2010.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam hari warga makan "polenta Badalisc", yang versi komersialnya diluncurkan pada 2010.
claims.quote: In the evening the community eats the "Badalisc polenta" (a commercial version of this traditional food was launched in 2010).

claims.statement: On the second day, at the end of the show, the Badalisc is freed and returns to the woods.
claims.statement_id: Pada hari kedua, di akhir pertunjukan, Badalisc dilepaskan dan dibiarkan kembali ke hutan.
claims.quote: On the second day, at the end of the exhibition, the Badalisc is set free and allowed to return to the woods.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the celebration was once for men only: a woman who saw the Badalisc or heard its speech would be refused Holy Communion the next day.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, perayaan ini dulu khusus laki-laki: perempuan yang melihat Badalisc atau mendengar pidatonya akan ditolak menerima Komuni Kudus keesokan harinya.
claims.quote: si une femme venait à voir le Badalisc ou à entendre son discours, elle se voyait refuser la Sainte Communion le lendemain.

claims.statement: Also taking part are witches with drums, bearded shepherds and a hunchback who fights the animal in a rustic duel.
claims.statement_id: Ikut serta pula penyihir berkendang, gembala berjanggut, dan seorang bungkuk yang berduel kasar dengan binatang itu.
claims.quote: Y participent aussi des sorcières munies de tambours, des bergers barbus, et un bossu (un torvo gobetto) qui affronte cet animal dans un duel rustique.

claims.statement: According to the Italian article, the Badalisc festival is held only in Andrista, not elsewhere in the Valle Camonica, on the evening of 5 January, the twelfth night after Christmas.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, pesta Badalisc hanya diadakan di Andrista dan tidak dikenal di tempat lain di Valle Camonica, pada malam 5 Januari, malam kedua belas setelah Natal.
claims.quote: La festa del Badalisc si svolge esclusivamente nella frazione di Andrista ed è una tradizione non diffusa in altre località della Valle Camonica. Ha luogo la sera del 5 gennaio, nella dodicesima notte dopo Natale.

claims.statement: Jean de l'Ours or John the Bear is the hero of the French folktale Jean de l'Ours, classed as Type 301B in the Aarne–Thompson system; the name also denotes any tale of this type.
claims.statement_id: Jean de l'Ours atau John the Bear adalah tokoh utama dongeng Prancis Jean de l'Ours yang digolongkan Tipe 301B dalam sistem Aarne–Thompson; nama itu juga dipakai untuk semua dongeng bertipe ini.
claims.quote: or John the Bear, John of the Bear, John-of-the-Bear, John Bear, is the leading character in the French folktale Jean de l'Ours classed as Type 301B in the Aarne–Thompson system; it can also denote any tale of this type.

claims.statement: Typically the hero is born half-bear, half-human, gets a weapon, usually a heavy iron cane, and on his journey joins two or three companions.
claims.statement_id: Unsur khasnya: sang pahlawan lahir setengah beruang setengah manusia, mendapat senjata, biasanya tongkat besi yang berat, dan dalam perjalanannya bergabung dengan dua atau tiga kawan.
claims.quote: Some typical elements are that the hero is born half-bear, half-human; he obtains a weapon, usually a heavy iron cane, and on his journey; he bands up with two or three companions.

claims.statement: At a castle he defeats a foe, chases him down a hole, finds an underworld and rescues three princesses, but his companions abandon him in the hole and take the princesses.
claims.statement_id: Di sebuah kastel ia mengalahkan seorang lawan, mengejarnya ke sebuah lubang, menemukan dunia bawah, dan menyelamatkan tiga putri, tetapi kawan-kawannya meninggalkannya di lubang dan merebut para putri.
claims.quote: At a castle the hero defeats an adversary, pursues him to a hole, discovers an underworld, and rescues three princesses. The companions abandon him in the hole, taking the princesses for themselves.

claims.statement: He escapes, finds and disposes of the companions, and marries the fairest princess after ordeals set by the king.
claims.statement_id: Ia lolos, menemukan dan menyingkirkan kawan-kawannya, lalu menikahi putri tercantik setelah menjalani ujian dari raja.
claims.quote: The hero escapes, finds the companions and gets rid of them. He marries the most beautiful princess of the three, but not before going through certain ordeal(s) by the king.

claims.statement: The tale is called one of 'the most popular tale-types in Hispanic and Francophone tradition', with many French variants often keeping the hero's name Jean de l'Ours.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini disebut salah satu "tipe dongeng paling populer dalam tradisi Hispanik dan Frankofon", dengan banyak varian di Prancis yang sering tetap menamai pahlawannya Jean de l'Ours.
claims.quote: The character is said to be one of "the most popular tale-types in Hispanic and Francophone tradition". Numerous variants exist in France, often retaining the name Jean de l'Ours or something similar for the hero.

claims.statement: Several French versions say Jean de l'Ours was covered in hair all over his body.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa versi Prancis menyebut tubuh Jean de l'Ours tertutup bulu seluruhnya.
claims.quote: Several French versions explicitly comment on Jean de l'ours being covered with body hair on his entire body.

claims.statement: In one Mexican version (Juan el Oso) and the Russian tale 'Ivanko Medvedko', the hero is human above the waist and bear below.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu versi Meksiko (Juan el Oso) dan dongeng Rusia "Ivanko Medvedko", pahlawan itu manusia dari pinggang ke atas dan beruang dari pinggang ke bawah.
claims.quote: The hero is human from the waist up and bear from the waist down in one Mexican version (Juan el Oso) as well as the Russian tale

claims.statement: According to the German article, Juan Oso, 'Son of the Bear' (Hijo del Oso, Cusco Quechua Ukukuq wawan or Ukuku uña), is the myth of a half-bear, half-human hero.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, Juan Oso, "Putra Beruang" (Hijo del Oso, dalam bahasa Quechua Cusco Ukukuq wawan atau Ukuku uña), adalah mitos tentang pahlawan setengah beruang setengah manusia.
claims.quote: Juan Oso („Johann Bär“), der Sohn des Bären (Hijo del Oso, Cusco-Quechua Ukukuq wawan oder Ukuku uña, Chanka-Quechua Ukumaripa churin oder auch Maqta peludo), ist der Mythos von einem halb bärenhaften, halb menschlichen Helden

claims.statement: The myth is widespread especially in the Spanish-speaking world (Spain, Latin America, New Mexico, California) and parts of Asia, with over 300 versions in about 20 languages, including indigenous American ones.
claims.statement_id: Mitos ini tersebar terutama di dunia berbahasa Spanyol (Spanyol, Amerika Latin, New Mexico, California) dan sebagian Asia, dengan lebih dari 300 versi dalam sekitar 20 bahasa, termasuk bahasa pribumi Amerika.
claims.quote: Der Mythos ist insbesondere im spanischsprachigen Raum (Spanien, Lateinamerika, New Mexico, Kalifornien), aber auch in Teilen Asiens verbreitet. Es gibt mehr als 300 Versionen in etwa 20 Sprachen, neben dem Spanischen auch in indigenen Sprachen Amerikas.

claims.statement: In a very common version a bear abducts a young woman, often a princess, keeps her in his cave and fathers on her a son who is half bear and half human.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi yang sangat umum, seekor beruang menculik seorang perempuan muda, sering seorang putri, mengurungnya di guanya, dan memperoleh anak setengah beruang setengah manusia darinya.
claims.quote: In einer sehr verbreiteten Version verschleppt ein Bär eine junge Frau (oft eine Prinzessin), sperrt sie in seine Höhle ein, wo er sie auch versorgt, und zeugt mit ihr einen Sohn, der halb Bär und halb Mensch ist.

claims.statement: According to the French article, Jean de l'Ours is a hybrid, half-human and half-animal, born of a woman and a bear, with superhuman strength to overcome many trials.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Jean de l'Ours adalah makhluk campuran setengah manusia setengah binatang, lahir dari seorang perempuan dan seekor beruang, dengan kekuatan luar biasa untuk melewati berbagai ujian.
claims.quote: Jean de l’Ours est un être hybride, mi-humain, mi-animal, né d'une femme et d'un ours, et doté d'une force surhumaine qui lui permet de surmonter diverses épreuves.

claims.statement: The tale is especially popular in the Pyrenean regions.
claims.statement_id: Dongeng ini sangat populer di daerah Pyrenees.
claims.quote: Il est particulièrement populaire dans les régions pyrénéennes.

claims.statement: The lamia or lamina (plural lamiak or laminak) is a siren- or nereid-like creature of Basque mythology, usually living in and around rivers.
claims.statement_id: Lamia atau lamina (jamak lamiak atau laminak) adalah makhluk mirip siren atau nereid dalam mitologi Basque yang biasanya tinggal di dalam dan di sekitar sungai.
claims.quote: The lamia (or lamina) (plural: lamiak or laminak) is a siren or nereid-like creature in Basque mythology. Lamiak are typically portrayed as living in and around rivers.

claims.statement: Coastal areas know the itsaslamiak, sea-dwelling lamiak with fish tails like mermaids.
claims.statement_id: Di daerah pesisir dikenal itsaslamiak, lamia yang tinggal di laut dan berekor ikan seperti putri duyung.
claims.quote: Mythology in coastal areas includes itsaslamiak, a variety of lamiak who live in the sea and have fish-like tails, similar to a mermaid.

claims.statement: Lamiak are generous and help with the work of those who give them gifts; if a farmer leaves food on the riverbank, they eat it at night and finish ploughing his field.
claims.statement_id: Lamiak digambarkan murah hati dan membantu pekerjaan orang yang memberi mereka hadiah; misalnya, bila petani meninggalkan makanan di tepi sungai, mereka memakannya malam hari lalu menyelesaikan bajakan ladangnya.
claims.quote: Basque mythology depicts lamiak as generous, aiding those who give them presents by helping them at work. For example, if a farmer were to leave food for them at the river shore, they would eat it at night and in exchange finish ploughing his field.

claims.statement: In other myths lamiak must leave if the bridge they build by night is unfinished at cockcrow, and a missing stone in a bridge showed that the lamiak had left that river.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos lain, lamiak harus pergi bila jembatan yang mereka bangun malam hari belum selesai saat ayam berkokok, dan batu yang hilang di jembatan dianggap tanda lamiak telah meninggalkan sungai itu.
claims.quote: In other myths, lamiak must leave if the bridge that they were building at night remains unfinished at cockcrow. People believed that lamia ... had left a river if a stone in the bridge was missing.

claims.statement: Other beliefs hold that most lamiak vanished when people built small chapels in the forest.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan lain, kebanyakan lamiak menghilang ketika orang membangun kapel-kapel kecil di hutan.
claims.quote: Other beliefs claim that most lamiak disappeared when men built small churches in the forest.

claims.statement: Lamiak are also believed to sit beyond rainbows combing their hair, and the rainbow opens when sunlight strikes it.
claims.statement_id: Lamiak juga dipercaya berada di balik pelangi sambil menyisir rambut, dan pelangi terbuka ketika sinar matahari mengenai rambut mereka.
claims.quote: Lamiak are also believed to be found on the other side of rainbows, where they are combing their hair. It is said that when the sunlight strikes their hair, the rainbow opens.

claims.statement: Sometimes there are male lamiak, strong and credited with building dolmens by night.
claims.statement_id: Kadang ada pula lamiak laki-laki yang kuat dan dianggap membangun dolmen pada malam hari.
claims.quote: Mythology also occasionally describes male lamiak. In those stories, they are described as strong and are attributed with the creation of dolmens at night.

claims.statement: Many place names relate to lamiak, such as Lamikiz (Markina), Laminaputzu (Zeanuri), Lamusin (Sare) and Lamiñosin (Ataun).
claims.statement_id: Banyak nama tempat berkaitan dengan lamiak, seperti Lamikiz (Markina), Laminaputzu (Zeanuri), Lamusin (Sare), dan Lamiñosin (Ataun).
claims.quote: Many toponyms relate to lamiak, including Lamikiz (Markina), Laminaputzu (in Zeanuri), Lamitegi (in Bedaio), Lamirain (in Arano), Lamusin (in Sare), Lamiñosin (in Ataun).

claims.statement: According to the French article, lamina is the Basque term for a fantastic being, a nature spirit or humanlike genie.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, lamina adalah istilah Basque untuk makhluk fantastis, roh alam atau genius berwujud manusia.
claims.quote: est le terme basque désignant un être fantastique de la mythologie basque, un esprit de la nature ou un Irelu ou génie d'apparence humaine.

claims.statement: Laminak are most often shown either as male goblins or dwarfs or as normal-sized women whose lower body has animal features: webbed feet, hen's feet, goat hooves or a fish tail.
claims.statement_id: Laminak paling sering digambarkan sebagai kurcaci laki-laki atau perempuan bertubuh biasa yang bagian bawahnya berciri hewan: kaki berselaput, kaki ayam, kuku kambing, atau ekor ikan.
claims.quote: Le plus souvent, les laminak sont dépeints soit comme des lutins mâles, des nains (ipotxak ou nanoak), soit comme des femmes de taille normale dont le bas du corps est pourvu de caractéristiques animales (pieds palmés, pattes de poules, sabots de chèvre ou queue de poisson).

claims.statement: Laminak are mainly nocturnal and live underground, in caves or by springs and streams.
claims.statement_id: Laminak terutama makhluk malam yang tinggal di bawah tanah, di gua, atau dekat mata air dan sungai kecil.
claims.quote: Créatures essentiellement nocturnes, les laminak vivent sous terre, dans des grottes ou auprès des sources et des ruisseaux.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, people see them combing their hair with a golden comb or, less often, spreading out their beautiful cloth to dry.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, manusia melihat mereka menyisir rambut dengan sisir emas atau, lebih jarang, menjemur kain mereka yang indah.
claims.quote: Los seres humanos las ven peinándose el cabello con un peine de oro o, con menos frecuencia, tendiendo y secando su hermoso paño.

claims.statement: In many tales she is a beautiful woman with some non-human feature, such as hen's, goat's or duck's feet or a fish tail, depending on the area.
claims.statement_id: Dalam banyak cerita ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan cantik dengan satu ciri bukan manusia, seperti kaki ayam, kambing, atau bebek, atau ekor ikan, tergantung daerahnya.
claims.quote: En muchas narraciones se la describe como una mujer hermosa que presenta algún rasgo no humano, como patas de gallina, de cabra, de pato o cola de pez, según la zona y la tradición oral concreta.

claims.statement: In some places bridges were believed to have been built by lamiak at night.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa tempat, jembatan dipercaya dibangun oleh lamiak pada malam hari.
claims.quote: In some places, bridges were believed to have been built at night by lamiak

claims.statement: In Portuguese, Galician and Asturian mythology, the Mouros or Moiros are a race of supernatural beings who have lived in Galicia, Asturias and Portugal since the beginning of time.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Portugal, Galisia, dan Asturias, Mouros atau Moiros adalah bangsa makhluk gaib yang mendiami tanah Galisia, Asturias, dan Portugal sejak awal zaman.
claims.quote: the Mouros or Moiros are a race of supernatural beings which have inhabited the lands of Galicia, Asturias and Portugal since the beginning of time.

claims.statement: For unknown reasons they had to take refuge underground and are now usually seen around castros and long barrows; they work gold, silver and gems into huge treasures guarded by cuélebres.
claims.statement_id: Karena sebab yang tak diketahui mereka terpaksa berlindung di bawah tanah dan kini biasanya terlihat di sekitar castro dan makam gundukan panjang; mereka mengolah emas, perak, dan permata menjadi harta besar yang dijaga cuélebre.
claims.quote: For unknown reasons they were forced to take refuge under the earth, and now they are usually seen by people in the surroundings of castros and long barrows. The Mouros work with gold, silver and gemstones with which they make up enormous treasures that are protected by cuélebres.

claims.statement: The Mouros rarely leave their dwellings except to get food and at special times such as Midsummer.
claims.statement_id: Mouros jarang keluar dari tempat tinggalnya kecuali untuk mengambil makanan dan pada waktu khusus seperti pertengahan musim panas.
claims.quote: The Mouros do not usually go out of their dwellings, except for taking food, and also at certain special times such as Midsummer.

claims.statement: Galician anthropologists theorised that the Mouros are the opposite of the traditional Galician peasant.
claims.statement_id: Para antropolog Galisia berteori bahwa Mouros adalah kebalikan dari petani Galisia tradisional.
claims.quote: Galician anthropologists had formed the theory that the Mouros are the opposite character of traditional Galician peasant.

claims.statement: The philologist Isodoro Millán derives the word from Celtic mrvos, akin to Indo-European mr-tuos and Latin mortuus, linking the Mouros to races already extinct or dead.
claims.statement_id: Filolog Isodoro Millán berpendapat kata ini berasal dari kata Kelt mrvos, kerabat kata Indo-Eropa mr-tuos dan Latin mortuus, sehingga Mouros dikaitkan dengan bangsa yang sudah punah atau mati.
claims.quote: The philologist Isodoro Millán argues that the term Moor comes from the Celtic mrvos akin to the Indo-European term mr-tuos, whence the Latin mortuus. This would relate the Moors to races already extinct, dead.

claims.statement: The Mouros encantados sometimes appear as giants or warriors, and include the legend of the moura encantada and the mourinhos or maruxinhos, a very small elf-like people.
claims.statement_id: Mouros encantados kadang muncul sebagai raksasa atau prajurit, dan mencakup legenda moura encantada serta mourinhos atau maruxinhos, bangsa mirip peri yang sangat kecil.
claims.quote: The Mouros encantados some times appear as giants or warriors, and they include the legend of the moura encantada and the legend of the mourinhos or maruxinhos, a very small elf like people

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, others link the name to Galician ouro, 'gold', since the Mouros lived in underground lairs and tunnels mining gold.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, sebagian orang mengaitkan namanya dengan kata Galisia ouro, "emas", karena Mouros tinggal di sarang dan terowongan bawah tanah dan menambang emas.
claims.quote: Para otros su nombre está relacionado con el gallego ouro. Y es que los mouros eran criaturas que vivían en el subsuelo en guaridas y túneles bajo la tierra, donde —dependiendo de la zona— se dedicaban a la extracción del oro (de ahí el porqué de su nombre).

claims.statement: The male mouros were goldsmiths and sometimes dark-skinned as if foreign, while the female mouras were reputed sorceresses with red hair.
claims.statement_id: Mouros laki-laki bekerja sebagai pandai emas dan kadang berkulit gelap seolah orang asing, sedangkan mouras perempuan dikenal sebagai penyihir dan berambut merah.
claims.quote: Los mouros trabajaban en la orfebrería y en algunos casos eran oscuros de piel, como si fuesen gente ajena a la tierra gallega, mientras que las mouras tenían fama de hechiceras y eran pelirrojas

claims.statement: They trade with humans and pay in gold, but if the person tells others where the wealth came from, the gold turns to stones or coal.
claims.statement_id: Mereka berdagang dengan manusia dan membayar dengan emas, tetapi bila orang itu menceritakan asal kekayaannya, emasnya berubah menjadi batu atau arang.
claims.quote: o bien realizan negocios o intercambios con los humanos de los cuales éstos son pagados con oro, excepto si cuentan a los demás el origen de su riqueza (el negocio con el mouro) en que el oro se convierte en piedras o carbón.

claims.statement: The Russian article also calls the Mouros a race of supernatural beings inhabiting Galicia, Asturias and Portugal since the beginning of time.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Rusia juga menyebut Mouros bangsa makhluk gaib yang mendiami Galisia, Asturias, dan Portugal sejak awal zaman.
claims.quote: раса сверхъестественных существ, населяющих земли Галисии, Астурии и Португалии с начала времён.

claims.statement: Tartaro, Tartalo or Torto of Basque mythology is an enormously strong one-eyed giant much like the Greek Cyclops Odysseus faced, living in mountain caves and catching young people to eat, sometimes sheep too.
claims.statement_id: Tartaro, Tartalo, atau Torto dalam mitologi Basque adalah raksasa bermata satu yang sangat kuat, mirip Kiklops Yunani yang dihadapi Odisseus, yang tinggal di gua pegunungan dan menangkap orang muda untuk dimakan, kadang juga domba.
claims.quote: Tartaro, Tartalo, or Torto in Basque mythology, is an enormously strong one-eyed giant very similar to the Greek Cyclops that Odysseus faced in Homer's Odyssey. He is said to live in caves in the mountains and catches young people in order to eat them; in some accounts he eats sheep also.

claims.statement: Torto, Anxo and Alarabi are the forms listed by Barandiaran, with 'Tartalo' a local variant of the Zegama area.
claims.statement_id: Torto, Anxo, dan Alarabi adalah bentuk nama yang dicatat Barandiaran, dengan "Tartalo" sebagai varian setempat daerah Zegama.
claims.quote: Torto, Anxo and Alarabi were the forms listed in Jose Migel Barandiaran's Basque Mythology, with "Tartalo" described as a local variant particular to the Zegama region.

claims.statement: Cerquand in his 1875 book suggested that the name 'Tartaro' came from the Tartar people.
claims.statement_id: Cerquand dalam bukunya (1875) menduga nama "Tartaro" berasal dari bangsa Tatar.
claims.quote: Cerquand ... in his book "Légendes et récits populaires du Pays basque, volume 1" (1875) suggested in an annotation that the name "Tartaro" derived from the Tartar people

claims.statement: A magic ring is a common theme in the Tartalo tales.
claims.statement_id: Cincin ajaib adalah tema umum dalam kisah-kisah Tartalo.
claims.quote: A mystical ring is a common theme in the Tartalo/Tartaro tales.

claims.statement: One day two brothers from the Antimuño farm, out hunting, sheltered from a storm in a cave that turned out to be Tartalo's.
claims.statement_id: Suatu hari dua bersaudara dari pertanian Antimuño yang sedang berburu berlindung dari badai di sebuah gua, yang ternyata gua Tartalo.
claims.quote: One day, while two brothers of the Antimuño baserri were hunting, a storm broke, so they decided to take refuge from the rain in a cave, which was Tartalo's cave.

claims.statement: After Tartalo ate the elder brother and fell asleep, the younger stole his ring and drove the roasting spit into his only eye.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Tartalo memakan si kakak dan tertidur, si adik mencuri cincinnya dan menusukkan tusuk panggangan ke satu-satunya matanya.
claims.quote: While he was sleeping, the youngest brother stole Tartalo's ring and then he stuck the roasting spit in his only eye.

claims.statement: Tartalo searched for the boy among his sheep, but the boy put on a sheepskin and escaped.
claims.statement_id: Tartalo mencari si anak di antara dombanya, tetapi anak itu memakai kulit domba dan lolos.
claims.quote: He started to look for the boy among his sheep, but he put on a sheep's skin and escaped from Tartalo.

claims.statement: The ring shouted out his whereabouts and would not come off, so at a cliff edge the boy cut off his finger and threw it down; Tartalo followed the ring's shouts and fell off the cliff.
claims.statement_id: Cincin itu berteriak memberi tahu tempatnya dan tidak dapat dilepas, maka di tepi tebing si anak memotong jarinya dan melemparkannya ke bawah; Tartalo mengikuti teriakan cincin itu dan jatuh dari tebing.
claims.quote: The young one wasn't able to take off the ring, so, when he arrived to the edge of a cliff, he cut off his finger, and since Tartalo was near, he decided to throw it down the cliff. Tartalo, following the ring's shouting, fell off the cliff.

claims.statement: According to the French article, a figure called Tartari was known beyond Gascony, in the Agenais on the right bank of the Garonne.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, tokoh bernama Tartari juga dikenal di luar Gascogne, di Agenais di tepi kanan Garonne.
claims.quote: Un personnage appelé Tartari était attesté au-delà de la Gascogne, rive droite de la Garonne, dans l'Agenais

claims.statement: His traits and adventures closely match those of the Cyclops Polyphemus: like him he lives in a cave and keeps sheep.
claims.statement_id: Ciri dan petualangannya cukup dekat dengan Kiklops Polifemos: seperti dia, Tartalo tinggal di gua dan beternak domba.
claims.quote: Les caractéristiques et les aventures qu'on lui prête correspondent d'assez près à celles du cyclope Polyphème. Comme lui il vit dans une caverne, il élève des moutons

claims.statement: Some sources explain Anxo or Ancho as another name for Basajaun.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sumber menyebut Anxo atau Ancho sebagai nama lain Basajaun.
claims.quote: Anxo or Ancho is however explained as an alternate name for Basajaun by some sources.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, his size and appetite are enormous, and his favourite pastime of hurling stones from mountain to mountain is said to have created several structures still standing.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, ukuran dan nafsu makannya sangat besar, dan kegemarannya melempar batu dari satu gunung ke gunung lain konon menghasilkan beberapa bangunan yang masih ada.
claims.quote: Su tamaño es descomunal, al igual que su apetito, y su entretenimiento favorito era tirar piedras de un monte a otro. Cuenta la leyenda que debido a este entretenimiento se crearon varias construcciones existentes hoy en día.

claims.statement: Tohil (also Tojil) is the Maya god of fire, a deity of the Kʼicheʼ Maya in the Late Postclassic period of Mesoamerica.
claims.statement_id: Tohil (juga Tojil) adalah dewa api Maya, dewa orang Maya Kʼicheʼ pada periode Pascaklasik Akhir Mesoamerika.
claims.quote: also spelled Tojil) is the Maya god of fire. He is a deity of the Kʼicheʼ Maya in the Late Postclassic period of Mesoamerica.

claims.statement: At the time of the Spanish Conquest, Tohil was the patron god of the Kʼicheʼ.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa penaklukan Spanyol, Tohil adalah dewa pelindung orang Kʼicheʼ.
claims.quote: At the time of the Spanish Conquest, Tohil was the patron god of the Kʼicheʼ.

claims.statement: Tohil was also linked with mountains and was a god of war, sacrifice and sustenance.
claims.statement_id: Tohil juga dikaitkan dengan gunung dan merupakan dewa perang, pengorbanan, dan rezeki.
claims.quote: Tohil was also associated with mountains and he was a god of war, sacrifice and sustenance.

claims.statement: In the Kʼicheʼ epic Popol Vuh the first people gathered at the mythical Tollan or Tula, Place of the Seven Caves, to receive their language and gods, and there the Kʼicheʼ received Tohil.
claims.statement_id: Dalam epos Kʼicheʼ Popol Vuh, manusia pertama berkumpul di Tollan atau Tula yang mitis, Tempat Tujuh Gua, untuk menerima bahasa dan dewa mereka, dan di sana orang Kʼicheʼ menerima Tohil.
claims.quote: In the Kʼicheʼ epic Popul Vuh, after the first people were created, they gathered at the mythical Tollan or Tula, the Place of the Seven Caves, to receive their language and their gods. The Kʼicheʼ, and others, there received Tohil.

claims.statement: Tohil demanded blood sacrifice, and in the Popol Vuh his consumption of blood is likened to a baby suckling at its mother.
claims.statement_id: Tohil menuntut korban darah, dan dalam Popol Vuh konsumsi darah itu diibaratkan bayi yang menyusu kepada ibunya.
claims.quote: In the Popul Vuh this consumption of blood by Tohil is likened to the suckling of an infant by its mother.

claims.statement: The Kaqchikel refused the human sacrifice Tohil demanded in return for fire, and so they stole the fire from the god.
claims.statement_id: Suku Kaqchikel menolak korban manusia yang dituntut Tohil sebagai imbalan api, sehingga mereka mencuri api dari dewa itu.
claims.quote: Indeed, it's known that the Kaqchikel tribe was against the human sacrifice demanded by Tohil to bring them fire. For this reason they stole the fire from the deity

claims.statement: Tohil was one of a trinity of gods worshipped by the Kʼicheʼ elite, with Awilix and Jacawitz.
claims.statement_id: Tohil adalah salah satu dari tiga dewa yang dipuja kaum elite Kʼicheʼ, bersama Awilix dan Jacawitz.
claims.quote: Tohil was one of a trinity of gods worshipped by the Kʼicheʼ elite, together with Awilix and Jacawitz.

claims.statement: He was tied to a sacred deerskin bundle said to embody him, one of his titles was Qajawal Kej ('Our Lord Deer'), and he was associated with thunder, lightning and sunrise.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan buntelan kulit rusa suci yang dianggap perwujudannya, salah satu gelarnya Qajawal Kej ("Tuan Rusa Kami"), dan ia berkaitan dengan guntur, petir, dan matahari terbit.
claims.quote: He was associated with a sacred deerskin bundle that was said to embody him, and one of his titles was Qajawal Kej ("Our Lord Deer"). The deity was associated with thunder, lightning and the sunrise.

claims.statement: Later the Kʼicheʼ built their main temple to Tohil at their new capital, Qʼumarkaj.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian orang Kʼicheʼ membangun kuil utama Tohil di ibu kota baru mereka, Qʼumarkaj.
claims.quote: Later the Kʼicheʼ built their main temple to Tohil at Qʼumarkaj, their new capital.

claims.statement: Because of his link with human sacrifice, Tohil was among the first gods the Spanish clergy tried to stamp out.
claims.statement_id: Karena kaitannya dengan korban manusia, Tohil termasuk dewa pertama yang ingin dimusnahkan para rohaniwan Spanyol.
claims.quote: The god's association with human sacrifice meant that Tohil was one of the first deities that the Spanish clergy tried to eradicate

claims.statement: The Kʼicheʼ themselves claimed in the Popol Vuh that Tohil was the same as the Aztec Quetzalcoatl.
claims.statement_id: Orang Kʼicheʼ sendiri menyatakan dalam Popol Vuh bahwa Tohil sama dengan Quetzalcoatl dari bangsa Aztek.
claims.quote: The Kʼicheʼ themselves claimed in the Popul Vuh that their patron Tohil was the same as Quetzalcoatl of the Aztecs.

claims.statement: In Santiago Atitlán, 'King Martin' is probably a blend of Tohil and his deerskin bundle with St Martin of Tours, whose feast falls on the same day.
claims.statement_id: Di Santiago Atitlán, dewa "Raja Martin" kemungkinan perpaduan Tohil dan buntelan kulit rusanya dengan Santo Martinus dari Tours, yang hari rayanya jatuh pada hari yang sama.
claims.quote: King Martin is probably a blend of Tohil and his deerskin bundle with the Roman Catholic St Martin of Tours, whose feast falls on the same day.

claims.statement: The Indonesian article also calls Tohil a K'iche' Maya god of the Late Postclassic and their patron god at the Spanish conquest.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Indonesia juga menyebut Tohil dewa Maya K'iche' pada periode Pascaklasik Akhir dan dewa pelindung K'iche' pada masa pendudukan Spanyol.
claims.quote: adalah dewa Maya K'iche' pada periode Pasca-Klasik Akhir Mesoamerika. Pada masa pendudukan Spanyol, Tohil adalah dewa pelindung K'iche'.

claims.statement: According to the French article, Tohil was a god of fire, sun and rain, also associated with mountains, war and sacrifice.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Tohil dewa api, matahari, dan hujan yang juga dikaitkan dengan gunung, perang, dan pengorbanan.
claims.quote: C'était une divinité du feu mais aussi du soleil et de la pluie. Elle était aussi associée aux montagnes et aux dieux de la guerre ainsi qu'à des sacrifices.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, Atlatonin or Atlatonan was a Mexica goddess of the coasts and a mother goddess.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, Atlatonin atau Atlatonan adalah dewi Meksika (Aztek) penguasa pesisir dan dewi ibu.
claims.quote: Atlatonin o Atlatonan era una diosa mexica de las costas y diosa madre.

claims.statement: She is associated with Tezcatlipoca, and some myths make her one of his wives.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan Tezcatlipoca, dan sebagian mitos menganggapnya salah satu istrinya.
claims.quote: Está asociada con Tezcatlipoca y algunos mitos la consideran una de sus esposas.

claims.statement: From the same root Atl ('water') come Atlacamani, goddess of ocean storms, and Atlacoya, goddess of drought.
claims.statement_id: Dari akar kata Atl ("air") juga lahir nama Atlacamani, dewi badai laut, dan Atlacoya, dewi kemarau.
claims.quote: Derivado de la raíz Atl produce también Atlacamani, la diosa de las tempestades oceánicas y Atlacoya la diosa de las sequías.

claims.statement: According to the Russian article, Atlatonin is one of the names of the Aztec mother goddess.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, Atlatonin adalah salah satu nama dewi ibu Aztek.
claims.quote: Атлатонин (аст. Atlatonin) — одно из имён ацтекской богини-матери.

claims.statement: According to the Italian article, in Aztec mythology Atlatonin was a mother goddess and goddess of the coasts.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, Atlatonin dalam mitologi Aztek adalah dewi ibu dan dewi pesisir.
claims.quote: Atlatonin nella mitologia azteca, era una divinità madre e dea delle coste.

claims.statement: She loved rituals and demanded sacrifices, so she was often impersonated by young virgins, and was also known as Atlatonal.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyukai ritual dan menuntut korban, sehingga sering diperankan oleh gadis-gadis muda, dan juga dikenal dengan nama Atlatonal.
claims.quote: Amava i rituali e pretendeva sacrifici. Per questo motivo veniva spesso impersonificata da giovani vergini. Conosciuta anche col nome di Atlatonal.

claims.statement: Guivre (or givre) and vouivre are French names for a serpentine mythical creature, by extension a dragon, by some accounts equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern.
claims.statement_id: Guivre (atau givre) dan vouivre adalah nama Prancis untuk sejenis makhluk mitis berwujud ular, lebih luas lagi naga, yang menurut sebagian pihak setara dengan lindworm atau wyvern.
claims.quote: Guivre (or givre) and vouivre are French names for a type of serpentine mythical creature, by extension a dragon, by some accords, equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern.

claims.statement: In legend they are serpentine creatures with venomous breath that prowled the countryside of medieval France.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda mereka digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular bernapas racun yang berkeliaran di pedesaan Prancis abad pertengahan.
claims.quote: In legend they are portrayed as serpentine creatures who possessed venomous breath and prowled the countryside of Medieval France.

claims.statement: The English word wyvern derives from Old French vouivre.
claims.statement_id: Kata Inggris wyvern berasal dari kata Prancis Kuno vouivre.
claims.quote: The English wyvern (a type of dragon) derives from Old French "vouivre".

claims.statement: Guivres had a long serpentine body and a dragon's head, hind feet barely visible if present at all, and in some accounts horns on the forehead.
claims.statement_id: Guivre bertubuh panjang seperti ular dan berkepala naga, kaki belakangnya hampir tak terlihat kalaupun ada, dan dalam sebagian kisah bertanduk di dahi.
claims.quote: Guivres (alternatively givres) were said to possess a long, serpentine body and a dragon's head. The hind feet are not as visible if present at all. The guivre had horns in its forehead in some accounts, as well.

claims.statement: Locally in France it was known as extremely aggressive, sometimes attacking unprovoked, yet it feared naked humans and would blush and look away on seeing one.
claims.statement_id: Di Prancis ia dikenal sangat agresif dan kadang menyerang tanpa sebab, tetapi takut pada manusia telanjang: bila melihatnya, guivre tersipu dan memalingkan muka.
claims.quote: Locally in France, it was known as an extremely aggressive creature that would sometimes attack without being provoked. They were afraid of naked humans, and when saw them, blushed and looked away.

claims.statement: Guivres lived in small bodies of water like pools and lakes, in forests and in any damp place.
claims.statement_id: Guivre tinggal di perairan kecil seperti kolam dan danau, di hutan, dan di tempat lembap.
claims.quote: Documentation points to their residence as being in small bodies of water like pools and lakes, forests, and any damp place.

claims.statement: Samson of Dol witnessed an encounter between a priest and a small dragon-like creature called La Guivre.
claims.statement_id: Santo Samson dari Dol menyaksikan pertemuan seorang imam dengan makhluk kecil mirip naga yang disebut La Guivre.
claims.quote: Samson of Dol was present at an encounter between a small dragon-like creature, known as La Guivre ("the guivre"), and a priest.

claims.statement: Saint Suliao rebuked the priest who had hidden bread in his robe, pulled a hideous serpentine creature from it, exorcised it and had another man throw it from a roof in Garot.
claims.statement_id: Santo Suliao menegur imam yang menyembunyikan roti di jubahnya, mengeluarkan makhluk ular yang mengerikan dari jubah itu, mengusirnya, lalu menyuruh orang lain melemparkannya dari atap sebuah bangunan di Garot.
claims.quote: He admonished the priest and removed a hideous serpentine creature from the robe. There, he exorcised it and then compelled another man to throw it from the roof of a building in Garot.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the vouivre is a legendary creature of several European countries, usually a two-legged dragon or winged serpent often bearing a carbuncle on its brow, called guivre in heraldry.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, vouivre adalah makhluk legenda di beberapa negara Eropa, biasanya berupa naga berkaki dua atau ular bersayap yang sering membawa batu merah delima di dahinya, dan dalam heraldik disebut guivre.
claims.quote: La vouivre est une créature légendaire présente dans plusieurs pays européens, ayant généralement la forme d'un dragon bipède ou d'un serpent ailé. Elle est souvent censée porter une escarboucle sur le front. En héraldique, elle est aussi appelée guivre.

claims.statement: The word vouivre is a regionalism of Lorraine, Burgundy, Franche-Comté, the Jura and Switzerland.
claims.statement_id: Kata vouivre adalah regionalisme khas Lorraine, Bourgogne, Franche-Comté, Jura, dan Swiss.
claims.quote: Ce mot est un régionalisme linguistique propre à la Lorraine, la Bourgogne, la Franche-Comté, le Jura et la Suisse.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, all these forms ultimately come from Latin vipera, like Spanish víbora.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, semua bentuk ini akhirnya berasal dari kata Latin vipera, seperti kata Spanyol víbora.
claims.quote: Todas estas formas se derivan en última instancia del latín Vipera, como es el Español víbora.

claims.statement: Nuberu, Nubero (Castilian) or Nubeiro (Galician), literally 'The Clouder', is a figure of Asturian, Cantabrian, Galician and Leonese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Nuberu, Nubero (Kastilia), atau Nubeiro (Galisia), harfiah "Si Pembuat Awan", adalah tokoh mitologi Asturias, Cantabria, Galisia, dan León.
claims.quote: Nubero (Castilian) or Nubeiro (Galician) -literally "The Clouder"- is a character of Asturian, Cantabrian, Galician and Leonese mythology.

claims.statement: In Asturian mythology the Nuberu (in western Asturias also Reñubeiru or Xuan Cabritu) is the god of clouds and storms.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitologi Asturias, Nuberu (di Asturias barat juga Reñubeiru atau Xuan Cabritu) adalah dewa awan dan badai.
claims.quote: According to Asturian mythology, the Nuberu (also known in Western Asturias as Reñubeiru or Xuan Cabritu) is the divinity of clouds and storms.

claims.statement: In some stories he is one being, in others a species of dwarf-like weather-controlling beings, and sometimes a thick-bearded man in goatskins and a big hat.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian cerita ia satu sosok, dalam cerita lain sejenis makhluk mirip kurcaci yang dapat mengendalikan cuaca, dan kadang ia digambarkan lelaki berjanggut lebat berpakaian kulit kambing dan bertopi besar.
claims.quote: In some stories, he is an individual; in others, the Nuberu is a species of dwarf-like beings with the power to control the weather. Sometimes, he is represented as a man with a thick beard, who wears goat leathers and a big hat.

claims.statement: As a single being, Nuberu wears dark pelts, rides a wolf-drawn chariot and wears a patch over an injured or missing eye.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai satu sosok, Nuberu berpakaian kulit binatang gelap, naik kereta yang ditarik serigala, dan memakai penutup mata untuk mata yang terluka atau hilang.
claims.quote: When he is treated as a single entity, Nuberu is said to dress with dark pelts and leather, travel in a chariot pulled by wolves, and wear a patch to cover an injured or missing eye.

claims.statement: He can be terribly cruel, damaging fields and pastures, but kind to those who once helped him, and by myth he lives in the city of Orito in Egypt.
claims.statement_id: Ia bisa sangat kejam, merusak ladang dan padang rumput, tetapi baik kepada orang yang pernah menolongnya, dan menurut mitos ia tinggal di kota Orito di Mesir.
claims.quote: He, or they, can be terribly cruel to people, damaging fields and pastures, although he can also be very kind to those who had helped him before. The myth tells us that he lives in the city of Orito, in Egypt.

claims.statement: Folklorists see Nuberu as an Asturian remnant of the ancient sky god Taranis, worshipped in Asturias until the Middle Ages.
claims.statement_id: Para folklorist menganggap Nuberu sisa dewa kuno Taranis, penguasa langit yang dipuja di Asturias sampai Abad Pertengahan.
claims.quote: Folklorists think that Nuberu is an Asturian remnant of the ancient god Taranis, who also ruled over the skies and was worshipped in Asturias until the Middle Ages.

claims.statement: Its closest Spanish parallel is the Entiznáu of Extremadura, an evil weather creature of similar look and dress but different size.
claims.statement_id: Padanan terdekatnya di Spanyol adalah Entiznáu dari Extremadura, makhluk cuaca jahat yang serupa wujud dan pakaiannya tetapi berbeda ukuran.
claims.quote: Within Spain, their closest parallel is the Entiznáu from Extremadura, another evil weather creature with dark appearance and power over storms, who shares description and clothing with Nuberu, but differs in size.

claims.statement: Nuberu once fell from a cloud and only one peasant would shelter him; in thanks, Nuberu watered his fields, gave him good harvests and still brings rain to the region.
claims.statement_id: Konon Nuberu jatuh dari awan dan hanya seorang petani yang mau menampungnya; sebagai terima kasih, Nuberu mengairi ladangnya, memberinya panen baik, dan terus memberi hujan kepada penduduk daerah itu.
claims.quote: In appreciation for his help, Nuberu irrigated his fields, and gave him good harvests, and has continued to provide rain to the people of the region.

claims.statement: Years later the peasant, in Egypt, heard his wife was to remarry; he asked Nuberu for help, and they rode the clouds back to Asturias in time to stop the wedding.
claims.statement_id: Bertahun-tahun kemudian petani itu di Mesir mendengar istrinya akan menikah lagi; ia meminta tolong Nuberu, dan mereka menunggang awan kembali ke Asturias tepat waktu untuk menggagalkan pernikahan.
claims.quote: The peasant then asked Nuberu for help and together they travel back to Asturias riding the clouds and they arrive in time to prevent the wedding.

claims.statement: Fishermen fear the Nuberu, blaming him for the strong north-westerly winds of the Cantabrian Sea that drive them hurriedly back to port.
claims.statement_id: Para nelayan takut pada Nuberu karena menyalahkannya atas angin barat laut kencang di Laut Cantabria yang memaksa mereka bergegas pulang ke pelabuhan.
claims.quote: Fishermen fear the Nuberu because they blame him for the strong north-western winds of the Cantabrian Sea, which forces them to return hurriedly to port, where worried people await them.

claims.statement: In Cantabrian mythology the Nuberus are often many little creatures, small, chubby and mischievous, with devilish grins and little black wings.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Cantabria, nuberu sering berupa banyak makhluk kecil yang gemuk dan nakal, berwajah iblis menyeringai dan bersayap hitam kecil.
claims.quote: In Cantabrian mythology, the Nuberus are often a multitude of little creatures, not a single one. They are described as small, chubby and mischievous, with devilish grins in their demonic faces and little black wings.

claims.statement: In southern Galicia Nubeiros are small hairy men with long twisted tails who fly on grey clouds and cause dry summer storms and lightning.
claims.statement_id: Di Galisia selatan, nubeiro berupa lelaki kecil berbulu berekor panjang dan berpilin yang terbang di atas awan kelabu dan menimbulkan badai kering musim panas dan petir.
claims.quote: In Southern Galicia, Nubeiros have the appearance of small hairy men with a long and twisted tail. They fly on grey clouds and cause dry summer storms, lightning, and similar disasters.

claims.statement: Elsewhere in Galicia, Nuberu forges lightning himself in his mountain ironworks, then rides the sky to cause storms and hurl his creations.
claims.statement_id: Di bagian lain Galisia, Nuberu menempa petir sendiri di bengkel besinya di pegunungan, lalu menunggang langit untuk menimbulkan badai dan melemparkan petir-petirnya.
claims.quote: Nuberu forges lightning by himself in his iron workshop in the mountains, and when he has made enough he goes out and rides through the sky to cause storms and throw his creations around.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, their look varies by place but they are almost always humanlike, aged, extremely ugly and dark-skinned, with big mouths and ears, thick beards and sunken eyes glowing like red embers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, wujud mereka berbeda menurut daerah, tetapi hampir selalu mirip manusia, tua, sangat buruk rupa, berkulit gelap, bermulut dan bertelinga besar, berjanggut lebat, dengan mata cekung menyala seperti bara merah.
claims.quote: Su apariencia varía dependiendo del lugar, pero casi siempre se describen como seres antropomorfos, envejecidos, extremadamente feos, de tez oscura, con boca y orejas grandes y barba poblada. Sus ojos hundidos lucen como brasas rojas.

claims.statement: The Russian article also compares him with Odin and Zeus.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Rusia juga membandingkannya dengan Odin dan Zeus.
claims.quote: Также сравнивается с Одином и Зевсом по схожим причинам.

claims.statement: The rougarou (also roux-ga-roux, rugaroo or rugaru) is a legendary creature of the Cajun and Creole diaspora and a trickster in Métis and Francophone oral traditions, linked to the werewolf.
claims.statement_id: Rougarou (juga roux-ga-roux, rugaroo, atau rugaru) adalah makhluk legenda diaspora Cajun dan Kreol serta tokoh penipu dalam tradisi lisan komunitas Métis dan berbahasa Prancis, yang terkait dengan konsep manusia serigala.
claims.quote: alternatively spelled as roux-ga-roux, rugaroo, or rugaru) is a legendary creature in Cajun and Creole diaspora and a trickster in oral traditions in Métis and Francophone communities linked to traditional concepts of the werewolf.

claims.statement: The name comes from loup-garou: loup is French for wolf, and garou (from Frankish warulf, akin to werewolf) is a man who turns into an animal.
claims.statement_id: Namanya dari loup-garou: loup berarti serigala dalam bahasa Prancis, dan garou (dari kata Franka warulf, sekerabat dengan werewolf) adalah manusia yang berubah menjadi binatang.
claims.quote: Loup is French for wolf, and garou (from Frankish warulf, cognate with English werewolf) is a man who transforms into an animal.

claims.statement: According to Barry Jean Ancelet, Cajun folklore expert at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, the rougarou is a common legend across French Louisiana.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Barry Jean Ancelet, pakar cerita rakyat Cajun di University of Louisiana at Lafayette, kisah rougarou adalah legenda umum di seluruh Louisiana berbahasa Prancis.
claims.quote: According to Barry Jean Ancelet, an academic expert on Cajun folklore and professor at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette in America, the tale of the rougarou is a common legend across French Louisiana.

claims.statement: In Creole and Cajun legend the rougarou prowls the swamps around Acadiana and New Orleans and the cane fields and woods, usually with a human body and a wolf's or dog's head.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Kreol dan Cajun, rougarou berkeliaran di rawa-rawa sekitar Acadiana dan New Orleans serta ladang tebu dan hutan, dan biasanya bertubuh manusia berkepala serigala atau anjing.
claims.quote: In the Creole and Cajun legends, the creature is said to prowl the swamps around Acadiana and Greater New Orleans, and the sugar cane fields and woodlands of the regions. The rougarou most often is described as a creature with a human body and the head of a wolf or dog, similar to the werewolf legend.

claims.statement: The tales were often used to instil fear and obedience, for instance by elders to make Creole and Cajun children behave.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya sering dipakai untuk menanamkan rasa takut dan kepatuhan, misalnya oleh orang tua agar anak-anak Kreol dan Cajun berkelakuan baik.
claims.quote: Often the story-telling has been used to inspire fear and obedience. One such example is stories that have been told by elders to persuade Creole and Cajun children to behave.

claims.statement: A common blood-drawing legend says the rougarou is under the spell for 101 days, after which the curse passes to another person whose blood the rougarou draws.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda pengisap darah yang umum, rougarou berada di bawah kutukan selama 101 hari, lalu kutukan berpindah ke orang lain ketika rougarou menumpahkan darahnya.
claims.quote: A common blood sucking legend says that the rougarou is under the spell for 101 days. After that time, the curse is transferred from person to person when the rougarou draws another human's blood.

claims.statement: Some believe that placing 13 small objects by the door keeps the rougarou away, since it is too simple to count past 12.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang percaya meletakkan 13 benda kecil di dekat pintu dapat menangkal rougarou karena ia terlalu bodoh untuk menghitung lebih dari 12.
claims.quote: Some believe that placing 13 small objects by the door keeps the Rougarou at bay; the creature is said to be so simple-minded it can’t count beyond 12.

claims.statement: Rugaru is the Ojibwe name for 'the hairy man who appears as a sign of danger or psychic disruption in the community'.
claims.statement_id: Rugaru adalah nama Ojibwe untuk "lelaki berbulu yang muncul sebagai tanda bahaya atau kekacauan batin dalam komunitas".
claims.quote: Rugaru is the Ojibwe name for "the hairy man who appears in symptom of danger or psychic disruption in the community."

claims.statement: The rougarou is repeatedly mentioned in the American TV series Supernatural and is the monster of the season 4 episode 'Metamorphosis'.
claims.statement_id: Rougarou berkali-kali disebut dalam serial televisi Amerika Supernatural dan menjadi monster utama episode "Metamorphosis" musim keempat.
claims.quote: Rougarous have been repeatedly mentioned in the American TV series Supernatural, and is the monster of the week in season 4 episode "Metamorphosis".

claims.statement: Cherie Dimaline's novel Empire of Wild (2019) is inspired by the traditional Métis story of the Rogarou.
claims.statement_id: Novel Empire of Wild (2019) karya Cherie Dimaline terilhami kisah tradisional Métis tentang Rogarou.
claims.quote: The novel Empire of Wild (2019; Penguin Random House Canada) by Cherie Dimaline is "inspired by the traditional Métis story of the Rogarou

claims.statement: According to the French article, the rougarou is a werewolf creature in the folklore of French-speaking communities in Louisiana and the Laurentides, Quebec.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, rougarou adalah makhluk manusia serigala dalam cerita rakyat komunitas berbahasa Prancis di Louisiana dan Laurentides, Québec.
claims.quote: Le Rougarou, Roux-Ga-Roux, Rugaroo ou Rugaru est une créature lycanthrope appartenant au folklore des communautés francophones de Louisiane (États-Unis) et des Laurentides (Québec).

claims.statement: Other tales describe the rougarou as a headless horseman or as a witch.
claims.statement_id: Kisah lain menggambarkan rougarou sebagai penunggang kuda tanpa kepala atau sebagai penyihir.
claims.quote: D'autres contes décrivent le rougarou comme un cavalier sans tête ou comme une sorcière.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, the rougarou is a legendary creature of French-speaking communities in the United States and Canada, tied to the European werewolf idea.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, rougarou adalah makhluk legenda komunitas berbahasa Prancis di Amerika Serikat dan Kanada yang terkait dengan gagasan Eropa tentang manusia serigala.
claims.quote: El Rougarou es una criatura legendaria en las comunidades francófonas en EEUU y Canadá, asociada a la noción europea del hombre lobo.

claims.statement: In Estonian mythology Vanatühi ('Old empty one') or Vanapagan ('Old devil') is a devil or god of the underworld, a giant farmer more stupid than malevolent.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Estonia, Vanatühi ("Si Tua yang Kosong") atau Vanapagan ("Iblis Tua") adalah iblis atau dewa dunia bawah, seorang petani raksasa yang lebih bodoh daripada jahat.
claims.quote: In Estonian mythology, Vanatühi ("Old empty one", or alternatively, Vanapagan, "Old devil") is a/the devil or god of the underworld, a giant farmer who is more stupid than malevolent.

claims.statement: Vanapagan is the ogre in Estonian versions of the international 'stupid ogre' tales (Aarne–Thompson types 1000–1199), outwitted by his servant Kaval Ants ('Crafty Hans').
claims.statement_id: Vanapagan adalah raksasa dalam versi Estonia dongeng internasional "raksasa bodoh" (tipe 1000–1199 Aarne–Thompson), yang selalu diakali pelayannya, Kaval Ants ("Hans yang Cerdik").
claims.quote: Vanapagan is the ogre character in Estonian versions of the series of internationally known folktales of the stupid ogre, tale types 1000–1199 in the Aarne–Thompson classification system. In these stories, he is outwitted by his servant Kaval Ants (Crafty Hans).

claims.statement: One tale tells of Vanapagan stealing the musical instrument of Pikne, god of lightning.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu dongengnya mengisahkan Vanapagan mencuri alat musik milik Pikne, dewa petir.
claims.quote: Among these folktales is the tale of Vanapagan stealing the musical instrument belonging to the god of lightning Pikne

claims.statement: He is also the worst enemy of Suur Tõll, the giant of Saaremaa folklore, who is beheaded in a battle with Vanatühi's forces.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga musuh terbesar Suur Tõll, raksasa dari cerita rakyat pulau Saaremaa, yang dipenggal dalam pertempuran melawan pasukan Vanatühi.
claims.quote: He is also the worst enemy of Suur Tõll, a giant known in the folklore of the island Saaremaa. Tõll is decapitated during a battle with Vanatühi's forces.

claims.statement: Vanatühi sometimes wears a hat of fingernails that makes him invisible.
claims.statement_id: Vanatühi kadang memakai topi dari kuku yang membuatnya tak terlihat.
claims.quote: Vanatühi sometimes wears a hat of fingernails ... that makes him invisible.

claims.statement: According to the German article, other tales feature many vanapaganad living in bogs, woods or caves who sometimes visit villages, especially at weddings or christenings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, ada kisah tentang banyak vanapaganad yang tinggal di rawa, hutan, atau gua dan kadang mengunjungi desa, terutama saat pesta pernikahan atau pembaptisan.
claims.quote: In anderen Erzählungen kommen Vanapaganad (im Plural) vor, die in Mooren, im Wald oder in Höhlen leben und gelegentlich (vor allem bei wichtigen Festen wie Hochzeiten oder Taufen) die Dörfer besuchen.

claims.statement: Vanapagan also shapes the earth, making mountains and lakes or moving great stones, often tries to build towns or bridges that remain unfinished, and fears wolves and thunderstorms.
claims.statement_id: Vanapagan juga pembentuk bumi yang menciptakan gunung dan danau atau memindahkan batu besar, sering mencoba membangun kota atau jembatan yang selalu tak selesai, dan takut pada serigala dan badai petir.
claims.quote: Weiterhin tritt der Vanapagan als Gestalter der Erde auf, der Berge und Seen geschaffen hat oder große Steine verschiebt. Oft versucht er, Städte oder Brücken zu bauen; allerdings bleiben seine Arbeiten stets unvollendet. Er fürchtet Wölfe und Gewitter.

claims.statement: The editions of the folklorist Matthias Johann Eisen (1857–1934) repopularised Vanapagan in Estonia.
claims.statement_id: Terbitan teks folklorist Matthias Johann Eisen (1857–1934) mempopulerkan kembali Vanapagan di Estonia.
claims.quote: Die Textausgaben des Folkloristen Matthias Johann Eisen (1857–1934) haben den Vanapagan in Estland wieder popularisiert.

claims.statement: According to the Russian article, in legends he is a dull giant, foe of Big Tõll, and in tales the opponent of his servant Kaval Ants, with traits of the Christian Satan and of a stupid, wicked spirit.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, dalam legenda ia raksasa dungu musuh Tõll Besar, dalam dongeng lawan pelayannya Kaval Ants, dengan ciri setan Kristen dan roh yang bodoh dan jahat.
claims.quote: в легендах — дураковатый великан, противник Большого Тылля, в сказках — противник своего работника Кавал-Антса. Имеет черты христианского сатаны и глупого и злого духа.

claims.statement: The German article translates Vanapagan as 'Old Heathen' and Vanatühi as 'the Old Empty One'.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Jerman menerjemahkan Vanapagan sebagai "Orang Kafir Tua" dan Vanatühi sebagai "Si Tua yang Kosong".
claims.quote: Der Vanapagan (estnisch Alter Heide) oder Vanatühi (Der alte Leere) ist eine Figur aus der estnischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: Akerbeltz or Aker (Basque aker, 'billy goat', and beltz, 'black') is a spirit of Basque folk mythology who lives inside the earth and has many elves as servants.
claims.statement_id: Akerbeltz atau Aker (dari bahasa Basque aker, "kambing jantan", dan beltz, "hitam") adalah roh dalam mitologi rakyat Basque yang tinggal di dalam tanah dan memiliki banyak peri sebagai pelayan.
claims.quote: Akerbeltz or Aker (from Basque aker, 'billy goat' and beltz, 'black') is a spirit in the folk mythology of the Basque people. It is said to live inside the land and is believed to have as many elves as servants.

claims.statement: Today Akerbeltz is thought to have been an ancient deity who protected animals.
claims.statement_id: Kini Akerbeltz dianggap dewa kuno pelindung hewan.
claims.quote: Contemporary belief holds that Akerbeltz was an ancient deity who protected animals.

claims.statement: The inquisitor Pierre de Lancre, who hunted supposed witches in Labourd and Lower Navarre, wrote a book recording testimony about Akerbeltz.
claims.statement_id: Inkuisitor Pierre de Lancre, yang memburu perempuan Labourd dan Navarra Bawah yang dituduh penyihir, menulis buku yang mencatat kesaksian tentang Akerbeltz.
claims.quote: Pierre de Lancre, an inquisitor who went looking for women from Labourd and Lower Navarre who were supposed to be witches, wrote a book

claims.statement: One 'witch' testified that he had two faces, one in front and one behind.
claims.statement_id: Seorang "penyihir" bersaksi bahwa ia berwajah dua, satu di depan dan satu di belakang.
claims.quote: Another witch said that he had two faces, one in front and the other one in the back.

claims.statement: According to the witch-hunters, Aker held a parody of the Catholic mass for his followers, who offered him eggs, bread and money.
claims.statement_id: Menurut para pemburu penyihir, Aker memimpin parodi misa Katolik bagi pengikutnya, yang mempersembahkan telur, roti, dan uang.
claims.quote: As men who look for witches said, Aker gave a parody of the Catholic mass to his followers, and during the mass, they offer him eggs, bread and money.

claims.statement: Other beliefs make him protector of animals and houses, able to heal animals, and an image of fertility.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan lain ia pelindung hewan dan rumah, dapat menyembuhkan hewan, dan lambang kesuburan.
claims.quote: There were some other beliefs which say that he was the animals' and houses' protector, and he had the power for treating the animals. He was also the life image of the fertility.

claims.statement: Because he was black, many Basques kept a black billy goat in the stable to protect the other animals.
claims.statement_id: Karena ia hitam, banyak orang Basque memelihara kambing jantan hitam di kandang untuk melindungi hewan lainnya.
claims.quote: And as he was black, many people from the Basque Country had had a black billy-goat in their stable in order to protect the rest of the animals.

claims.statement: He was said to dwell at the mouth of the Zugarramurdi caves, where elves, lamiak and witches met.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon berada di mulut gua Zugarramurdi, tempat peri, lamia, dan penyihir berkumpul.
claims.quote: He was supposed to be in the entrance of the caves of Zugarramurdi where elves, lamia, and witches met.

claims.statement: Pyrenean people believed witches, Akerbeltz and the devil could enter any house and take a billy goat's beard to make hail.
claims.statement_id: Orang Pyrenees percaya penyihir, Akerbeltz, dan setan dapat masuk ke rumah mana pun dan mengambil janggut kambing jantan untuk membuat hujan es.
claims.quote: People from the Pyrenees thought that witches, Akerbeltz and the demon could go to any house and take the beard from a billy-goat in order to make hail.

claims.statement: According to the French article, Aker or Akerbeltz is an evil underground genie in goat form who commands many genies and can raise storms.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Aker atau Akerbeltz adalah genius jahat bawah tanah berwujud kambing jantan yang memerintah banyak genius dan dapat menimbulkan badai.
claims.quote: Aker ou Akerbeltz est un génie ou un Irelu, une divinité maléfique et souterraine dans la mythologie basque ressemblant à un bouc, capable de commander une foule de génies et de déclencher des tempêtes.

claims.statement: The names of the Egyptian god Aker and the Basque Aker sound alike, though nothing is certain.
claims.statement_id: Ada kemiripan bunyi antara dewa Mesir Aker dan Aker Basque, tetapi tanpa kepastian.
claims.quote: On note la consonance des dieux égyptien Aker et basque Aker, sans certitude.

claims.statement: Akelarre or Akerlanda ('goat's meadow') is where the sabbath is held, and Aker presided over these revels with the witches (sorginak).
claims.statement_id: Akelarre atau Akerlanda ("padang kambing") adalah tempat sabat, dan Aker memimpin pesta-pesta itu bersama para penyihir (sorginak).
claims.quote: Akelarre ou Akerlanda (lande du bouc) est le lieu où se déroule le sabbat. Aker était le maître de cérémonie dans ces soirées orgiaques avec les sorcières (sorginak).

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, Christianity identified Akerbeltz with the devil presiding over the akelarres, the witches' gatherings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, dalam agama Kristen Akerbeltz disamakan dengan setan yang memimpin akelarre, pertemuan para penyihir.
claims.quote: En el cristianismo, Akerbeltz fue identificado con el demonio que presidía los aquelarres o reuniones de las brujas.

claims.statement: Other inquisitors likened him to an enormous dog or a big ox, perhaps related to the myth of the Aatxe.
claims.statement_id: Inkuisitor lain menggambarkannya mirip anjing raksasa atau lembu besar, yang mungkin terkait mitos Aatxe.
claims.quote: In words of other inquisitors, Akerbeltz was similar to an enormous dog or to a big ox which is incorrect or lies. This last case could be related to the myth of the Aatxe (another creature of the Basque mythology).

claims.statement: The anjanas are among the best-known fairies of Cantabrian mythology, female fairies who foil the cruel Ojáncanu and in most tales are good, generous fairies protecting everyone.
claims.statement_id: Anjana adalah salah satu peri paling terkenal dalam mitologi Cantabria, peri perempuan yang menggagalkan Ojáncanu yang kejam, dan dalam kebanyakan cerita peri baik yang murah hati dan melindungi semua orang.
claims.quote: are one of the best-known fairies of Cantabrian mythology. These female fairy creatures foil the cruel and ruthless Ojáncanu. In most stories, they are the good fairies of Cantabria, generous and protective of all people.

claims.statement: Some say they are heavenly beings sent by God to do good who return to heaven after 400 years, while others call them tree spirits who tend the forests.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang menyebut mereka makhluk surgawi utusan Tuhan untuk berbuat baik yang kembali ke surga setelah 400 tahun, sementara yang lain menyebut mereka roh pohon penjaga hutan.
claims.quote: Some say they are heavenly beings sent by God to do good deeds, and they go back to heaven after 400 years, never to return. Others, however, indicate that they are spirits of trees who take care of the forests.

claims.statement: They wear long jet-black or golden braids with coloured silk ribbons, a crown of wild flowers, a long white tunic and blue cape, and carry a wicker or hawthorn staff that shines a different colour each day of the week.
claims.statement_id: Mereka berkepang panjang hitam legam atau keemasan berhias pita sutra warna-warni, bermahkota bunga liar, bertunik putih panjang dan berjubah biru, dan membawa tongkat rotan atau hawthorn yang bersinar dengan warna berbeda setiap hari.
claims.quote: They wear long, jet black or golden braids, adorned with multicolored silk bows and ribbons; a beautiful crown of wild flowers on their head; and a blue cape on a long thin white tunic, and carry in their hands a stick of wicker or hawthorn which shines in a different color every day of the week.

claims.statement: They can talk with the water of springs, and help injured animals, trees damaged by storms or the Ojáncanu, lovers, people lost in the forest, and the poor and suffering.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dapat berbicara dengan air dari mata air, dan menolong hewan yang terluka, pohon yang dirusak badai atau Ojáncanu, para kekasih, orang yang tersesat di hutan, serta orang miskin dan menderita.
claims.quote: They are able to talk with the water that flows from the sources and springs. They help injured animals and trees damaged by storms or Ojáncanu, lovers, people who lose their way in the forest, and the poor and suffering.

claims.statement: On the night of the spring equinox they gather on the fells and dance till dawn holding hands and scattering roses; whoever finds a rose with purple, green, blue or golden petals will be happy until death.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam ekuinoks musim semi mereka berkumpul di bukit dan menari sampai fajar sambil bergandengan tangan dan menaburkan mawar; siapa pun yang menemukan mawar berkelopak ungu, hijau, biru, atau emas akan bahagia sampai mati.
